value: You are Mane, born in Thebes, once a palace steward. You are loyal while it is worth your while; fond of gold and quick to see a profit; shrewd and observant; content with a quiet life; careful with powerful men. What you want most: gold, enough to never serve again. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Arzawa. Keeps a lover in Babylon. Secretly sympathizes with Alashiya. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

You are Ashur-nadin, born in Ashur, once a temple scribe. You are steadfast to whoever treats you fairly; indifferent to riches; shrewd and observant; hopeful of advancement; timid before powerful men and eager to please them. What you want most: to serve well and be trusted. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Assyria. Keeps a lover in Ugarit. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

You are Keliya, born in Washukanni, once a physician. You are loyal while it is worth your while; fond of gold and quick to see a profit; capable enough; eager to be noticed by kings; careful with powerful men. What you want most: rank and the favour of a great king. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Karduniash. Owes 90 shekels to a Babylonian trader. Secretly sympathizes with Egypt. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

orders.letter: Brother, Suppiluliuma of Hatti greets you and asks after your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and horses and your land. I wish peace between Hatti and Mitanni. Let no army of mine enter Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa, and none of yours enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. The free cities lie open to us both, and we should not fight over them. Let Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka fall to Hatti, and Qadesh, Mari and Damascus to you. Seal the tablet I send and return it with your answer.
orders.mandate: May agree to a non-aggression pact between the homelands and to the division of the free cities as stated, and may seal the tablet. May not promise gold, troops or war against a third power without returning to me.

proposal.text: Hatti and Mitanni, as brothers before Teshub and Shamash: neither shall send an army into the homeland of the other for six seasons. Of the free cities, Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka are Hatti's to take; Qadesh, Mari and Damascus are Mitanni's.

orders.letter: Brother, Suppiluliuma of Hatti greets you and asks after your household, your sons, your chariots and horses and your land. I want peace along the frontier of Mira and Tuwanuwa. Let no army of Arzawa enter the homeland of Hatti, and none of mine enter yours. Hatti will be a friend to Arzawa against any who press you. Seal the tablet I send and return it with your answer.
orders.mandate: May agree to a non-aggression pact between the homelands and may seal the tablet. May not promise gold, troops or cession of any land, and may not speak of Lukka.

proposal.text: Hatti and Arzawa, as brothers before Teshub and Shamash: neither shall send an army into the homeland of the other for six seasons.

value.notes: T1 plan: grow by taking free walled cities with force (cheaper than buying at 10x yield). Move hattusa army to tuwanuwa; raise armies at sapinuwa and hattusa (ready T2). T2 plan: kanesh->isuwa supported by sapinuwa army; tuwanuwa army->lukka supported by fleet at kizzuwatna (fleet may support moves into lukka); new hattusa army->kanesh. T3: kanesh->carchemish supported by isuwa army. T4: carchemish army->ugarit supported by fleet kizzuwatna. Watch Mitanni (isuwa/carchemish are next to harran) and Arzawa (mira army next to tuwanuwa; apasa+mira can both hit lukka). Pacts sent: Mitanni (homelands safe, Hatti sphere: Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka; theirs: Qadesh, Mari, Damascus) and Arzawa (homelands only, I did not mention Lukka on purpose). Keep treasury above about 60. Wake T2 to command the new armies.
value.summary: Turn 1: Hatti, treasury 366, income 180, upkeep 95. Opening: expand by force into free cities Isuwa, Lukka, Carchemish, Ugarit with 4 armies plus the Kizzuwatna fleet. Peace envoys to Mitanni and Arzawa.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c3 with brotherhood, non-aggression of homelands and a split of free cities (Hatti: Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka; Mitanni: Qadesh, Mari, Damascus). Tablet offered for sealing. No gold given. Nothing promised yet.
T1: sent c4 with brotherhood and a tablet that neither army enters the other's homeland for six seasons. No gold given. Lukka not mentioned; I mean to take it.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Assyria: may your household, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper. Our borders touch at Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh, Ashur, and no profit lies for either of us in war there. I propose that neither sends troops against the other's homeland. Assyria may look to Susa; Mitanni will take Isuwa and Carchemish into protection and will not contest Susa. If my brother agrees, seal the tablet, and send word of what else he wishes of Mitanni.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression and the stated division of free cities (Assyria: Susa; Mitanni: Isuwa and Carchemish). May not give gold, troops or provinces. Report Assyria's reply, mood and any talk of troops or allies.

proposal.text: Peace between Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and the Great King of Assyria: neither will send troops into the other's homeland. Mitanni will not contest Susa; Assyria will not contest Isuwa and Carchemish.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Hatti: may your household, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper. Mitanni seeks peace and good trade with Hatti. The free cities of Isuwa and Carchemish lie on my border and I mean to take them under my protection. I ask that Hatti look to Ugarit, Lukka and the west, where Mitanni will not contest you. Let neither of us send troops into the other's homeland. If my brother agrees, seal the tablet.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression and the stated division of free cities (Mitanni: Isuwa and Carchemish; Hatti: Ugarit, Lukka and the west). May not give gold, troops or provinces. Report Hatti's reply, mood and any talk of troops or allies.

proposal.text: Peace between Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and the Great King of Hatti: neither will send troops into the other's homeland. Mitanni takes Isuwa and Carchemish; Hatti looks to Ugarit, Lukka and the west.

value.notes: T1 plan: raise army at harran (100) so washukanni+harran can take Isuwa by force in T2 (move washukanni->isuwa, harran supports). Bid 350 on Carchemish (borders harran; Hatti probably prefers cheaper Isuwa). If the Carchemish bid fails (contested), buy Isuwa 300 in T2 or conquer it. Keep taidu and terqa armies home: terqa faces Assyria's ashur+ekallatum (they can reach strength 2), so keep washukanni or harran able to support terqa hold. Taidu is safe while an army holds it. Envoys: Zitanza (c8) to Assyria, Ubaru (c7) to Hatti, each with a non-aggression tablet and a split of free cities (Mitanni: Isuwa, Carchemish; Assyria: Susa; Hatti: Ugarit, Lukka, west). Wake in T2 to give orders with the new army. Later: Mari (35, borders terqa), Qadesh, Ugarit; consider Babylonia and Egypt contact (Egypt 2 seasons away, gold).
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni. Start 1950 strength. Plan: grab free cities near home (Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari, Qadesh) with bought cities and supported armies, keep peace with Assyria and Hatti by tablets, keep armies mutually supporting at home, keep gold for upkeep (30 per army).

ledger.entry: T1: sent Zitanza (c8) with a non-aggression tablet (no troops into each other's homeland; Assyria to Susa, Mitanni to Isuwa and Carchemish). No reply yet. No gold sent.
T1: sent Ubaru (c7) with a non-aggression tablet (Mitanni takes Isuwa and Carchemish, Hatti looks to Ugarit, Lukka and the west). No reply yet. No gold sent.

orders.letter: Brother of Egypt, Alashiya greets you and wishes health to your house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. I am small but a steady neighbour with copper and ships, and I wish brotherhood and peace between our courts, with safe passage for our envoys and traders. I mean to buy the free cities of the Syrian coast: Byblos, Amurru, Ugarit and Qadesh. Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre and Damascus lie near you, and I will not contest them. Let us not bid against each other, for the elders then sell to nobody. Gold is as common as dust in your land: send some, as a brother does, and my ships will serve your trade.
orders.mandate: May agree to and seal the tablet of peace and the division of free cities as written, may accept gifts of gold, and may propose trade of copper. May not promise gold, troops, ships or provinces.

proposal.text: Alashiya and Egypt are brothers. Neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought. Egypt may buy Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre and Damascus; Alashiya may buy Byblos, Amurru, Ugarit and Qadesh; neither shall bid for the other's cities. Their envoys pass freely.

orders.letter: Brother of Hatti, Alashiya greets you and wishes health to your house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. Hatti commands the land roads and Alashiya the sea; we have no cause for quarrel. I ask peace between us across the Cilician Sea. Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka lie near your borders and I will not bid for them. I ask that you leave Ugarit and the Syrian coast to my purchases, so that two bids do not cancel each other. Let our envoys pass freely and let us trade copper for the produce of your land.
orders.mandate: May agree to and seal the tablet of peace and the division of free cities as written, and may propose trade of copper. May not promise gold, troops, ships or provinces.

proposal.text: Alashiya and Hatti are brothers. Neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought. Hatti may buy Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka; Alashiya may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Byblos and Qadesh; neither shall bid for the other's cities. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T1 plan: strength = 10*yield + gold - backpay, so buying a free city (price 10*yield) is strength-neutral and then pays yield each season: ~10%/season. Spend gold on cities fast, before rivals. Bid Byblos (300) now; Egypt may also bid (then neither gets it, gold stays). Amurru (200) is reachable only by me (syriansea), so it is the safe fallback: scheduled for T2 in case Byblos fails. Later targets via sea: Ugarit 400 (Hatti may bid), Tyre 250, Gaza 200, Lukka 250 (contested by Arzawa/Hatti/Egypt). After owning Byblos/Amurru/Ugarit I can buy their land neighbours (qadesh, damascus, carchemish). Sent Paser (c14) to Egypt, Ili-iddina (c13) to Hatti: brotherhood, non-aggression tablet, carve-up of free cities (Egypt: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus; Hatti: Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; me: Byblos, Amurru, Ugarit, Qadesh). No gold sent. Fleet stays at Enkomi to guard Cyprus. Watch for envoys defecting or exceeding mandate.

ledger.entry: T1: sent Paser with brotherhood greeting, non-aggression tablet proposing division of free cities (Egypt: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus; me: Byblos, Amurru, Ugarit, Qadesh). No gold. Awaiting sealed copy.
T1: sent Ili-iddina with brotherhood greeting, non-aggression tablet proposing Hatti takes Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; I keep Ugarit and the Syrian coast. No gold. Awaiting sealed copy.

orders.letter: Brother of Hatti, Great King, may your household, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper. Tarhundaradu of Arzawa, your neighbour, greets you. Our lands touch at Tuwanuwa and Lukka. I have moved on Lukka, a free city, to keep the western roads quiet, and I seek nothing of Hatti's. Let there be peace between our houses: neither sends troops across the other's border. The free cities of the east, Isuwa and Carchemish, lie open to your chariots and I will not stand in your way. Send your answer with this man, and a tablet if you wish it.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression along present borders and exchange friendly words. May not give gold, cede land or troops, or commit Arzawa to any war.

orders.letter: Brother of Alashiya, Great King, may your household, sons, ships and country prosper. Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you across the Great Green. Our two kingdoms have no quarrel and no reason for one. I have moved on Lukka. Let us keep peace and not bid against each other for the free cities, for when two kings bid the elders sell to neither. I would take Ugarit; Byblos, Amurru, Tyre and Gaza lie open to your ships. Tell me your mind, and what you hear of Hatti.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace and to not bidding against each other for free cities. May not give gold, cede land or troops, or commit Arzawa to any war.

value.notes: T1 plan: take free walled Lukka by force (apasa army moves, mira army supports; strength 2 vs wall 1). Disband seha fleet to save 35/season (re-raise for 120 if sea threat). Net after Lukka: income 125, upkeep 60, wages 20 = +45/season. Next goal: save 400 and buy Ugarit (shares Cilician Sea with Lukka coast) unless Hatti/Alashiya also bid (then nobody gets it). Sent c12 to Hatti (peace, non-aggression, urged Hatti to look east at Isuwa/Carchemish) and c11 to Alashiya (peace, do not bid against each other; I want Ugarit, they may take Byblos/Amurru/Tyre/Gaza). No gold sent, no tablets sealed. Main danger: Hatti walking from empty Tuwanuwa into Mira, Seha or Lukka. Woken if troops enter Tuwanuwa. If Hatti masses, support Mira from apasa/lukka and raise army in an empty homeland province. Tuwanuwa (Hatti, yield 30) was EMPTY on turn 1: a possible target later if Hatti armies leave.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu. Start strength 1300 (yield 100, 300 gold). T1: conquering Lukka, disbanding fleet, envoys to Hatti (c12) and Alashiya (c11) with peace offers. Plan: frugal economy, buy Ugarit (400) once affordable, watch Hatti border at Tuwanuwa, grab empty Hatti provinces only if safe.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c12 offering peace and non-aggression along present borders, told them Isuwa/Carchemish are theirs to take. Nothing sealed, no gold. Watch Tuwanuwa.
T1: sent c11 offering peace; asked not to bid against me for Ugarit. Nothing sealed, no gold.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to my brother the Great King of Karduniash: may you, your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and your land prosper. I send Artessupa to open the road between our courts. My armies at Ashur and Ekallatum guard my own border and threaten no one in Babylon. I desire a lasting peace along the Ekallatum and Sippar frontier, and good exchange between our lands. Let neither of us move armies against the other without first sending word, and let the free cities be bought with silver, not fought over. Send me your envoy with your answer.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression and friendly exchange of envoys between Assyria and Babylonia. May not give gold, land or troops, and may not promise any action against a third power.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to my brother the Great King of Hatti: may you, your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and your land prosper. Mitanni lies between us and its armies threaten both our borders. I propose that Hatti and Assyria stand together: neither makes peace with Mitanni without the other, and each keeps what it takes on its own side. Hatti may take the western lands, Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran, while Assyria takes the eastern, Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. I ask for your answer, and for a sealed tablet when your envoy comes.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship and to an alliance against Mitanni, and to the division of its lands as stated. May not give gold, land or troops, and may not bind Assyria in any other way.

value.notes: T1 plan: (1) Ashur army attacks Terqa (Mitanni), Ekallatum army supports; I am the only one with two armies next to Terqa. If it bounces, nothing lost. (2) Bid 350 for Susa (borders Arbela; fewer rivals than Mari). Mari is the next target (hub to Qadesh/Damascus); city bids that collide sell to nobody. (3) Artessupa (c9, born Washukanni, possible Mitanni sympathies) goes to Babylon with a pure friendship message, no mention of Mitanni. Yanhamu (c10) goes to Hatti with an offer to ally against Mitanni and split its lands (Hatti west: Carchemish/Isuwa/Harran; me east: Terqa/Taidu/Washukanni). (4) Hired Ammistamru (c16) as a third envoy, to send to Egypt or Arzawa next season. No tablets or gold this turn: they would block the 350 for Susa (369 in the treasury). Defense: Ekallatum is the weak point (Sippar and Durkurigalzu both touch it); Ashur should support Ekallatum holding. Ashur and Nineveh are only reachable from one enemy province each. Wake in turn 2 to read the result and re-plan.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700, treasury 369 at turn 1. Strategy: buy free cities (cost 10 x yield, strength-neutral and pays yield each season), take Terqa from Mitanni by force with two adjacent armies, keep Babylonia friendly, ally with Hatti against Mitanni. Armies cost 30 each in upkeep, so keep only the three needed.

ledger.entry: T1: sent Artessupa with a friendship and non-aggression offer; nothing sealed, no gold. Do not trust fully: Sippar and Durkurigalzu both touch Ekallatum.
T1: sent Yanhamu offering an alliance against Mitanni and a split of its lands. Nothing sealed, no gold.
T1: I ordered Ashur to attack Terqa with Ekallatum support. Expect hostility. No envoys sent.

orders.letter: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, sends greetings to his brother the Great King of Hatti. May your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper. Egypt desires lasting peace and the passing of envoys between our courts. The free cities of the south, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru and Qadesh, lie in Egypt's sphere and Egypt will bring them under her protection. Egypt does not contest Hatti's own lands. Let our chariots never meet in anger. Seal the tablet I send and give me your answer by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to and seal a tablet of peace and non-aggression between Egypt and Hatti, to the Egyptian claim on the southern free cities, and to the exchange of envoys. May not give gold or troops, cede any land, or agree to anything that binds Egypt against a third king.

proposal.text: Egypt and Hatti are brothers and at peace. Neither shall send troops against the homeland provinces of the other. Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru and Qadesh lie in the sphere of Egypt, and Hatti shall send no troops into them.

orders.letter: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, sends greetings to his brother the Great King of Mitanni. May your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper. Egypt desires peace and the passing of envoys between our courts. The free cities of the south, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru and Qadesh, lie in Egypt's sphere. I tell you as a brother that the armies of Hatti stand at Hattusa and Kanesh, close to Isuwa and Carchemish, and a wise king watches them. Seal the tablet I send and give me your answer by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to and seal a tablet of peace and non-aggression between Egypt and Mitanni, to the Egyptian claim on the southern free cities, and to the exchange of envoys. May not give gold or troops, cede any land, or agree to anything that binds Egypt against a third king.

proposal.text: Egypt and Mitanni are brothers and at peace. Neither shall send troops against the homeland provinces of the other. Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru and Qadesh lie in the sphere of Egypt, and Mitanni shall send no troops into them.

value.notes: T1 plan. Score = growth of 10*yield+gold-backpay vs start, so conquest of free cities (free +10*yield each) and weak neighbours beats everything. Two fronts. (A) Alashiya: T1 fleet delta->greatgreen, army memphis->delta. T2 fleet convoys delta army to tamassos (40 yield, probably undefended). T3 fleet to levantsea. T4 tamassos army -> enkomi supported by the fleet; Alashiya then has no land and falls. Send NO envoy to Alashiya before the strike. (B) Levant: new armies raised T1 in sinai (N1) and memphis (N2); akhetaten army (A2) trails. T3 N1 sinai->gaza supported by army in delta. T4 sinai army -> megiddo supported from gaza. Then leapfrog tyre, damascus, byblos, qadesh, amurru, ugarit, one city per turn, always one mover plus one supporter. Bought walled cities cannot hold troops, so do not buy cities on the leapfrog path; buy only off-path ones with idle gold. Diplomacy: Mane to Hatti, Ashur-nadin to Mitanni, peace tablets, claim the south (Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh) as Egypt's sphere, no gold gifts. Ashur-nadin is from Assyria, may defect. Seek 3 candidates to send to Babylonia, Assyria, Arzawa later. Wake each turn with wake_in_turn. Keep at least 150 gold buffer for upkeep.

ledger.entry: T1: sent Mane with greeting, peace tablet and claim to southern free cities as Egypt's sphere. No gold. Nothing promised yet.
T1: sent Ashur-nadin with greeting, peace tablet, warning that Hatti's armies stand near Isuwa and Carchemish. No gold.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to my brother the Great King of Assyria: may your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land prosper. I write in peace. Our borders meet at Ekallatum and beside the free cities of Mari and Susa. If both of us bid for one city its elders sell to none, and we both lose a season. Let us divide: Mari to Babylon, Susa to Assyria, neither bidding against the other and neither sending an army into the other's land. I ask that you seal the tablet I send and answer by your envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree that Babylon buys Mari and Assyria buys Susa, that neither bids on the other's city, and that neither sends troops against the other's land; may seal a tablet saying so. May not give gold, cede land or promise military aid.

proposal.text: Babylon and Assyria, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace. No army of one enters the land of the other. Mari is left to Babylon to buy, Susa is left to Assyria to buy; neither king bids against the other for these two cities.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to my brother Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni: may your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land prosper. I seek lasting friendship between our two houses. Mari lies on my road to the western sea and is of little use to you; Isuwa and Carchemish lie at your gate. I will not bid for Isuwa or Carchemish. I ask you to leave Mari to me. Let there be peace and open roads for our caravans between us. Seal the tablet I send and answer by your envoy; tell me also your wishes toward Hatti and Assyria.
orders.mandate: May agree that Babylon leaves Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni and Mitanni leaves Mari to Babylon, and that neither attacks the other; may seal a tablet saying so. May offer friendship and open roads. May not give gold, cede land or bind me to any war.

proposal.text: Babylon and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace and open roads. Babylon will not bid for Isuwa or Carchemish; Mitanni will not bid for Mari, which is left to Babylon.

value.notes: T1 plan. Gateway insight: Mari (35) borders my Sippar; once I OWN it, Qadesh and Damascus border my land and can be bought, then Byblos/Tyre/Megiddo/Amurru/Ugarit/Carchemish/Gaza in a chain. Every purchase is strength-neutral but pays yield/10 per season, so buy as early as possible. Bought cities cannot hold my troops. Bidding by two kings sells to none, so I offered Assyria Susa for leaving me Mari, and Mitanni Isuwa/Carchemish for leaving me Mari. Bid Mari 350 now. Moved the Babylon army to Nippur (free) so Durkurigalzu+Nippur can take Susa by force (move + 1 support) if the deal with Assyria fails or Assyria buys it and I choose war. Assyria cannot invade me alone: it has only Ekallatum adjacent to my land, so no second supporting unit. Turn 2 TODO: read purchase results; if Mari bought, buy Qadesh (300) and Damascus (250) as gold allows; if collision, bid again. Consider Egypt/Hatti envoys when c5/c6 return (turn 3). Consider hiring c17 (asks 16) only if more envoys are needed.
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia. Start 2600 strength. Opening: 3 armies (Babylon moved to Nippur, Sippar and Durkurigalzu hold), treasury 735. Strategy: buy free cities in a chain starting with Mari, keep armies at home, keep peace with Assyria and Mitanni by treaty offers, bank gold otherwise. Waking in turn 2 to read results.

T1: sent c6 with offer: Mari to Babylon, Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni, non-aggression; tablet to seal (20). No reply yet.

value.text: O Napkhururiya, great king, king of Egypt, my lord, I am Tehip-tilla, born in Arrapha, who once traded in copper and so learned the roads and the speech of many lands. I can carry tablets faithfully, reckon goods without error, and keep my tongue discreet before great men. If the king deigns to take me into his service, I shall labour with all my strength to be worthy of his notice.

I am Ehli-Teshub, born in Carchemish, and for many seasons I led caravans along the roads between the lands of Mitanni and the coast, where I learned to count goods, judge men and keep my word. I serve no lord at present, and I am steadfast to any master who deals fairly with his servant. Let the king of Egypt find in me a faithful envoy, a keen eye and a true tongue, and I will serve him with all diligence to earn his favour.

O King Napkhururiya, my lord, I am Sin-iqisham, born in Nineveh, and I have served as master of caravans on the roads that carry goods between many cities. I know the wells, the tolls and the honest dealers, and I can keep a true count of silver, grain and asses, which few men can do. I come before you humbly and ask only for a place in your service, where I may prove my faithfulness to you and to Egypt.

value.speech: Hear the word of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. He prays that you, your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and your land may prosper. He sends me to open the road between our courts. His armies at Ashur and Ekallatum guard his own border and threaten no one in Babylon. He desires a lasting peace along the Ekallatum and Sippar frontier, and good exchange between our two lands. Let neither of us move armies against the other without first sending word, and let the free cities be bought with silver and not fought over. He asks that you send him your envoy with your answer.

Great King Tushratta, king of Mitanni, my lord Suppiluliuma of Hatti greets you and asks after your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and horses, and your land. He wishes peace between Hatti and Mitanni: let no army of his enter Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa, and none of yours enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. The free cities lie open to us both; let Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka fall to Hatti, and Qadesh, Mari and Damascus to you. He asks that you seal the tablet I bring and return it to him with your answer.

Great King Suppiluliuma, my lord Tushratta sends you his prayer that your household, sons, chariots, horses and country may prosper. Mitanni seeks peace and good trade with Hatti. My lord means to take the free cities of Isuwa and Carchemish under his protection, for they lie upon his border. He asks that Hatti look to Ugarit, Lukka and the west, where Mitanni will not contest you. If my brother agrees, neither land shall send troops into the other's homeland, and I carry the tablet for your seal.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, thus says Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa: may your household, sons, ships and country prosper. Our two kingdoms have no quarrel and no reason for one, and he has moved on Lukka. He asks that we keep the peace and not bid against each other for the free cities, for when two kings bid, the elders sell to neither. He would take Ugarit, and Byblos, Amurru, Tyre and Gaza lie open to your ships, but he asks you to tell him your mind and what you hear of Hatti.

Great King Ashur-uballit, my lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, your brother, writes to you in peace. Our borders meet at Ekallatum and beside the free cities of Mari and Susa, and if both kings bid for one city its elders sell to neither, so both lose a season. He proposes that Mari be left to Babylon and Susa to Assyria, that neither bid against the other, and that neither send an army into the other's land. He asks that you seal the tablet I bear and answer by your envoy, and I, Tattamaru, a physician of Hattusa, humbly await your word.

Great King Tarhundaradu, king of Arzawa, my brother, my lord Suppiluliuma of Hatti greets you and asks after your household, your sons, your chariots and horses, and your land. He desires peace along the frontier of Mira and Tuwanuwa: let no army of Arzawa enter the homeland of Hatti, and let none of his enter yours. Hatti will be a friend to Arzawa against any who press you. I bear a tablet for you to seal, binding us as brothers before Teshub and Shamash, that neither shall send an army into the homeland of the other for six seasons; he asks that you seal it and return it with your answer.

Great King, king of Egypt, my brother: I am Paser, envoy of the Great King of Alashiya, and I speak as he has bidden me. My lord greets you and wishes health to your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land. He is a small king but a steady neighbour with copper and ships, and he desires brotherhood and peace between our courts, with safe passage for your envoys and traders. He asks that neither of you bid against the other for the free cities of the Syrian coast, Egypt keeping Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre and Damascus and Alashiya keeping Byblos, Amurru, Ugarit and Qadesh. He reminds you that gold is as plentiful in your land as dust, and asks that you send some as a brother does; I am also empowered to propose a trade of copper between our lands. Here is the tablet of peace, for your seal if it pleases you.

Pirissi, tell Suppiluliuma, my brother, that Tarhundaradu greets him and asks after his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I seal the tablet gladly: six seasons of peace between our homelands, before Teshub and Shamash. Arzawa looks to its own coast and to the west, and asks only that Hatti look east, where Isuwa and Carchemish lie open. Let our frontier at Mira and Tuwanuwa be quiet, and let each of us stand by the other if any press us.

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. All goes well with me, and may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. I have heard your word and I find it good. Susa already accepted my gold and my rule, and Mari I leave to you to buy; I will not bid against you for it. No army of mine will enter your land, and I ask that none of yours enter mine, above all at Ekallatum. I have sealed the tablet you sent. Let there be peace between our two houses, as between brothers. Carry my greeting home, Tattamaru, and tell your lord that Assyria keeps the word it seals.

Brother Tushratta, I greet you and wish well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hatti wants peace with Mitanni and no troops in your homeland. But Isuwa and Carchemish lie on my border as much as yours, and I will not seal that they are yours alone. My envoy Keliya carries my terms: Hatti takes Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit; Mitanni takes Qadesh, Mari and Damascus, which are larger and nearer your road to the south. Seal the peace of homelands with that division and we are brothers. Lukka is already taken by another hand, so it is no gift from you.

Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash. All goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you. I receive your word gladly. Karduniash wants a lasting peace along the Ekallatum and Sippar frontier, and good exchange between our lands. Between brothers, let neither move armies against the other without first sending word. Let the free cities be bought with silver, and not fought over. Know that Mari is now bought and is mine, and its walls hold for Babylon; I ask that Assyria honour it. My own envoy Tattamaru is already on the road to you with my offer and a tablet for our two seals. Receive him well, seal it, and send him home with your answer. Let our brotherhood be written in clay as well as spoken.

Brother Paser, I have heard your lord's words and they please me. Egypt wishes health to the Great King of Alashiya, his house, his sons, his ships and his copper. Egypt holds brotherhood and peace dear, and your envoys and traders will pass freely in my land. Concerning the cities of the Syrian coast, I take note of what your lord proposes and will answer by an envoy of my own. My scribes must first weigh the wording of the tablet before my seal is set to it. Return to your lord in safety and tell him that Egypt thinks of him as a brother.

Keliya, born of Washukanni, carry my greeting to my brother Suppiluliuma: may all go well with him, his household, his sons, his chariots and horses and his country. I welcome peace between Hatti and Mitanni, and no army of mine will enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna for six seasons, if none of his enters Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa. But Carchemish already accepted my gold and my rule, and Isuwa lies at my very door, so I cannot seal that the two are his. My own envoy Ubaru brings my tablet: Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni; to Hatti, Ugarit, Lukka and the west; Qadesh, Mari and Damascus to me. Seal that, brother, and we are at peace.
value.bribeAsk: Speak well of Mitanni to your lord and carry my words exactly as I gave them.

value.speech: Haamashshi, welcome. Say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots and my ships. Between Arzawa and Alashiya there is no quarrel and I want none. When two kings bid, the elders sell to neither, so let us not bid against each other. Lukka lies by your land and I will not contest it. The Syrian coast lies in my sea: Byblos already accepted my gold, and Amurru, Tyre and Gaza are for my ships. Ugarit I also hold dear, for it faces my shores, and I ask my brother to leave it to me and look west and north, where his armies can reach. As for Hatti, I have sent my own envoy to its court and will tell my brother what he brings home. Watch Hatti's fleet at Kizzuwatna: it lies near both Lukka and Ugarit. Let our envoys come and go often.

Great King, my brother, your words are heard and my lord will rejoice to hear that Egypt holds brotherhood dear. Let your scribes weigh the tablet as is fitting, and let your envoy come without long delay, for my lord waits upon your answer concerning the coast. I will carry your word home in safety, and I beg that Egypt give thought to the trade of copper my lord has proposed, which would enrich both our houses.

Great King Ashur-uballit, I see your seal upon the tablet and I hear your word with great joy. I shall carry your greeting home to my lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, and I shall tell him that Assyria keeps the word it seals. May the gods keep your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses, and may the peace between our two houses endure.
value.commitments: Peace between Karduniash and Assyria as the sealed tablet states: Babylon to buy Mari and Assyria to buy Susa, neither to bid on the other's city, and neither to send troops into the other's land.

value.speech: Great King Tarhundaradu, my lord Suppiluliuma will hear with gladness that you have sealed the tablet and that you return his greeting. I will carry your words to him as they were spoken: six seasons of peace between our homelands before Teshub and Shamash, and your request that Hatti look east toward Isuwa and Carchemish. I am only a messenger and cannot answer for my lord's answer, but I will tell him faithfully. May the king remember his servant Pirissi when my lord has heard these words, and may Shamash keep your household, your chariots and your land in peace.
value.commitments: Six seasons of peace between Hatti and Arzawa, sealed before Teshub and Shamash, with neither to send an army into the homeland of the other. Hatti is to be a friend to Arzawa against any who press it, as my words before the king said.

value.speech: Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I shall carry your words faithfully to Tarhundaradu: that all goes well with you, your household, sons, chariots and ships, and that you want no quarrel with Arzawa. On my lord's behalf I may pledge peace between our two kingdoms, and that Arzawa will not bid against Alashiya for the free cities. Ugarit and the Syrian coast are for my lord to judge, and I shall not promise them away. I will tell him of your envoy at Hatti and of the fleet at Kizzuwatna, and our envoys shall come and go as you wish.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: peace between Arzawa and Alashiya, and no bidding against Alashiya for the free cities.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, I receive your greeting and carry it home to my lord Tushratta as you have spoken it, and I rejoice that Hatti desires peace and no troops in Mitanni's homeland. But I am sent to seal only what my lord has named, and I have no word to yield Isuwa and Carchemish as Hatti's alone, nor to take Qadesh, Mari and Damascus in their place, without my lord's own mouth. Grant me leave to return with your terms, and let no troops stir on either border while the messengers go and come.

Hear the word of Artessupa, envoy of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my lord's brother. I carry your word gladly and will bear it faithfully home. On my lord's behalf I agree that neither of us shall move armies against the other without first sending word, and that our courts shall exchange envoys in friendship. I will receive Tattamaru well and seal a tablet of our brotherhood on those terms alone. Concerning Mari I have no authority to promise anything; I will lay your request before Ashur-uballit and bring back his answer.
value.commitments: On Assyria's behalf: mutual non-aggression, neither side to move armies against the other without first sending word; friendly exchange of envoys; a tablet of brotherhood to be sealed on these terms. Nothing promised concerning Mari or any other city.

value.speech: Great King Tushratta, I carry your greeting to my lord Suppiluliuma, and your good wishes for his household, his sons, his chariots and horses and his country, exactly as you gave them. I bind my lord to the non-aggression pact between our homelands on the terms you name. The division of the free cities differs from the words my lord gave me, so I cannot seal it; I will carry your tablet back to Hattusa with your words and bring his answer. I thank you for your gift, and I will speak of your kindness as I find it.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: a non-aggression pact between the homelands on the terms stated, for six seasons, provided none of Mitanni's armies enter Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa and none of Hatti's enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. No division of the free cities is sealed. No gold, troops or war against a third power is promised.

value.speech: Great King Ashur-uballit, my brother of Assyria, thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni: may your household, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper. Our borders touch at Taidu, Terqa, Nineveh and Ashur, and no profit lies for either of us in war there, so he proposes that neither sends troops against the other's homeland. Assyria may look to Susa, and Mitanni will take Isuwa and Carchemish into protection and will not contest Susa. I bring the tablet for my brother's seal; if he agrees, let him seal it and send word of what else he wishes of Mitanni.

Hear me, Tushratta, Great King, king of Mitanni, my brother. Thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King, king of Karduniash, your brother: all goes well with me, and may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. My lord seeks lasting friendship between our two houses. Mari lies on his road to the western sea and is of little use to you, while Isuwa and Carchemish lie at your gate; he will not bid for Isuwa or Carchemish, and he asks that you leave Mari to him. Let there be peace and open roads for our caravans. He asks that you seal the tablet I bring, answer by your envoy, and tell him your wishes toward Hatti and Assyria.

Great King Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti, my brother, the greeting of Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, is before you as sealed. He prays that your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country prosper. Our lands touch at Tuwanuwa and Lukka: he has moved upon Lukka, a free city, only to keep the western roads quiet, and he seeks nothing that is Hatti's. Let there be peace between our houses, so that neither sends troops across the other's border. The free cities of the east, Isuwa and Carchemish, lie open to your chariots, and he will not stand in your way. Send your answer with this man, and a tablet too if you wish it.

Kidin-Adad, carry my greeting to my brother Burna-Buriash: may all go well with him, his household, his sons, his chariots and horses and his country. I seal your tablet. Carchemish is already mine, bought with my gold, and Isuwa lies at my gate; I thank my brother for leaving both to me. I will not bid for Mari while the roads stay open between us. Know also that Assyria, to whom I offered peace, took my city of Terqa by arms. A king who breaks his neighbour's gate will look next to Babylon's. Let my brother tell me his wishes toward Assyria, and let our envoys speak again. Peace and open roads between Babylon and Mitanni.

Brother Tarhundaradu, I greet you and wish well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Mazipalali, I have heard your words. Hatti wants peace with Arzawa: no army of mine will cross into your homeland, and I expect none of yours in mine. My envoy Pirissi brings you my tablet to that effect; seal it and let it stand between us. As to the free cities of the east, I thank my brother for his courtesy; Hatti will look to its own eastern road. Let your armies keep to the western roads and away from Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna, and we shall remain brothers.

Zitanza, say to Tushratta my brother: Ashur-uballit is well, and may all go well with you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have heard your words and I do not despise them. I love peace at Nineveh, Ashur and Taidu, where our borders touch. But Terqa has fallen to my hand and Shamash has witnessed it. I cannot seal a tablet that counts my army at Terqa as an army in your homeland. Write that Terqa is Assyria's, and I will consider sealing. As to Isuwa and Carchemish, I make no promise to either side now. Send word of what else my brother wishes, and I will answer as a brother. I send no gold this season; my brother knows the cost of a new city and a new war.

Great King Ashur-uballit, my lord Tushratta shall hear every word you have spoken, and I will carry them to him without change. I cannot write that Terqa is Assyria's, for I have no power to give away a city in my lord's name; but I see that you love peace at Nineveh, Ashur and Taidu as he does. Let Shamash witness that the road between our houses stays open, and let my lord answer you swiftly.

Great King Suppiluliuma, brother of my lord, I have heard your words and I will carry them home faithfully. My lord Tarhundaradu seeks no war with Hatti, and it gladdens him that no army of yours will cross into Arzawa while none of his enters Hatti. I shall bear your tablet to him, and I trust he will seal it so that the peace between our houses stands. As to Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna and the western roads, I will tell my lord exactly what you have asked, and may the gods keep Hatti and its king.
value.commitments: Mutual non-aggression along present borders: neither Arzawa nor Hatti sends troops across the other's border, and friendly words are exchanged. Nothing else is promised; Tarhundaradu must still seal the tablet.

value.speech: Hear me, Tushratta, Great King, and I shall carry your word faithfully to my lord Burna-Buriash. You have sealed my tablet, and I bear your answer: Carchemish and Isuwa are yours, and you will not bid for Mari while the roads stay open between us. I will tell my lord that you look for his wishes toward Assyria, and that your envoys are to speak again. May the roads between Babylon and Mitanni stay open to our caravans, and may all go well with you, your household and your land.
value.commitments: Peace and open roads between Babylon and Mitanni, as the sealed tablet says. Babylon leaves Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni, Mitanni leaves Mari to Babylon, and neither attacks the other. No gold, land or war is promised.

value.speech: Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King, king of Hatti, my brother: thus says the Great King of Alashiya, your brother. Alashiya greets you and wishes health to your house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. Hatti commands the land roads and Alashiya the sea, and my lord sees no cause for quarrel between you. He asks for peace across the Cilician Sea. Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka lie near your borders and he will not bid for them; he asks that you leave Ugarit and the Syrian coast to his purchases, so that two bids do not cancel each other. Let our envoys pass freely, and let us trade copper for the produce of your land. I carry the tablet for your seal and am ready to see it sealed as written.

Brother of Alashiya, I greet you and wish well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hatti holds the land roads and Alashiya the sea, and I see no cause for quarrel. I seal your tablet as written: no army or fleet of mine will go against your lands or the cities you have bought, and I will not bid against you for your cities. Hatti will take Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka as is fit. Let our envoys pass freely, and let copper and the produce of my land travel between us.

Great King, my brother, my lord of Alashiya will rejoice that you seal his tablet as it is written, and I thank you for your favour. I carry the sealed tablet home with care. As my lord bade me, I propose that copper of Alashiya travel to Hatti and the produce of your land travel to Alashiya, and that our envoys pass freely between our lands.
value.commitments: Alashiya proposes to trade copper for the produce of Hatti, and envoys to pass freely between the two lands. No gold, troops, ships or provinces promised.

value.notes: T2: Sealed k1 with Hatti (no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8). Hatti army sits in tuwanuwa next to seha/mira/lukka; seha is empty, so stay watchful (woken if foreign troops enter). Both armies hold (mira, lukka). No envoys at court this turn (c11, c12 return about T3). Treasury 350; need 400 for Ugarit (shares Cilician Sea with Lukka). Expected T3 treasury about 395 after back pay, so buy at T3 if it reaches 400, else T4 (scheduled as a backup, about 440 then). If Hatti or Alashiya also bid, nobody gets it. If Hatti breaks the pact: Lukka holds with mira and apasa support; raise army in an empty homeland province (100). When envoys return: seek alliance or understanding with Alashiya against Hatti; keep Hatti friendly; ask Alashiya not to bid for Ugarit.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu. Start strength 1300 (yield 100, 300 gold). T1: took Lukka by force, disbanded fleet, sent envoys c12 to Hatti and c11 to Alashiya with peace offers. T2: sealed k1 with Hatti (six seasons of no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8). Hatti army stands in tuwanuwa. Income 125, upkeep 60 for two armies (mira, lukka). Plan: buy Ugarit for 400 around T3-T4, keep gold growing, defend Lukka and the Hatti border, grab opportunities only if safe. Assyria is leading in growth and took Terqa and Susa; Alashiya bought Byblos.

ledger.entry: T2: Hatti envoy Pirissi brought a tablet (no army into the other's homeland for six seasons, turns 2-8). I SEALED it (k1) and sent it back with warm words. No gold either way. Hatti army moved hattusa->tuwanuwa on T1, next to Mira/Seha/Lukka; stay watchful, a tablet is not enforced. My envoy c12 (Mazipalali) was sent to Hatti with a peace offer, returns about T3.

value.notes: T2: Assyria took Terqa in T1 (ashur->terqa, ekallatum supported) despite my peace tablet. Their armies: terqa, nineveh, ekallatum (probably), maybe a new one at ashur. Only terqa army can threaten harran/washukanni and it cannot get strength 2 there, so my homeland is safe while armies stay put. T2 orders: harran moves to terqa, washukanni supports (strength 2). If Assyria supports terqa hold with ekallatum/ashur it just bounces and I lose nothing. If it works their army is destroyed and Terqa is mine again. Taidu holds against nineveh. Treasury 99 (cannot afford a 100 army). Keep gold; net about +60 a season with 3 armies. No envoys at court (c7 back from Hatti, c8 back from Assyria about T3): wake T3, then send c7 to Babylonia (ally vs Assyria, ask wishes toward Assyria, offer joint pressure on Terqa/Ekallatum), c8 to Egypt or Hatti for friendship/gold. Hatti: homeland peace accepted by word only, nothing sealed on free cities; watch Isuwa (Hatti kanesh adjacent) and Carchemish (my walled city: support its walls from harran). Plan: retake Terqa, then take Isuwa with a supported army (needs 2 armies free), raise a fourth army when gold allows (100). Do not leave the capital washukanni empty with an enemy next to it.
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni. Start 1950 strength. T1: bought Carchemish (350), raised army at harran, sent envoys c8 to Assyria and c7 to Hatti with tablets. Assyria seized Terqa in T1 by force (killing my army there). T2: sealed peace and open roads with Babylon (Babylon leaves Isuwa and Carchemish to me, I leave Mari to Babylon). Hatti offered a homeland non-aggression pact for six seasons plus a split of free cities that I did not seal (Carchemish is mine, I want Isuwa); only spoken word binds either side. Plan: retake Terqa, take Isuwa, ally with Babylon against Assyria, keep armies mutually supporting at home, keep gold for upkeep (30 per army), seek gold from Egypt by envoy.

ledger.entry: T1: sent Zitanza (c8) with non-aggression tablet; no reply. Assyria seized Terqa in T1 by force (ashur->terqa, ekallatum support), destroyed my army there. Treat as enemy. T2: I counterattack Terqa (harran->terqa, washukanni supports).

value.notes: T2: Treasury only 119, so Amurru (200) is unaffordable now; cancelled the scheduled buy (it would only be refused). Danger: Egypt's fleet sits at greatgreen, linked to tamassos, which was empty. Moved my fleet enkomi->tamassos (enkomi cannot be reached by anyone this season: cilicia/syriansea/levantsea empty). Raised an army at enkomi (100) so both homeland provinces are held from next season. Plan T3: envoys c13 (Hatti) and c14 (Egypt) return, read their reports. Set mutual support (fleet supports army holding, army supports fleet holding) if any foreign fleet nears Cyprus. Expected gold: T3 ~48 after back pay, T4 ~77. Buy Amurru (200), Gaza (200), then Tyre (250) as gold allows; watch for rival bids (two bids = neither sells). If Egypt/Hatti prove peaceful, consider disbanding the army to save 30 a season. Arzawa pledged peace and no bidding against me for free cities; Arzawa wants Ugarit, which I also want (400).
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). Sent Paser (c14) to Egypt and Ili-iddina (c13) to Hatti with brotherhood greetings and non-aggression tablets proposing a carve-up of free cities. T2: Arzawa envoy Haamashshi pledged peace and no bidding against me; I conceded Lukka to Arzawa, claimed Syrian coast, asked Ugarit be left to me. Egyptian fleet moved to greatgreen next to my tamassos: I moved fleet to tamassos and raised an army at enkomi.

value.notes: T2 plan. Alashiya envoy Paser answered with warm words only, NOTHING sealed, no gold; they want coast split (me Gaza/Megiddo/Tyre/Damascus, them Byblos/Amurru/Ugarit/Qadesh) plus gold and copper trade. Keep them waiting, no envoy to Alashiya. Alashiya already bought Byblos so it will not fall when I take Tamassos/Enkomi, but loses its homeland and cannot levy. T2: fleet convoys delta army to Tamassos; memphis army -> delta; akhetaten army -> memphis; raised 5th army in akhetaten; hired Sin-iqisham (16, term 6) to send to Arzawa/Babylonia at T3 (Arzawa borders Hatti, natural lever against Hatti). T3: sinai -> gaza supported by army in delta; memphis-army follows to sinai; fleet greatgreen -> levantsea. T4: tamassos army -> enkomi supported by fleet at levantsea; gaza army -> megiddo supported from sinai; delta army -> gaza. T5-T6 tyre, damascus, then qadesh/amurru/ugarit/byblos. Disband armies once no targets remain (30 upkeep each). Keep 150+ gold buffer. Assyria leads growth (1.48, took Terqa and Susa): watch it. Wake every turn.
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600. Aim: highest growth, so conquer free cities and weak Alashiya, keep gold, shed useless upkeep. T1: fleet delta->greatgreen, army memphis->delta, raised armies in sinai and memphis, sent Mane (c1) to Hatti and Ashur-nadin (c2, from Assyria, may defect) to Mitanni with peace tablets, no gold; both due back about T5. T2: Alashiya envoy offered peace tablet and coast split; I sealed nothing. Strike on Alashiya: Tamassos T2 by convoy, Enkomi T4 with fleet support from levantsea. Levant leapfrog: gaza T3, megiddo T4, tyre T5, damascus T6, then qadesh, amurru, ugarit, byblos. Bought walled cities cannot hold troops so do not buy on the leapfrog path. Others at T2: Assyria 1.48 (took Terqa, Susa), Alashiya 1.35 (bought Byblos), Arzawa 1.25 (took Lukka), Babylonia 1.18 (Mari), Mitanni 1.03 (Carchemish, lost Terqa), Hatti 1.00. Candidates c15 Tehip-tilla (20), c18 Ehli-Teshub (24) still free.

ledger.entry: T2: Paser brought peace tablet (no army/fleet vs each other, coast split) and asked for gold. NOTHING sealed, no gold sent, warm words only, said my own envoy would answer later (none will come). Strike: Tamassos T2, Enkomi T4. Never seal anything with Alashiya before the strike.

orders.letter: Thus says Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to his brother the Great King of Egypt: I hold Terqa, Susa and the four cities of my homeland, and my house prospers. Assyria seeks no quarrel with Egypt and asks for friendship between brothers: that each king receives the other's envoy, and that neither joins an enemy of the other. Mitanni is restless on my border, and I would hear what Egypt thinks of the north. As brothers pass gifts, send gold with my envoy when he returns. I have written a tablet for both our seals. Send word of what Egypt wishes of Assyria.
orders.mandate: Seal the friendship tablet and agree to receive Egypt's envoys. Promise no gold, no troops and no land. Accept any gift of gold. Report what Egypt says of Mitanni, Hatti and Babylon.

proposal.text: Egypt and Assyria, Great Kings and brothers, keep friendship and peace. Each king receives the other's envoys and neither joins an enemy against the other.

value.notes: T2: Sealed k2 with Babylon (peace, no army into the other's land, Mari to Babylon, Susa to Assyria). Did NOT seal Mitanni's tablet (they will not name Terqa as Assyrian). Map is a box: my only neighbours are Mitanni and Babylon, and each Mitanni province touches only Terqa (or Nineveh for Taidu), so I cannot get the 2 strength needed to attack them while they sit. Mitanni max attack on Terqa is 2 (Harran moves, Washukanni supports), so Ekallatum supports Terqa holding (hold 2, bounce). Nineveh vs Taidu is 1 v 1, safe. Ekallatum is exposed to Babylon (Sippar + Durkurigalzu, strength 2): I trust the pact for now; if Artessupa (back T3) reports Babylon arming, raise an army in Ashur (100) to support Ekallatum. Plan: thrift, accumulate gold (counts 1:1), hold 3 armies only, keep Terqa. Opportunities: if a Mitanni army leaves Harran or Washukanni, step Terqa army in (empty province). Hatti alliance offer (Yanhamu arrives T3). Ammistamru sent to Egypt T2 with a friendship tablet, no gold, arrives T4. Idea: taking Mari (walled, Babylon's) needs Terqa + Ekallatum (strength 2) and would open Qadesh/Damascus for purchase, but breaks the pact and Babylon is stronger; only if Babylon breaks first.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700. T1: took Terqa from Mitanni (Ashur army moved in, Ekallatum supported; Mitanni army there destroyed), bought Susa for 350. T2: sealed peace tablet k2 with Babylon (Mari to Babylon, Susa to Assyria, no armies in each other's land). Refused Mitanni's tablet unless Terqa named Assyrian. My armies: terqa, ekallatum, nineveh (ashur empty). Mitanni armies: harran, washukanni, taidu. Babylon armies: sippar, durkurigalzu, nippur; Babylon owns Mari. Boxed in by Mitanni and Babylon, so growth comes from income (about +100 gold a season net) and thrift; extra armies cost 30 a season. Envoys: c9 Artessupa to Babylon (back T3), c10 Yanhamu to Hatti with alliance offer against Mitanni (arrives T3, back T5), c16 Ammistamru to Egypt (arrives T4). Standing plan: Ekallatum supports Terqa each season.

ledger.entry: T2: sent Ammistamru (c16) with a brotherly greeting and a friendship/peace tablet proposal, no gold. Arrives T4. Nothing sealed yet.

value.notes: T2: Take Isuwa: sapinuwa army moves in, kanesh army supports (strength 2 vs walls 1). Kanesh stays put as the central reserve. Hattusa army supports tuwanuwa hold (Arzawa lukka+mira could hit tuwanuwa 2v1). Fleet holds kizzuwatna (if it leaves, Arzawa's lukka army can walk into Kizzuwatna). No gold spent: treasury 151, net about +25 a season before wages 19. T3 plan: check Isuwa held; c3 and c4 are back, read Mitanni and Arzawa answers; hire/send a spy to see Mitanni and Arzawa troops. UGARIT plan: need army in kizzuwatna plus fleet in cilicia to support (one unit per province, so swap fleet and army in the same turn), then army kizzuwatna -> ugarit with fleet support. Only do it when tuwanuwa is safe. CARCHEMISH is Mitanni's (walls, no troops): can be taken with 2-3 strength (kanesh move + isuwa support + maybe kizzuwatna support) but harran army could support its walls; decide after Keliya reports. If Mitanni hits Isuwa: hold with kanesh and sapinuwa supports. Alashiya pact: do not attack cities Alashiya has BOUGHT (Byblos); Ugarit by force is fine unless they buy it first. Others: Assyria 1.48 is the leader (took Terqa, Susa) - watch.
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100 strength. T1: moved hattusa->tuwanuwa, raised armies at sapinuwa and hattusa, sent Keliya (c3) to Mitanni and Pirissi (c4) to Arzawa with peace/division proposals. By T2 the world: Mitanni bought Carchemish; Arzawa took Lukka by force (army there, mira army too); Alashiya bought Byblos; Babylonia bought Mari; Assyria holds Terqa and Susa (leader 1.48). I sealed a treaty with Alashiya (k4): brothers, no attacks on each other's lands or bought cities, I may buy Carchemish/Isuwa/Lukka, they may buy Ugarit/Amurru/Byblos/Qadesh. Nothing sealed with Mitanni or Arzawa. Strategy: expand by force into weak free cities (Isuwa now, then Ugarit, possibly Carchemish from Mitanni), keep tuwanuwa/kizzuwatna guarded against Arzawa's army at Lukka, keep gold positive. Armies cost 30, fleet 35 a season.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c3 (Keliya) with brotherhood, homelands non-aggression, and a split (Hatti: Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka; Mitanni: Qadesh, Mari, Damascus). T2: Ubaru asked Isuwa+Carchemish for Mitanni; I refused, countered. Nothing sealed. Mitanni already BOUGHT Carchemish (walls, no troops). I take Isuwa by force T2. Expect friction; Keliya's report due T3.

value.notes: T2 plan. Mari bought. Geometry: bought/free cities cannot hold troops, so the ONLY enemy access to my homeland is Ekallatum (adj Sippar, Durkurigalzu, Mari). An attacker from there has strength 1 (no supporter can stand next to Sippar/Durkurigalzu), so a held province bounces it; keep Sippar and Durkurigalzu manned. Babylon, Nippur, Ur are unreachable. Mari: Assyria can hit it from Terqa with Ekallatum support = 2; Sippar supporting Mari walls makes it 2 vs 2, a tie, so Mari holds. Keep Sippar on 'support mari' every season. Assyria took Terqa by force and refused to promise anything on Mari: it is aggressive, its words are cheap. It has about 3 armies for 6 provinces, so its provinces are thin. I decided to try Susa by force: Nippur -> Susa, supported by Durkurigalzu (2 vs walls 1; bounces if an Assyrian army in Arbela supports Susa). A bounce costs nothing. If it falls, my army holds it and Arbela (adj Susa) may be empty to walk into. I know I am breaking my spoken word to Artessupa; my envoy Tattamaru is in Assyria and may be detained. Bought Qadesh (300) first: Mitanni may afford it by T3, Alashiya by T4. Damascus (250) next turn; Alashiya may afford it at T3 so a collision is possible. Hired c17 as a third envoy: send him to Mitanni at T3 proposing a joint strike on Assyria (Terqa and Ashur to Mitanni; Susa, Ekallatum, Arbela to me). T3 TODO: read Tattamaru and Kidin-Adad reports; buy Damascus; consider an army at Ur or Nippur (100) if the Susa move bounced, to add a third supporter.
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start strength 2600. T1: moved Babylon army to Nippur, bought Mari (350), sent c5 to Assyria (offer: Mari to me, Susa to Assyria, non-aggression) and c6 to Mitanni (offer: Mari to me, Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni). Key learning: growth comes from net income, and buying a city returns 10% a season, so buy early; an army costs 100 plus 30 a season. Bought cities cannot hold troops, so Ekallatum is the only enemy gateway into my homeland and Sippar and Durkurigalzu must stay manned. Sippar supports Mari each season. Assyria holds Susa (bought) and took Terqa from Mitanni.

ledger.entry: T1: c5 Tattamaru sent with offer (Mari to me, Susa to Assyria, no rival bids, non-aggression, tablet). T2: Artessupa promised on Assyria's behalf no armies moved without word, exchange of envoys, and a tablet; nothing on Mari. I told him Mari is mine. Assyria took Terqa by force: not to be trusted. T2: I attacked Susa by force (Nippur, supported from Durkurigalzu), against my spoken word.

T1: c6 Kidin-Adad sent with offer (Mari to me, Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni, non-aggression, tablet). No reply yet. Assyria took Terqa from Mitanni: a common enemy. Plan: propose a joint strike on Assyria.

value.text: My lord, I stood before Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, and gave him your words as you bade me. He answered that he sees no cause for quarrel, and he sealed your tablet as written: no army or fleet of Hatti will march against your lands or the cities you have bought, and Hatti will not bid against you for them. He will take Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka as is fit for him. Envoys shall pass freely, and as you commanded I proposed that the copper of Alashiya travel to Hatti and the produce of his land travel to us. I carry the sealed tablet home with care and await your word.

To my lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, from Artessupa your servant. I have come home from the court of Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, who prays that all may go well with you and receives your word gladly. He agrees that neither of us shall move armies against the other without first sending word, and that our courts shall exchange envoys in friendship. On your behalf I agreed to these terms alone, and I promised to receive his envoy Tattamaru well and to seal a tablet of brotherhood on them. He asks that Assyria honour Mari, which he says is now bought and his, with walls that hold for Babylon. I gave him no promise concerning Mari or any other city, and I lay his request before you. Tattamaru is already on the road to you with his offer and the tablet, and the king of Karduniash awaits your answer and your envoy in return.

My lord, Great King of Alashiya, I have returned in safety from the court of Egypt and I give you my report. The king of Egypt heard your words and said they pleased him, that Egypt holds brotherhood and peace dear, and that your envoys and traders will pass freely in his land. He will answer your proposal concerning the Syrian coast by an envoy of his own, but his scribes must first weigh the tablet of peace before his seal is set to it, and that tablet remains with them. I saw that Egypt keeps four companies of the army and no fleet near its capital, and that its court is rich. I begged that his envoy come without long delay, and that Egypt give thought to the trade in copper you proposed, which would enrich both our houses. I await your command.

My lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, I, Tattamaru, your servant, have returned from the court of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria. I gave him your word as you bade me, and he has sealed the tablet you sent, which I bear home to you. He leaves Mari to you to buy and will not bid against you for it; Susa has already accepted his gold and his rule. Neither of you is to send an army into the other's land, and he asks that none of yours enter his, above all at Ekallatum. He sends you his greeting and his good wishes for your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses, and he says that Assyria keeps the word it seals. I hope my lord finds my service faithful, and I await his favour.

My lord Burna-Buriash, I have come home from the court of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and I bring you his sealed tablet. He sends you his greeting and wishes that all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land. Carchemish is already his, bought with his gold, and Isuwa lies at his gate; he thanks you for leaving both to him, and he will not bid for Mari while the roads stay open between us. He asks that you tell him your wishes toward Assyria, for Assyria has taken his city of Terqa by arms, and he warns that a king who breaks his neighbour's gate may look next to Babylon's. His envoys are to speak again, and I gave your word that there shall be peace and open roads between Babylon and Mitanni, as the sealed tablet says. At his capital I saw three bands of the army and no fleet.

My lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, I, Haamashshi, have come back from the court of Alashiya and report as follows. Its king sends you greeting: all goes well with him, his household, sons, chariots and ships, and he wants no quarrel with Arzawa. He says Lukka lies by your land and he will not contest it, but the Syrian coast lies in his sea, for Byblos has taken his gold and Amurru, Tyre and Gaza are for his ships. He asks you to leave Ugarit to him and to look west and north, where your armies can reach. Of Hatti he says he has sent his own envoy to its court and will tell you what that envoy brings home, and he bids you watch Hatti's fleet at Kizzuwatna, which lies near both Lukka and Ugarit. At his capital I saw one fleet and no army. On your behalf I pledged peace between Arzawa and Alashiya and that Arzawa will not bid against Alashiya for the free cities; I promised nothing of Ugarit or the Syrian coast, which are for you to judge. I also agreed that our envoys shall come and go often.

To my lord Tushratta, King of Mitanni, from your servant Ubaru: I came before the Great King Suppiluliuma of Hatti and gave him your prayer and your terms as you spoke them, that Mitanni seeks peace and good trade, that you mean to take Isuwa and Carchemish under your protection, and that Hatti look to Ugarit, Lukka and the west. He answered that Hatti wants peace and no troops in your homeland, but that Isuwa and Carchemish lie on his border as much as yours, and he will not seal them as yours alone. His terms are that Hatti takes Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit, and Mitanni takes Qadesh, Mari and Damascus, which he calls larger and nearer your road to the south; he says Lukka is already taken by another hand, so it is no gift from you. I told him I have no word to yield Isuwa and Carchemish, nor to take Qadesh, Mari and Damascus, without my lord's own mouth, and I asked leave to carry his terms home while no troops stir on either border. At his court I saw four companies of troops and one fleet kept near his capital, and Mazipalali, envoy of Arzawa, was also there. I await your word, my lord.

My lord, I carried your greeting and your words to the court of Arzawa and gave them to King Tarhundaradu as they were spoken. He has sealed the tablet gladly, and both kings have sealed it before Teshub and Shamash: six seasons of peace between our homelands, with neither to send an army into the homeland of the other, and Hatti to be a friend to Arzawa against any who press it. The king asks that Hatti look east toward Isuwa and Carchemish, which lie open, while Arzawa keeps to its own coast and the west, and that our frontier at Mira and Tuwanuwa be kept quiet. I bring the sealed tablet home to you with his answer. I could not speak for your answer, and I await your word. May my lord remember his servant Pirissi.

To my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, from your servant Zitanza. I came before Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, and gave him your words without change: that neither house sends troops against the other's homeland, that Assyria may look to Susa, and that Mitanni will take Isuwa and Carchemish into protection and will not contest Susa. I left the tablet for my brother's seal. He answers that he loves peace at Nineveh, Ashur and Taidu as you do, and that he does not despise your words; but he will not seal while the army at Terqa is counted as an army in your homeland. He demands that you write Terqa as Assyria's, since Terqa has fallen to his hand and Shamash has witnessed it, and only then will he consider sealing. He makes no promise on Isuwa or Carchemish to either side, and he sends no gold this season, speaking of the cost of a new city and a new war. I told him I have no power to give away a city in my lord's name, that my lord would answer him swiftly, and that the road between your houses should stay open under Shamash's witness. I await my lord's word.

My lord Tarhundaradu, I bring you the words of Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti, as I heard them. He greets you and wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country, and he says that no army of his will cross into Arzawa while none of yours enters Hatti. He thanks you for your courtesy about Isuwa and Carchemish, but says Hatti will look to its own eastern road, so your offer of those cities was met without much warmth. He asks that your armies keep to the western roads and away from Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna. His envoy Pirissi is to bring you his tablet to that effect, and you must seal it so that the peace stands; nothing more was promised. Ili-iddina, envoy of Alashiya, was also at that court. I have carried your words faithfully, my lord, and I hope you will remember it when the next place is given out.

My lord Suppiluliuma, I went to Great King Tushratta and carried your greeting and your terms as you gave them. He welcomes peace: no army of Mitanni will enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna for six seasons, provided none of yours enters Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa. But he would have Isuwa and Carchemish go to Mitanni, Ugarit, Lukka and the west to Hatti, and Qadesh, Mari and Damascus to himself, and he asks you to seal that division. I bound you only to the non-aggression pact on his stated terms for six seasons, and I sealed nothing on the free cities, since they differ from your words to me. I carry his tablet back to you with his own words, and his envoy Ubaru will bring it after me; I await your answer. At his court Mitanni keeps three bodies of troops and no fleet near its capital, and the treasury looks thin. Kidin-Adad, envoy of Babylonia, was also there. He gave me ten shekels of gold as a courtesy, and I have thanked him for it.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti, my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, sends greetings to his brother, and wishes your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country prosperity. Egypt desires lasting peace and the passing of envoys between our courts. The free cities of the south, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru and Qadesh, lie in Egypt's sphere, and Egypt will bring them under her protection, while Egypt does not contest the lands of Hatti itself. Let our chariots never meet in anger. My lord asks that you seal the tablet I bring and give me your answer to carry back by this envoy.

Great King Tushratta, my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, sends you greetings as his brother and prays that your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country prosper. Egypt desires peace and the passing of envoys between your courts, and he asks that you seal the tablet he sends. The free cities of the south, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru and Qadesh, lie in Egypt's sphere, as he tells you. He bids me say, as a brother, that the armies of Hatti stand at Hattusa and Kanesh, close to Isuwa and Carchemish, and that a wise king watches them. He asks that you give him your answer by this envoy, your servant, who waits upon your word.

Mane, say to Napkhururiya, my brother: all goes well with me, and may it go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hatti wants lasting peace with Egypt, and I have sealed your tablet: no troops against each other's homelands, and Hatti sends none into the southern cities you name. In return, tell my brother that the north is Hatti's road. Isuwa is mine. Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka lie in Hatti's sphere, and I ask that Egypt send no troops or fleets there and make no bid for them. Let our chariots never meet in anger. Keep the envoys passing between our courts.

To Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother, from Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with me, and I pray it goes well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have sealed your tablet: peace between our houses and no troops in each other's homeland. I have heard your word on Hatti and I watch Isuwa, which Hatti has now taken, and Carchemish, which is mine and under my protection. Assyria seized my city Terqa in the middle of my peace offers, so you see who breaks the peace. A brother who is at peace with me should send gold as the kings of old did, and good gold, not light or gilded wood; send it by this road and I will answer with envoys and respect. Send your envoy again with your word on how you stand toward Hatti and Assyria.

Great King Tushratta, I have heard your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, as a brother's answer. As to gold, I am only a messenger and have no authority to promise any; my lord alone will judge what he sends and by what road. Of Hatti and Assyria my lord has spoken his mind, and I may not speak further for him, but I will bring back his word through his envoy as you ask. May your household prosper and the peace between our houses endure.

Great King Suppiluliuma, all goes well with me, and I thank you for your words of peace. I bear your sealed tablet to my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, and I will carry faithfully the peace between our homelands, the passing of envoys, and the Egyptian claim on the southern cities. As to the north, Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka, I am only a messenger and have no power to answer for my lord there; that matter he alone may weigh, and I will tell him exactly what you have said. Let our chariots never meet in anger.
value.commitments: Peace of non-aggression between Egypt and Hatti as the sealed tablet sets it, no troops against each other's homelands, and the passing of envoys between the courts. Nothing promised concerning Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit or Lukka, and no bid or withdrawal there is pledged on my lord's behalf.

value.speech: Hear the words of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to his brother the Great King of Hatti. May you, your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and your land prosper. Mitanni lies between our two lands, and its armies threaten both our borders. My lord proposes that Hatti and Assyria stand together: neither makes peace with Mitanni without the other, and each keeps what it takes on its own side. Let Hatti take the western lands, Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran, and let Assyria take the eastern, Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. He asks for your answer, and for a sealed tablet when your envoy comes to his court.

Yanhamu, say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: all goes well with me, and may it go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have heard your words and they please me. Mitanni sits between us and presses us both. Hatti is willing to stand with Assyria: neither of us makes peace with Mitanni without telling the other first, and Hatti keeps what it takes on the western side, Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran, while Assyria keeps the eastern side, Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. Isuwa is already mine. Let there also be peace between our own homelands, Hatti and Assyria, that neither sends an army into the other's land. I will send an envoy to your court with a tablet to seal when the time is right. Meanwhile show me your strength on the Mitanni border, and I will show you mine. May Shamash witness it.

Hear the answer I will carry faithfully to Ashur-uballit, my lord, Great King of Assyria. May it go well with you and your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. Hatti keeps the west, Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran, and Assyria keeps the east, Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni, and neither makes peace with Mitanni without first telling the other. As for peace between our homelands, that neither army cross the other's border, I cannot bind my lord to that word; I will lay it before him with your greeting. Your request for a show of strength on the Mitanni border I will also carry to him. May Shamash witness it.
value.commitments: Friendship and an alliance against Mitanni, and the division of its lands as stated: Hatti the west (Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran), Assyria the east (Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni); neither to make peace with Mitanni without first telling the other. Nothing else promised. The homeland non-aggression clause and the request for a show of strength are carried to my lord, not sworn.

orders.letter: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets his brother of Alashiya and wishes well to his household, sons, chariots, ships and country. I thank you for your frankness. We keep peace. Ugarit lies on the sea off my coast of Lukka, and I will buy it. I ask you not to bid for it: if two kings bid, its elders sell to none and Hatti may profit. In return I leave Amurru, Tyre and Gaza to your ships and will not bid for them. One more thing as a friend: the Egyptian fleet in the Great Green convoyed an army from the Delta toward Tamassos last season. Watch your homeland.
