orders.mandate: May agree to: peace between Arzawa and Alashiya; Alashiya does not bid for Ugarit; Arzawa does not bid for Amurru, Tyre and Gaza; may seal the tablet below. No gold, no military commitment, no promise about Hatti or Egypt.

proposal.text: Arzawa and Alashiya, brothers before Teshub and Shamash: there is peace between them. Arzawa will buy Ugarit and Alashiya will not bid for it. Alashiya will take Amurru, Tyre and Gaza and Arzawa will not bid for them.

value.notes: T3: Treasury 375, need 400 for Ugarit. Buy scheduled T4 (expected treasury about 411 after the 20 scribe fee for the Alashiya tablet). Sent c11 to Alashiya with a tablet: Arzawa buys Ugarit, Alashiya does not bid for it; Alashiya takes Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Arzawa will not bid for those. Also warned Alashiya of the Egyptian fleet convoying an army delta->tamassos. c12 stays home as my envoy for audiences. Armies mira and lukka hold; seha and apasa empty. Hatti pact k1 runs to turn 8; Hatti army at tuwanuwa. If Hatti or Alashiya also bids for Ugarit, nobody gets it: rebid later. After Ugarit: save gold, consider a fleet in cilicia to support Ugarit walls, and look at Tuwanuwa after turn 8 if Hatti is weak. Wake T5 to check.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu. Start strength 1300 (yield 100, 300 gold). T1: took Lukka by force, disbanded fleet, sent envoys to Hatti and Alashiya with peace offers. T2: sealed k1 with Hatti (no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8). Hatti army stands in tuwanuwa. Hatti said it will look east and asked me to keep away from Tuwanuwa/Kizzuwatna; it was cool to my offer of Isuwa/Carchemish. Alashiya wants no quarrel, will not contest Lukka, wants Ugarit and the Syrian coast for itself; my envoy pledged Arzawa will not bid against Alashiya for free cities (not Ugarit). T3: income 125, upkeep 60 for two armies (mira, lukka), wages about 20. Plan: buy Ugarit for 400 at T4 (scheduled), then save. Egypt fleet at greatgreen convoyed an army delta->tamassos (Alashiya's land) at T2. Standings T3: Babylonia 1.51, Alashiya 1.35, Arzawa 1.25, Assyria 1.22, Hatti 1.17, Mitanni 1.03, Egypt 1.00.

ledger.entry: T2: sealed k1 with Hatti (no army into the other's homeland for six seasons, turns 2-8). T3: c12 returned: Hatti cool to my Isuwa/Carchemish offer, wants my armies away from Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna, promised nothing more. Hatti army sits at tuwanuwa. A tablet is not enforced; watch it. No gold either way.

T1: c11 offered peace. T3: c11 back: Alashiya wants no quarrel, will not contest Lukka, claims Syrian coast (Byblos held, Amurru/Tyre/Gaza) and asked me to leave Ugarit to him. c11 pledged peace and no bidding against Alashiya for free cities. T3: sent c11 again with a tablet to seal: I buy Ugarit, Alashiya does not bid; Alashiya takes Amurru/Tyre/Gaza, I do not bid. No gold sent.

orders.letter: To Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother, from Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Ubaru gave me your terms. Isuwa is in your hand; I do not contest it. Carchemish I bought and it is mine; I will not yield it, and I ask you to leave it in peace. You offer Qadesh and Mari as a gift, but they already belong to Babylon, whose Burna-Buriash grows by the southern road; watch him, brother. I offer six seasons of peace: no troops against each other's homeland, none against Carchemish or Isuwa. Ugarit and the west I leave to you while this peace stands. Seal the tablet and let our envoys pass freely.
orders.mandate: Ubaru may agree to the tablet as written, or to small changes of wording. He may not give up Carchemish or any Mitanni province, promise troops or gold, or yield more than Isuwa and Ugarit.

proposal.text: Hatti and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace for six seasons. Neither sends troops against the homeland of the other, nor against Carchemish, which is Mitanni's, nor against Isuwa, which is Hatti's. Mitanni will not bid for Ugarit while this peace stands.

orders.letter: To Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, my brother, from Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Zitanza brought me your answer. Terqa is in your hand and Shamash saw it; I will write it so. Let the tablet say that Terqa is Assyria's and that neither house sends troops against the homeland of the other. Carchemish is mine and under my protection. Brother, look south: Babylon has taken Susa, Mari and Qadesh and grows beside Ekallatum and Arbela; a strong Babylon is no friend to Assyria nor to Mitanni. Seal, and the road between our houses stays open under Shamash.
orders.mandate: Zitanza may agree to the tablet as written, writing Terqa as Assyria's. He may not give any other province, promise troops or gold, or agree to anything against Babylon beyond words.

proposal.text: Assyria and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace. Terqa is Assyria's. Neither sends troops against the homeland of the other: Assyria not against Harran, Washukanni or Taidu, nor against Carchemish, which is Mitanni's; Mitanni not against Nineveh, Ashur, Arbela, Ekallatum or Terqa.

value.notes: T3: Sealed Egypt k10 (peace; I send no troops into Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh). Geometry: I can reach Terqa or Isuwa with only strength 2 (harran + washukanni), defenders get 2 by support, so no solo offensive. Hatti took Isuwa (sapinuwa->isuwa, kanesh support): next target is likely Carchemish (isuwa->carchemish + kanesh support = 2 vs walls 1). So harran supports carchemish walls, washukanni supports harran, taidu supports washukanni (T3-T8). Envoys out: c7 to Hatti with peace tablet (Isuwa Hatti's, Carchemish mine, I leave Ugarit while peace stands; may break if I get gold), c8 to Assyria conceding Terqa for homeland non-aggression (cheap; a seal obliges nobody; if the Terqa army leaves, walk in). Nudged both toward Babylon (leader 1.51). Plan: save gold (127, +44/season), buy Ugarit (400) if still free, hope for Egyptian gold. Wake T5 or when c7/c8 return.
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni, start 1950. T1: bought Carchemish (350), raised army at harran; Assyria took Terqa by force in T1 (killed my army). T2: sealed peace and open roads with Babylon (k3: Babylon leaves Isuwa and Carchemish to me, I leave Mari to Babylon); Hatti offered a homeland pact plus a split of free cities that I did not seal; my T2 attack on Terqa bounced 2 v 2. T3: Hatti took Isuwa; Babylon holds Susa, Mari, Qadesh (295 yield, leader); Assyria refuses to seal unless Terqa is written as Assyria's; sealed Egypt k10 (peace, southern free cities in Egypt's sphere). Lessons: only two of my provinces touch Terqa or Isuwa, so offense needs an ally's third unit; defenders with a support hold 2. Buying a free city costs 10 x yield and returns 10 percent a season, so buy when gold allows (Ugarit 400 borders Carchemish). Upkeep 30 per army, income 150, wages 16, net about +44. Defensive chain: harran supports Carchemish walls, washukanni supports harran, taidu supports washukanni.

ledger.entry: T3: Hatti took Isuwa by force (sapinuwa->isuwa, kanesh support). Ubaru told me Hatti wants Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit for itself and homeland peace. T3: sent Ubaru (c7) with a tablet: six seasons peace, no troops vs homelands, Carchemish or Isuwa; I leave Ugarit while it stands. Nothing sealed yet. Watch Isuwa and Carchemish.

T1 Assyria seized Terqa by force. T2 my counterattack bounced 2 v 2. T3: Zitanza reports Ashur-uballit will seal only if Terqa is written as Assyria's; no gold. T3: sent Zitanza (c8) with a tablet writing Terqa as Assyria's plus homeland non-aggression (Carchemish mine). Not trusted; keep armies home; retake Terqa if its army leaves.

orders.letter: Brother Tushratta, I have read your words through Keliya and I accept the peace between our homelands for six seasons, as you stated it: no army of Mitanni into Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, none of mine into Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa. Seal the tablet Keliya brings. Isuwa I took with my own hand and it stays Hatti's; I will not trade it. Of the free cities I promise nothing now. Keep envoys passing between us.
orders.mandate: Seal the homeland-only tablet below for six seasons. You may drop nothing from it. Concede nothing on Isuwa or Carchemish, agree no division of free cities, give no gold, promise nothing about Assyria.

proposal.text: Hatti and Mitanni are brothers. For six seasons neither shall send army against the homeland provinces of the other: Mitanni not into Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna; Hatti not into Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa. Their envoys pass freely.

orders.letter: Brother of Babylonia, I greet you and wish well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hatti seeks lasting peace with Karduniash. Mari, Qadesh and Susa are yours and I send no troops there. In turn I ask that Babylonia send no army or fleet against what Hatti holds, and make no bid for Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit or Lukka, which lie on Hatti's road. Seal the tablet I send, and let our envoys pass freely.
orders.mandate: Seal the tablet below. You may promise that Hatti sends no troops into Mari, Qadesh or Susa. Give no gold, promise nothing against Egypt, Assyria or Mitanni, and make no alliance.

proposal.text: Babylonia and Hatti are brothers. Neither shall send army or fleet against the homeland of the other, nor against any province the other holds on the day this tablet is sealed, nor bid for it. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T3: Ugarit race. Fleet kizzuwatna -> cilicia; raise army in kizzuwatna (empty after movement; if fleet is blocked nothing is paid). T4 (I wake): new kizzuwatna army -> ugarit, fleet in cilicia supports (2 vs walls 1). Then T5: Carchemish: kanesh -> carchemish, supports from isuwa and ugarit army (3 vs walls 1, 2 if harran supports walls). Carchemish is not Mitanni homeland, so a homeland pact does not bar it. Defence unchanged: kanesh supports isuwa (hold 2 vs harran+washukanni 2), hattusa supports tuwanuwa (Arzawa pact k5 runs to about T8; watch mira/lukka/seha). Sent Keliya to Mitanni with homeland-only tablet (20). Sent Pirissi to Babylonia with a no-attack-on-held-provinces tablet (20), arrives T5; I concede Mari/Qadesh/Susa only by word. Treasury after this: about 28, T4 about 53. Keep above 20 or troops desert. Do not seal any division of free cities with Mitanni. Alashiya may buy Ugarit (400): if they do before T4 I am barred from attacking it; then turn to Carchemish and Lukka. Assyria: tell them later about the homeland pact with Mitanni; let them strike first. Not yet done: Assyria tablet, spies.
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100. T1: raised armies, sent Keliya (c3) to Mitanni and Pirissi (c4) to Arzawa. T2: took Isuwa by force (sapinuwa army in, kanesh supports). Sealed k4 with Alashiya (brothers, no attack on each other's lands or bought cities; I may buy Carchemish/Isuwa/Lukka; they may buy Ugarit/Amurru/Byblos/Qadesh) and k5 with Arzawa (no army into the other's homeland for six seasons from T2). T3: sealed k9 with Egypt (homelands safe; I send no troops into Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh). Assyria proposed a pact against Mitanni (Hatti: Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran; Assyria: Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni); I agreed by word only, nothing sealed. Mitanni offered homeland non-aggression for six seasons but wants Isuwa and Carchemish; Mitanni has 3 armies and a thin treasury. World at T3: Babylonia leads (1.51; holds Mari, Qadesh, Susa), Alashiya 1.35, Arzawa 1.25 (holds Lukka with army), Assyria 1.22, me 1.17 (land yield 210), Mitanni 1.03, Egypt 1.00. Armies: hattusa, kanesh, tuwanuwa, isuwa, fleet kizzuwatna. Plan: Ugarit T4 (fleet cilicia + new kizzuwatna army), Carchemish T5, later Lukka; keep treasury above 20; armies cost 30, fleet 35.

ledger.entry: T3: Keliya reported: Tushratta offers homeland non-aggression for six seasons (if I stay out of Harran, Washukanni, Taidu, Terqa) but wants Isuwa and Carchemish; nothing sealed. Mitanni: 3 armies, thin treasury, no fleet. I sent Keliya back with a homeland-only tablet (not covering Isuwa or Carchemish); he reaches Mitanni T4, home T5. Ubaru may come with Tushratta's tablet: seal no division of cities. Plan: take Carchemish about T5 (not homeland). Harran is off limits while a pact stands.

T3: sent Pirissi (c4) with a tablet: brothers, no army or fleet against homelands or any province the other holds on sealing day; I concede Mari, Qadesh, Susa by word. Arrives T5. Aim: stop Babylonia buying or attacking Ugarit, Carchemish, Lukka, Isuwa. Babylonia leads (1.51) and holds Mari and Qadesh next to Ugarit and Carchemish: watch.

orders.letter: To the Great King of Karduniash, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, wishes health to your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Egypt seeks lasting brotherhood and peace with Babylonia. Egypt marches only on the free cities of the south coast, from Gaza to Damascus, and on the sea lands. Egypt has no quarrel with Babylonia's holdings at Mari and Qadesh and will send no troops against them. Let no army of ours meet yours. Tell me what you ask of Egypt and what word you hear from Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria.
orders.mandate: May agree to and seal the tablet of peace and spheres. May promise an exchange of envoys and that Egypt will hear Babylonia before treating with a third king against it. May NOT promise gold, troops, marriage or any cession of land. Bring home any tablet sealed and the king's word on Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria.

proposal.text: Brotherhood of Egypt and Babylonia: neither shall send army or fleet against the other's lands. Egypt's sphere: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru. Babylonia's sphere: Mari, Qadesh and all lands north and east. Each will hear the other before treating with a third king against him.

value.notes: T3 plan. T2 convoy to Tamassos bounced (Alashiya fleet enkomi->tamassos, 1 v 1). Old schedule was stale (akhetaten->sinai not adjacent, memphis cannot support gaza), so I replaced T3 and T4. T3: delta army -> gaza with sinai army supporting (strength 2 v walls 1); delta then empty so raise fleet F2 there (120). Fleet F greatgreen -> tamassos as a free roll: succeeds if Alashiya fleet does not also enter; a bounce costs nothing. If F holds Tamassos, the Alashiya fleet cannot dislodge it alone. Then F2 delta->levantsea, F2 -> enkomi with F at tamassos supporting (2 v 1) kills their fleet and takes Enkomi. T4: gaza army -> megiddo, sinai army supports. M (memphis) and A (akhetaten) follow up as supporters: M to delta/sinai, then gaza; chain tyre, damascus, then amurru, byblos, ugarit, qadesh. Diplomacy: c17 sent to Babylonia with peace and sphere tablet, no gold, back about T7. c1 and c2 due back about T5; pay back pay then. Keep 150+ gold. Wake every turn (wake_in_turn). Watch Babylonia (1.51) and its Qadesh next to Damascus. Ashur-nadin (c2) may defect.
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600. Aim: highest growth, so take free cities and weak Alashiya, keep gold, avoid useless upkeep. T1-T2: fleet to greatgreen, armies raised in sinai, memphis, akhetaten; Mane (c1) to Hatti and Ashur-nadin (c2, Assyrian-born, may defect) to Mitanni with peace tablets and no gold, both due back about T5. T2: Alashiya envoy Paser got warm words only, nothing sealed; my convoy of the delta army to Tamassos bounced against their fleet. T3: delta army -> gaza (sinai supports), raised fleet F2 at delta, fleet F -> tamassos, c17 sent to Babylonia with sphere tablet (Egypt: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru; Babylonia: Mari, Qadesh, north). Plan: F2 + F take Enkomi (F2 from levantsea, F supports from tamassos); army chain megiddo T4, tyre, damascus, then amurru, byblos, ugarit, qadesh. Walled bought cities cannot hold troops, so conquer rather than buy on the path. Standings T3: Babylonia 1.51, Alashiya 1.35, Arzawa 1.25, Assyria 1.22, Hatti 1.17, Mitanni 1.03, Egypt 1.00. Candidates c15 (20) and c18 (24) are free if envoys are needed. Keep 150+ gold buffer and wake every turn.

ledger.entry: T3: sent c17 with greeting, peace and sphere tablet (Egypt: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru; Babylonia: Mari, Qadesh, north). No gold. Back about T7. Nothing sealed yet.
T2: Paser brought peace tablet and asked for gold. NOTHING sealed, no gold sent, warm words only. T3: my fleet tries Tamassos, second fleet raised for Enkomi. Never seal anything with Alashiya.

orders.letter: To Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land. Your tablet reached me and I thank you. You ask my wishes toward Assyria. Assyria took your Terqa by arms and broke faith with me also, so I took Susa from it. I stand with you, not against you: the tablet between us holds, Isuwa and Carchemish are yours, Mari is mine, the roads are open and no army of mine will enter your land. Assyria keeps few bands for five provinces. Let us act together and make no separate peace: you retake Terqa and press Ashur and Nineveh, I will take Arbela and Ekallatum. Send your envoy with your answer and I will hear him gladly.
orders.mandate: May agree for me that Babylon and Mitanni make war together on Assyria; that Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to Mitanni and Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Babylon; that neither makes peace with Assyria without the other; that the roads stay open and the old tablet stands. May NOT promise gold, cede land, bind my armies to a fixed season, or let any army of mine enter Mitanni's land. Seal nothing.

orders.letter: To the Great King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. We are neighbours now in the cities of the Levant: you hold Byblos, I hold Mari and Qadesh and this season I bid for Damascus. When two kings bid for one city its elders sell to neither, and both lose a season of its yield. Let us not bid against each other. I would take Damascus, Megiddo, Gaza and Tyre; you would take Amurru. Send your answer by your envoy and let copper and good gold pass between our houses.
orders.mandate: May agree that neither Alashiya nor Babylon bids against the other in the Levant, with Damascus, Megiddo and Gaza left to Babylon and Amurru left to Alashiya. May also concede Tyre to Alashiya if it insists. May NOT promise gold, cede land, or say anything of Ugarit. Seal nothing.

value.notes: T3 plan. Susa fell to me (army now stands there; walls gone so it can hold troops). Qadesh bought. Strength 3300, growth 1.27, best of all. Orders: buy Damascus (250, borders Mari and Qadesh; Alashiya probably cannot afford it yet), raise a 4th army at Nippur (100), Sippar keeps supporting Mari, Dk and Susa hold. Treasury ends near 0 but income 295+ covers upkeep. Arbela (Assyria) is EMPTY now; Susa army alone in Arbela would hold 1 and could be dislodged by 2 Assyrian armies (Ekallatum plus one from Ashur/Nineveh). So wait: T4 Susa -> Arbela and new Nippur army -> Susa (follow in); T5 Susa army supports Arbela holding (2), Assyria then needs 3. Do not strip Dk or Sippar: Ekallatum army would walk in. Susa is safe while my army holds it (only Arbela touches it, max attack 1 = bounce). If Assyria raises an army in Arbela, I cannot take it (only Susa touches it); then think again. Envoys: c6 to Mitanni (1 season) verbally proposing joint war on Assyria, no tablet (deniable); c5 to Alashiya (2 seasons) verbally proposing a split of Levant cities: they Amurru (and Tyre if pressed), I Damascus, Megiddo, Gaza, Tyre. Next purchases: Amurru 200, Tyre 250, Megiddo 200, Ugarit 400 (contested by Hatti, Mitanni, Alashiya), Gaza 200. Gold left over should become armies to take Assyrian land (Arbela 30, Ekallatum 25). Wake at T4 to give orders (new army cannot be scheduled before it exists).
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start strength 2600. T1: moved Babylon army to Nippur, bought Mari, sealed k6 with Assyria (no armies in each other's land; Mari mine to buy, Susa Assyria's to buy) and k7 with Mitanni (peace, open roads; I leave Isuwa and Carchemish to Mitanni; Mitanni leaves Mari to me). T2: took Susa from Assyria by force (Nippur army, supported from Durkurigalzu), bought Qadesh. Assyria took Terqa from Mitanni and is hostile and untrustworthy; Mitanni failed to retake Terqa. Key learning: growth comes from net income; a bought city returns 10 percent a season; an army costs 100 plus 30 a season. Bought cities cannot hold troops, so Ekallatum is the only enemy gateway into my homeland: Sippar and Durkurigalzu must stay manned, Sippar supports Mari each season (ties bounce). Susa is safe while manned (only Arbela touches it). Plan: buy Damascus (T3), then Amurru, Tyre, Megiddo, Gaza, Ugarit as gold allows; build a 4th army at Nippur to take Arbela (empty) with Susa supporting; coordinate with Mitanni against Assyria.

ledger.entry: T1: tablet k7 sealed (peace, open roads; Isuwa and Carchemish left to Mitanni; Mari left to me). T3: c6 back with their word: Tushratta asks my wishes toward Assyria and hints Babylon may be next after Assyria's attack on Terqa. T3: c6 sent again, spoken only, no tablet: joint war on Assyria (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to me), no separate peace.

T2: tablet k6 sealed (no armies in each other's land; Mari mine to buy, Susa Assyria's to buy). Assyria bought Susa; I took it by arms at T2, against the spirit of k6. Assyria took Terqa from Mitanni by arms: hostile. Expect revenge via Ekallatum or Arbela. Plan: take Arbela with a second army behind in Susa.
T3: c5 sent, spoken only, no tablet: neither bids against the other in the Levant; Alashiya takes Amurru (Tyre if pressed), I take Damascus, Megiddo, Gaza, Tyre. Alashiya holds Byblos.

orders.letter: Paser speaks for the Great King of Alashiya, to Egypt, my brother. Alashiya thanks you for welcoming my envoy and for your words of peace. Yet while Paser sat in your house, an army of Egypt set out by sea from the Delta against Tamassos, borne by your fleet in the Great Green. Alashiya holds this the error of your captains and not your will, brother; my fleet met it and it failed. Know that Alashiya keeps its ships and its army on guard, holds brotherhood with Hatti by a sealed tablet, and is at peace with Arzawa. Let us seal the peace: no army or fleet of Egypt against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos or any city Alashiya has bought; none of mine against Egypt or its cities. Egypt may buy Gaza and Megiddo; Alashiya may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Tyre and Damascus. Your envoys and traders pass freely in Cyprus. Send your envoy swiftly with the sealed answer, and let Egypt send gold in friendship for the copper I will send, as kings send to their brothers. May your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper.
orders.mandate: Paser may agree to a tablet of peace and free passage, may concede Gaza and Megiddo to Egypt, and may accept any gold Egypt gives. He may not promise gold, troops or land, nor concede Tyre, Damascus, Amurru or Ugarit, nor seal anything I have not seen. He should come home with Egypt's answer and note what troops and ships he sees.

orders.letter: Ili-iddina speaks for the Great King of Alashiya to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother. As I promised Haamashshi, I share news of Hatti. Suppiluliuma told my envoy that he will take Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka as is fit for him. Lukka is yours by your army, but Hatti counts it his to take; guard your border. Now let us seal what we spoke. Arzawa holds Lukka and I shall never bid for it. Arzawa may buy Ugarit and I will not bid against you. Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus are for Alashiya, and Arzawa will not bid for them. Neither sends army or fleet against the lands of the other or the cities the other has bought. Envoys pass freely. Seal the tablet and send it home with my envoy. May your household, sons, chariots and horses prosper.
orders.mandate: Ili-iddina may agree to the tablet as written, may promise to share news of Hatti, and may give up my claim to Ugarit. He may not pay gold, cede land, promise troops, or weaken the clause that protects Tamassos, Enkomi and my bought cities.

proposal.text: Alashiya and Arzawa are brothers. Neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought. Arzawa holds Lukka and Alashiya will not bid for it. Arzawa may buy Ugarit; Alashiya may buy Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus; neither shall bid for the other's cities. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T3: Egypt (army delta + fleet greatgreen) tried to land at Tamassos in T2 while I was empty; it bounced vs my fleet move (1 v 1). Egypt is NOT to be trusted; expect a retry with a second fleet for support (strength 2). Defence plan: two units on Cyprus with mutual support (fleet supports army holding, army supports fleet holding). This turn: fleet enkomi->tamassos, raise army AT TAMASSOS (levy happens after movement; works only if Egypt bounces my fleet again and tamassos stays empty; if no attack, fleet sits in tamassos, levy fails and costs nothing; then T4 raise army at enkomi, which nobody can reach this season). Enkomi cannot be attacked unless a foreign fleet first sits in levantsea/cilicia/syriansea (I can see those). Sent Paser to Egypt (protest, peace offer, Egypt may buy Gaza+Megiddo, ask gold gift, no tablet) and Ili-iddina to Arzawa (tablet: Arzawa keeps Lukka, may buy Ugarit; I get Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus; share news that Hatti means to take Lukka). Conceding Ugarit (400) is cheap: I cannot afford it for 8+ seasons anyway and Arzawa will beat me; it buys goodwill. Money: income 115, fleet 35, army 30, wages 21. Buy order: Amurru 200, Gaza 200 (Egypt may contest), Tyre 250, Damascus 250 (Babylon at Qadesh may contest). Two bids in one season = nobody gets it. Walled bought cities cannot hold troops but need 2 units to take. Wake T4 to re-plan.
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). Sent Paser (c14) to Egypt and Ili-iddina (c13) to Hatti with brotherhood and carve-up tablets. T2: Hatti sealed tablet k8 (no army/fleet vs each other's lands or bought cities; Hatti may buy Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; I may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Byblos, Qadesh). Hatti told me it will take Lukka, but Arzawa already holds it. Arzawa envoy Haamashshi pledged peace and no rival bidding; I conceded Lukka. Babylonia holds Mari, Qadesh, Susa (growth 1.51, the leader). Egypt tried to land an army at Tamassos by convoy in T2 (failed, bounced by my fleet). Egypt gave Paser warm words but has not sealed. T3: see notes. Economy: strength = 10*yield + gold - backpay; buying a free city costs 10*yield and pays yield each season. Free cities left: Ugarit 40, Amurru 20, Damascus 25, Gaza 20, Megiddo 20, Tyre 25.

ledger.entry: T2: Egyptian army convoyed from Delta tried to land at Tamassos while Paser sat in their court; bounced. T3: Paser says Egypt praises peace, will answer by own envoy, my T1 tablet unsealed in their scribes' hands. T3: sent Paser again: protest, peace offer (Egypt may buy Gaza, Megiddo; I Ugarit, Amurru, Tyre, Damascus), asked gold gift. No tablet, no gold. Distrust.

Sealed k8 (turn 2): no army or fleet against each other's lands or bought cities; Hatti may buy Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; I may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Byblos, Qadesh. Hatti said it will take Lukka (Arzawa holds it). Copper-for-produce trade proposed, no reply. No gold paid either way.

T2: Haamashshi pledged peace, no rival bidding; I gave Lukka. T3: sent Ili-iddina with tablet (Arzawa keeps Lukka, may buy Ugarit; I get Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus; no army or fleet against each other's lands) and the news that Hatti means to take Lukka. No gold.

orders.letter: To Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother, from Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have weighed the words Zitanza brought. I wish peace between our houses. Terqa is held by my armies and is Assyrian; I ask that you name it so. In return I will not move against Harran, Washukanni or Taidu, and I will not enter Carchemish or Isuwa. Hear this also: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash sealed a peace tablet with me and in the same season seized my city Susa. His word is wind, and a king who breaks one oath will break another. Let Assyria and Mitanni not feed him by fighting each other. Seal the tablet Artessupa carries and send word.
orders.mandate: Artessupa may seal the tablet as written, or with small changes if Terqa stays named Assyrian and nothing is ceded. He may not give gold, land or troops, and may not promise action against any named power.

proposal.text: Assyria and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace. Terqa is held by Assyria; Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish are held by Mitanni. Neither king moves an army against a province of the other. Assyria does not enter Isuwa or Carchemish. Either king who wishes to end this peace first sends word by envoy.

value.notes: T3: Babylon BROKE k2 (nippur->susa, durkurigalzu supporting, took my Susa; walls fell) in the same season it sealed. Trust nothing from Burna-Buriash. His envoy Tattamaru arrives T4 with a new tablet: use it only for calm, never rely on it. Babylon armies: sippar, durkurigalzu, susa; nippur empty. T3 orders: terqa holds, ekallatum supports terqa, nineveh army -> arbela (blocks Susa: 1 v 1 bounce), raised an army at ashur (capital reserve, appears end of T3). Nineveh is left empty on purpose as bait for Taidu: if Mitanni enters Nineveh, retake in T4 with arbela + ashur (2 v 1; dislodged units are destroyed). If they reinforced taidu it bounces. Ekallatum holds only 1 this turn (risk: sippar + durkurigalzu = 2). From T4: terqa holds, ekallatum supports terqa, arbela unit supports ekallatum, ashur army is the reserve (can refill nineveh). Arbela has three friendly neighbours (nineveh, ashur, ekallatum) so I can retake it with strength 3. Sent Artessupa (c9) to Mitanni with a peace tablet: Terqa named Assyrian, no armies into each other's provinces, I stay out of Isuwa and Carchemish. Wake T4: Tattamaru, maybe Zitanza's reply. Gold is about 29 after the army and tablet; net income about +45 with 4 armies, so no more armies. Hatti: Yanhamu (c10) back about T5 with their answer. Idea: Hatti army in Isuwa plus my Terqa army against Harran, if Hatti agrees.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700. T1: took Terqa from Mitanni (Mitanni army there destroyed), bought Susa for 350. T2: sealed k2 with Babylon (peace, Mari to Babylon, Susa to Assyria, no armies in each other's land). Babylon broke it at once: its army took Susa in T2 (I lost 350 of value). Mitanni attacked Terqa (harran + washukanni, 2) and bounced off Ekallatum's support. Map: I touch only Mitanni and Babylon; each enemy province touches only one of mine, so I cannot mass 2 on an attack alone. Dislodged units are destroyed, so a defender with several friendly neighbours wins exchanges inside his own land. Babylon is the leader (land yield 295, bought Mari and Qadesh, took Susa). People: c9 Artessupa (sent to Mitanni T3, back about T5), c10 Yanhamu (Hatti, alliance offer vs Mitanni, back about T5), c16 Ammistamru (Egypt, arrives T4, back T6). c13 Ili-iddina is secretly in my pay inside Babylon. Armies: terqa, ekallatum, arbela (from nineveh), new one at ashur. Wages cost about 37 a season; growth comes from thrift and opportunities.

ledger.entry: T2: sealed k2 (peace, no army into the other's land, Mari to Babylon, Susa to Assyria). Babylon BROKE it: took my Susa by force in T2. Tattamaru is on the road with a new tablet, arrives T4. I owe nothing now; trust nothing. I did not bid for Mari. Artessupa reported Burna-Buriash wants mutual warning before moves and envoys exchanged.

T1: I took Terqa by force. T2: I did not seal Tushratta's tablet (no Terqa clause). T3: sent Artessupa with a peace tablet: Terqa Assyrian, no armies into each other's provinces, I stay out of Isuwa and Carchemish, warning before any break. Nothing sealed yet. They attacked Terqa in T2 and failed.

value.speech: Great King Tushratta, my lord Suppiluliuma of Hatti sends his word to you by my mouth. Brother, he has read your words through Keliya and accepts the peace between your homelands for six seasons, as you stated it: no army of Mitanni shall enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, and none of Hatti shall enter Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa. He asks that you seal the tablet I bring. Isuwa he took with his own hand and it remains Hatti's; he will not trade it. Of the free cities he promises nothing now, but he asks that envoys keep passing between your courts.

Great King Ashur-uballit, my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother, sends this word: may all go well with you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. You have sent your answer by my hand, and Terqa is in your hand; Shamash saw it, and my lord will write it so. Let the tablet say that Terqa is Assyria's, and that neither house sends troops against the homeland of the other. Carchemish is my lord's and under his protection. Brother, look south: Babylon has taken Susa, Mari and Qadesh and grows beside Ekallatum and Arbela, and a strong Babylon is no friend to Assyria nor to Mitanni. Seal the tablet, I pray you, and the road between our houses stays open under Shamash.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, thus speaks Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, across the Great Green. He wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots, your ships and your country, and he thanks you for your frankness; we keep peace. Ugarit lies on the sea off his coast of Lukka, and he will buy it, so he asks you not to bid for it, for when two kings bid its elders sell to neither and Hatti may profit. In return he leaves Amurru, Tyre and Gaza to your ships and will not bid for them. As a friend he adds this warning: the Egyptian fleet in the Great Green convoyed an army from the Delta toward Tamassos last season, so watch your homeland. Here is the tablet of brothers before Teshub and Shamash, which I ask you to seal.

Great King Tarhundaradu, my brother, thus speaks the Great King of Alashiya, your brother, through me, Ili-iddina, who speaks for him. As he promised Haamashshi, I share news of Hatti: Suppiluliuma told my lord's envoy that he will take Carchemish, Isuwa and Lukka as is fit for him. Lukka is yours by your army, but Hatti counts it his to take, so guard your border. Let us now seal what we have spoken. Arzawa holds Lukka and Alashiya will never bid for it. Arzawa may buy Ugarit and Alashiya will not bid against you. Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus are for Alashiya, and Arzawa will not bid for them. Neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other or the cities the other has bought, and envoys shall pass freely. I ask that you seal the tablet and send it home with me. May your household, sons, chariots and horses prosper.

Great King Suppiluliuma, my lord Tushratta, King of Mitanni, your brother, sends you this word by my mouth: may all go well with you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Ubaru gave you my lord's terms, and my lord holds to them. Isuwa is in your hand and he does not contest it. Carchemish he bought and it is his; he will not yield it, and he asks you to leave it in peace. Qadesh and Mari, which you offer as a gift, already belong to Babylon, whose Burna-Buriash grows by the southern road; watch him, brother, my lord says. He offers six seasons of peace, with no troops against each other's homeland, none against Carchemish or Isuwa, and he leaves Ugarit and the west to you while this peace stands. Here is the tablet; I beg you seal it and let our envoys pass freely.

Great King Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, my lord's brother: thus says Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. He holds Terqa, Susa and the four cities of his homeland, and his house prospers; Assyria seeks no quarrel with Egypt. He asks for friendship between brothers, that each king receives the other's envoy and neither joins an enemy of the other. Mitanni is restless on his border, and he would hear what Egypt thinks of the north. As brothers pass gifts, he sends gold with me, and asks that Egypt send gold with his envoy when he returns. He has written a tablet for both our seals, and asks Egypt to say what it wishes of Assyria.

Brother Ashur-uballit, Napkhururiya greets you and your house. Egypt takes your friendship gladly. We will receive your envoys and join no enemy of yours. Egypt looks to the southern coast and to its own borders; of the north we say only that Hatti's armies stand near Isuwa and Carchemish, and a wise brother watches them. We seal your tablet. Gold from Egypt will follow when envoys have crossed and friendship is proven. Send me word of what you see in the north.

Brother Suppiluliuma, I have heard your word through Keliya and I seal the tablet: six seasons of peace between our homelands, and open roads for our envoys. Carchemish is mine by purchase and stands under my hand; I count it as my own country and will hold it so. Isuwa you took by your own hand, and I will not make it a quarrel between us while our peace stands. Let envoys keep passing between our courts. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your country.

Brother Tushratta, may Shamash keep you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your tablet names Terqa as Assyria's and keeps our homelands apart, and I seal it gladly. Assyria keeps its armies from Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish, and Mitanni keeps its from Nineveh, Ashur, Arbela, Ekallatum and Terqa. You judge Babylon rightly: Burna-Buriash has broken his oath to me once already, and a king who breaks one oath breaks the next. Let our two houses warn each other before either moves against a third land, and let our envoys come and go freely. Artessupa, my envoy, is at your court with my own word. Carry my brotherly greeting home.

Brother of Arzawa, I thank you for the warning, and for your frankness. I seal your tablet. Ugarit is yours to buy and I will not bid for it; Amurru, Tyre and Gaza I will take, and you will leave them to me. Let our peace stand before Teshub and Shamash. Know that Hatti's fleet now lies in the Cilician Sea, next to my capital, though Hatti swore brotherhood with me. Tell me what you see of Hatti's ships and armies, and I will tell you what I see. A gift of gold from your king to mine would show this peace is real.

Ili-iddina, brother of my brother, I receive you gladly and thank your lord for the warning about Suppiluliuma. I seal the tablet as written: Arzawa holds Lukka and Alashiya will not bid for it; Arzawa buys Ugarit and Alashiya does not bid; Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus are for Alashiya and I will not bid for them; neither sends army or fleet against the other's lands or bought cities; envoys pass freely. Carry it home. Hatti has an army and a fleet near Lukka, so I ask one thing more as a brother: if Hatti marches on Lukka, let your ships in the Cilician Sea stand by Lukka and Ugarit, as I would stand by your cities. Tell your lord that Egypt's fleet at the Great Green and its army in Tamassos are a danger to us both, and that I will share every report of them. May your lord's household, sons, chariots and horses prosper.

Ubaru, say to Tushratta, my brother: all goes well with me, and may all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have heard your word and read your tablet, and I have sealed it. Six seasons of peace between us: no troops against each other's homeland, none against Carchemish which is yours, none against Isuwa which is mine, and you will not bid for Ugarit. Let our envoys pass freely in both directions, and let no messenger of either house be held. I keep faith with a brother who keeps faith with me. Your warning about Babylon is noted.

Great King Tushratta, I take your sealed tablet to my lord Suppiluliuma, and I carry your word as you have spoken it: six seasons of peace between our homelands, and open roads for our envoys. Your words on Carchemish and on Isuwa I will set down before my lord exactly as you gave them, and I will add nothing to them. May the road be kind to me, and may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your country.
value.commitments: Envoys of Hatti and Mitanni to keep passing between the two courts while the six seasons of peace stand. Nothing given on Isuwa, Carchemish, the free cities or Assyria.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, all goes well with me, and I receive your word and your sealed tablet with gladness. I will carry them to my lord Tushratta and tell him that the six seasons of peace stand as you have written them, with no troops against each other's homeland, none against Carchemish or Isuwa, and Ugarit left to you. Your warning about Babylon is heard, and I will not forget it. May your household, sons, chariots, horses and country prosper, and may our envoys pass freely.
value.commitments: On behalf of my lord Tushratta: six seasons of peace with Hatti; no troops against each other's homeland; none against Carchemish (Mitanni) or Isuwa (Hatti); Mitanni will not bid for Ugarit; envoys and messengers of both houses pass freely in both directions and are not held.

value.speech: Great King Napkhururiya, my lord's brother, your word is heard and I will carry it home as it was spoken. Egypt takes my lord's friendship gladly, and Egypt will join no enemy of Assyria, while Assyria will receive Egypt's envoys. Of the north I will report that Hatti's armies stand near Isuwa and Carchemish and that a wise brother watches them; Egypt has said nothing of Mitanni or of Babylon, and I will report that silence as well. The tablet is sealed, and I trust my lord will rejoice that Egypt's gold will follow when envoys have crossed.
value.commitments: Assyria will receive Egypt's envoys, as the sealed tablet provides. No gold, troops or land promised.

value.speech: Great King Tarhundaradu, my brother, I am honoured that you receive me, and I take your sealed tablet home to my lord exactly as it is written: Arzawa holds Lukka and buys Ugarit, Alashiya will bid neither for Lukka nor against you at Ugarit, and Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus remain for Alashiya. I will carry your words on the Egyptian fleet at the Great Green and the army at Tamassos to my lord, and I will share what news of Hatti reaches me. As to ships standing by Lukka and Ugarit, I am only a messenger and cannot pledge my lord's fleet, but I will set your request before him with all respect. May your household, sons, chariots and horses prosper.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf, as sealed: Alashiya gives up its claim to Ugarit and will not bid against Arzawa for it; Alashiya will not bid for Lukka; neither side sends army or fleet against the other's lands or bought cities; envoys pass freely; Alashiya will share news of Hatti. No promise of ships, troops, gold or land was made; the request that ships stand by Lukka and Ugarit is referred to my lord.

value.speech: Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I have heard your words and I will carry them home to Tarhundaradu. Our tablet is sealed before Teshub and Shamash: you will not bid for Ugarit, and my lord will not bid for Amurru, Tyre and Gaza. As for gold, I have no word from my lord and no gold in my hands to give, so a gift must wait for his answer. As for Hatti's ships and armies, I have seen none on my road that I can swear to, but I will tell my lord all you have said of the fleet in the Cilician Sea.
value.commitments: Peace between Arzawa and Alashiya, sealed before Teshub and Shamash. Arzawa will not bid for Amurru, Tyre and Gaza. Alashiya will not bid for Ugarit. No gold, no military commitment, and no promise about Hatti or Egypt.

value.speech: Great King Ashur-uballit, my lord Tushratta will be glad to hear that you have sealed his word and sent your greeting. I take your tablet home as it stands: Terqa is Assyria's, neither house sends troops against the other's homeland, and each warns the other before moving against a third land. I will greet Artessupa, your envoy, at my lord's court. May Shamash keep you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country, and may the road between our houses stay open.
value.commitments: Agreed, as Mitanni's envoy, to the tablet as sealed: Terqa is Assyria's; neither house sends troops against the other's homeland; Assyria keeps its armies from Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish, and Mitanni from Nineveh, Ashur, Arbela, Ekallatum and Terqa; each house warns the other before moving against a third land; envoys may come and go freely. No other province, troops or gold promised, and nothing against Babylon beyond these words.

value.speech: Great King, my brother, king of Egypt, I speak for the Great King of Alashiya. My lord thanks you for welcoming his envoy and for your words of peace. Yet while Paser sat in your house, an army of Egypt set out by sea from the Delta against Tamassos, borne by your fleet in the Great Green; my lord holds this the error of your captains and not your will, brother, for his fleet met it and it failed. Let us seal the peace: no army or fleet of Egypt against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos or any city Alashiya has bought, and none of his against Egypt or its cities. Egypt may buy Gaza and Megiddo, and Alashiya may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Tyre and Damascus; let your envoys and traders pass freely in Cyprus, send your envoy swiftly with the sealed answer, and send gold in friendship for the copper my lord will send, as kings send to their brothers. May your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses prosper.

Kidin-Adad of Nippur, envoy of Burna-Buriash, speaks before Tushratta, Great King, my lord's brother. Thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash: may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land. Your tablet reached him and he thanks you. Assyria took your Terqa by arms and broke faith with him also, so he took Susa from it. He stands with you, not against you: the tablet between you holds, Isuwa and Carchemish are yours, Mari is his, the roads are open, and no army of his shall enter your land. Let us act together and make no separate peace: you retake Terqa and press Ashur and Nineveh, and he will take Arbela and Ekallatum. Send your envoy with your answer, for he will hear him gladly.

Brother of Alashiya, Egypt greets you and your house. The movement of ships in the Great Green was the haste of captains at sea, not a quarrel with you. Egypt wishes your household, chariots and country well and holds you a brother. Egypt has no sealed word to give today; your words are heard, and our own envoy will carry Egypt's answer when the season allows. Go in peace, and bring copper, brother, and we will speak of gifts when it comes.

Kidin-Adad, say to Burna-Buriash my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots and my horses, and I wish the same for you and all Karduniash. Your tablet holds with me: Isuwa and Carchemish are mine to keep from you, Mari is yours, and no army of mine will enter your land. I welcome your word against Assyria, who broke faith with us both. Let it be so: when your armies fall on Ekallatum and Arbela, my armies will be ready on Terqa, and I will strike the moment its garrison is drawn off or weakened. Move first at Ekallatum, since that draws their support away from Terqa, and send me word by your envoy of the season you strike so that our blows land together. Neither of us makes a separate peace with Ashur-uballit. Watch also the king of Hatti, who has taken Isuwa and now gathers armies on my border; a Hatti grown fat is a danger to us both.

Great King, my brother, I hear your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord of Alashiya. Since you say your envoy will come when the season allows, I ask that he come swiftly with the sealed answer, so that my lord's heart may be eased. As my lord has spoken, copper will follow, and I would count it an honour to be the one who carries it to your house. May your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses prosper, brother.

Hear me, Tushratta, Great King, as my lord's word. Burna-Buriash agrees that Karduniash and Mitanni make war together upon Assyria, that Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to you, and that Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa go to him; neither king makes peace with Ashur-uballit without the other, the roads stay open, and the old tablet stands. I have no mandate to name the season of his strike or the order of his blows, and I will not bind his armies to either, but I will carry your wish to him and bring back his word. Your warning of Hatti is heard, and my lord will consider it. Nothing is sealed today.
value.commitments: Agreed for Burna-Buriash within his mandate: Karduniash and Mitanni make war together on Assyria; Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa go to Karduniash; no separate peace with Assyria without the other; roads stay open; the old tablet stands. Nothing sealed. No season, no order of strikes, no gold, no land ceded, and no army of Karduniash to enter Mitanni's land.

value.speech: Hear the word of Artessupa, envoy of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. To Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. My lord has weighed the words Zitanza brought and wishes peace between our houses. Terqa is held by his armies and is Assyrian, and he asks that you name it so; in return he will not move against Harran, Washukanni or Taidu, nor enter Carchemish or Isuwa. Hear also that Burna-Buriash of Karduniash sealed a peace tablet with my lord and in the same season seized Susa; his word is wind, and Assyria and Mitanni should not feed him by fighting each other. Seal the tablet I carry, and send word.

Artessupa, say to Ashur-uballit my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots and my horses, and I wish the same for you and all Assyria. Your word and your tablet have reached me and I seal it. Terqa is held by your armies and is written as yours; Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish are mine, and neither of us moves an army against the other's lands. Hold to it: do not enter Carchemish or Isuwa, and I will not touch Terqa. Between brothers, let any word of ending this peace come first by envoy. Send me news of Hatti and of the armies on the roads of the north, and I will do the same for you.

Hear the word of Artessupa, envoy of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my lord's brother. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. My lord holds to what is sealed: Terqa is written as Assyrian, Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish are yours, and neither of us moves an army against the other's lands. He will not enter Carchemish or Isuwa. Between brothers, any word of ending this peace shall come first by envoy, as you ask. I will carry your request for news of Hatti and of the armies on the northern roads to my lord, and bring back his answer.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: the peace tablet as sealed, with Terqa named Assyrian; my lord will not enter Carchemish or Isuwa, nor move against Harran, Washukanni or Taidu; any word of ending this peace will come first by envoy. No gold, land, troops or action against any named power is promised.

orders.letter: Tarhundaradu greets Suppiluliuma, my brother, and asks after his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I keep the peace of our sealed tablet and send no army into your homeland. Travellers say your harvest has failed; may Teshub restore your fields. I hold Lukka, taken from free men, and mean only to keep it. Egypt's fleet roams the Great Green and Egypt's army stands in Alashiya's land, a danger to every coast. Tell me what Hatti wants from his brother in the west, and what he intends in the east, where Carchemish and the free cities lie. Arzawa will not bid for any city of Hatti.
orders.mandate: Restate our peace and listen to any proposal, then bring it home. Agree to nothing binding, give no gold, cede nothing, and seal no tablet. You may promise only that Arzawa will not bid for Hatti's cities.

value.notes: T4: Sealed k17 with Alashiya (Lukka mine, Ugarit mine to buy, Alashiya takes Byblos/Amurru/Tyre/Gaza/Damascus, no attack on each other's lands). Treasury 411; scheduled buy of Ugarit (400) runs this season, leaving about 11. Kept this season free of tablets and gold so the 400 is not blocked (letters reserve gold first). Mira and Lukka now support each other holding (free, strictly better than plain hold), scheduled through T12. Sent c12 to Hatti with a goodwill message and no tablet, no gold, no mention of Ugarit; due back about T6. c11 due home about T5. Seha and apasa are empty: a Hatti army at Tuwanuwa could walk into Seha unopposed. Hatti pact k1 runs to T8; Alashiya warns Hatti means to take Lukka. At T5: if treasury allows, raise an army in apasa (100) so Lukka can be held against army plus fleet support, and consider a fleet at cilicia to support Ugarit walls. Check whether Ugarit was bought (if Hatti bid too, nobody got it: rebid). After T8 consider Tuwanuwa if Hatti is weak (harvest failed). Babylonia leads at 1.64, so I need to grow income fast.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu, capital apasa. Start strength 1300. T1: took Lukka by force, disbanded the seha fleet. T2: sealed k1 with Hatti (no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8); Hatti army sits at tuwanuwa, Hatti fleet moved to cilicia, Hatti asked me to keep away from Tuwanuwa/Kizzuwatna. Hatti has taken Isuwa and told Alashiya it will take Carchemish and Lukka. Hatti harvest failed (T3). T4: sealed k17 with Alashiya (brothers; no army or fleet against each other's lands or bought cities; Lukka mine; I may buy Ugarit; Alashiya may buy Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus; envoys pass freely). Egypt fleet convoyed an army delta->tamassos (Alashiya) at T2 and lingers at greatgreen: a danger. Income 125, upkeep 60 (armies at mira and lukka), wages about 20. Scheduled buy of Ugarit (400) at T4. Standings T4: Babylonia 1.64, Alashiya 1.35, Arzawa 1.25, Assyria 1.22, Hatti 1.17, Egypt 1.11, Mitanni 1.03. Envoys: c11 Haamashshi (returning from Alashiya, about T5, back pay 11, serves to T13), c12 Mazipalali (interpreter, serves to T7, sent to Hatti T4). A foreign unit can attack Cyprus only from greatgreen (Egypt fleet there), cilicia (Hatti fleet there) or the other Cyprus province, so only a joint Egypt+Hatti attack could dislodge me. Walled bought cities fall to a move with one support (strength 2). Later, with a second army and fleet, I could take Qadesh or Damascus from Babylon, or urge others to. Keep costs low: units 65/season, wages 21/season.

value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700 (yield 135). T1 took Terqa from Mitanni and bought Susa for 350. value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start strength 2600. T1-T3: bought Mari, Qadesh, Damascus; took Susa by force from Assyria (T2, against the spirit of k6); sealed k6 (Assyria) and k7 (Mitanni) at T2. Assyria took Terqa from Mitanni and is hostile. I cannot attack Ekallatum (only 2 hostable provinces touch it, max strength 2) or Arbela (only Susa touches it, strength 1) unless Assyria leaves them empty or thin. An empty province falls to strength 1. Growth: gold counts 1:1 in strength, so net income (about +200/turn) is the engine; a bought city is strength-neutral and pays 10 percent a season; an army costs 100 plus 30 a season, so avoid idle armies. Free cities left: amurru 200, megiddo 200, tyre 250, ugarit 400 (Ugarit contested by Hatti, Mitanni, Alashiya, Arzawa). Egypt owns Gaza. Alashiya holds Byblos and is the main rival for growth (small base, low upkeep). Envoy c17 was lost (hired by another court). c5 reaches Alashiya T5, c6 back from Mitanni T5. value.notes: T4 plan. Real strength is 2365 (0.95): gold spent on units counts for nothing, so only conquest and income raise it. Standings shown are LAND ONLY. Babylonia's bought walled cities (Damascus, Qadesh, Mari, Susa) cannot hold troops, and Babylonia cannot reach them by land, so they are cheap targets: one mover plus one support beats walls 1. T5 megiddo army -> tyre (F2 at levantsea supports), sinai army -> gaza, followers close up. T6 tyre army -> byblos (F2 supports; Alashiya's walled city, take it by force), sinai army -> tyre. Alashiya: sealed nothing, never will; keep them calm with warm words, Byblos will fall soon. c1 and c2 due home T5; then decide: dismiss or send one to Assyria urging an attack on Babylonia (Susa/Mari). value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600, now 2365 (0.95). Standings are land yield only, not real strength. Envoy c1 Mane to Hatti and c2 Ashur-nadin (Assyrian-born, may defect) to Mitanni, both due back T5; c17 to Babylonia with a peace and sphere tablet (Egypt: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru; Babylonia: Mari, Qadesh, north), back about T7. NEW PLAN (land route): T4 kanesh->isuwa, hattusa->kanesh (prep, looks normal to Mitanni), kizzuwatna supports tuwanuwa hold (covers Arzawa mira+lukka 2v2 bounce this season).
