I SEALED it, no gold paid. Keliya (c3) returns about T5 with the older homeland-only tablet. PLAN (private): I may strike Carchemish at T5 and break this; Mitanni is weak and Assyria wants it so. Do not tell Assyria of k13.

value.text: Greetings, my lord king of Karduniash, from Tehip-tilla, a son of Arrapha. I have travelled the roads as a trader in copper, and I know the caravan routes and the men who keep them. I am faithful, I am willing to learn whatever my lord requires, and I ask only for the chance to serve you well and to be noticed by the king.

I am Ehli-Teshub, born in Carchemish, who for many seasons led my own caravans along the roads from the Euphrates to the western passes, and I know the waystations, the tolls and the men who keep them. I keep my accounts true to the last shekel, I hold my tongue where silence serves my lord, and I have never broken faith with one who dealt justly with me. If the king of Karduniash has need of an envoy or an agent to carry his word, I humbly offer my service and ask that my worth be weighed fairly.

To my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, from your servant Zitanza. I came before Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, and gave him your words as you spoke them: that Terqa is Assyria's, that neither house sends troops against the other's homeland, that Carchemish is yours and under your protection, and that Babylon, which has taken Susa, Mari and Qadesh, is a danger to both our houses. The king sealed your tablet gladly and sent his greeting. He keeps his armies from Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish, and asks that our houses warn each other before moving against a third land. Artessupa, his envoy, is at your court with his own word. I bring home the sealed tablet as it stands. At Ashur the treasury looks thin, which I thought my lord would wish to know.

To my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, from your servant Mane. I came to the court of Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, and gave him your words as you spoke them. He has sealed your tablet, which I now bear: no troops against each other's homelands, Hatti sends none into the southern cities you name, and the envoys shall pass between your courts. In return he asks that Egypt send no troops or fleets to Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit or Lukka, and make no bid for them, for he says the north is Hatti's road. I gave him no promise concerning those lands, telling him I am only a messenger with no power to answer for my lord there. At his court I saw Hatti keeping four bodies of army and one fleet near its capital, and Yanhamu, envoy of Assyria, was also present. The northern matter my lord must weigh for himself.

To my lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, from Artessupa your servant. I have come home from the court of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, who prays that all may go well with you and your house. He has received your word and your tablet and has sealed it; I carry the sealed tablet home to you. Terqa is written as Assyrian, and Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and Carchemish are his; neither of you shall move an army against the other's lands. He asks that you not enter Carchemish or Isuwa, and he will not touch Terqa. Any word of ending this peace shall come first by envoy, as he asks. He wishes news of Hatti and of the armies on the northern roads, and I have promised to carry that request to you. I noticed that Mitanni keeps 3 army and no fleet near its capital. Burna-Buriash of Karduniash sealed a peace with you and in the same season seized Susa; Assyria and Mitanni should not feed his wind by fighting each other.

To my lord Tushratta, King of Mitanni, from your servant Ubaru: I came before the Great King Suppiluliuma of Hatti and gave him your word as you spoke it, that six seasons of peace stand between our houses, with no troops against each other's homeland, none against Carchemish or Isuwa, and Ugarit left to Hatti while the peace stands. He heard your warning about Babylon and said it is noted. He read your tablet and has sealed it, and I carry that sealed tablet home to you. He also grants that envoys and messengers of both houses pass freely and are not held. May all go well with my lord, his household, sons, chariots, horses and country.

My lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, I came to the court of Great King Tushratta of Mitanni and gave him your greetings and your words: the peace you ask him to seal, the cities of the south that lie in Egypt's sphere, and the armies of Hatti at Hattusa and Kanesh, close to Isuwa and Carchemish. He has sealed your tablet, so peace stands between your houses with no troops in each other's homeland. He says he watches Isuwa, which Hatti has now taken, and Carchemish, which he holds under his protection, and he charges Assyria with seizing his city Terqa in the midst of his peace offers. He asks that a brother send good gold, not light or gilded wood, by this road, and that you send your envoy again with your word on how you stand toward Hatti and Assyria. I told him I have no authority to promise any gold, and that you alone will judge what you send and by what road. I noticed that Mitanni keeps three companies of the army and no fleet near its capital, and that its treasury looks thin.

To Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, my lord, from your servant Yanhamu: may Shamash and Ashur keep you, your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. I came to the court of Hatti and gave your words as you spoke them. The king of Hatti heard them with pleasure and answers that Hatti will stand with Assyria against Mitanni: neither of you makes peace with Mitanni without first telling the other, Hatti keeps the west, Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran, and Assyria keeps the east, Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. He says Isuwa is already his. He asks that neither army cross the other's border in peace between your homelands; I could not bind you to that word, and I lay it before you now. He asks for a show of your strength on the Mitanni border and will show you his own, and he will send an envoy with a tablet to seal when the time is right, so no tablet is yet sealed. The court of Hatti lives comfortably. May Shamash witness it.

My lord Burna-Buriash, I have come home from the court of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and I bring you his word. He wishes all well with you, your household and your land, he holds your tablet, and he welcomes your word against Assyria. Within your mandate I have agreed for you that Karduniash and Mitanni make war together upon Assyria, that Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to him and Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa go to you, that neither of you makes peace with Ashur-uballit without the other, that the roads stay open, and that the old tablet stands. Nothing is sealed. He asks that you move first at Ekallatum and send him word of the season you strike, so that the blows land together, and he will strike at Terqa when its garrison is drawn off. I had no mandate to name a season or bind your armies, and I did not. He warns that Hatti has taken Isuwa and gathers armies on his border, and he calls a Hatti grown fat a danger to you both. Your word is awaited, my lord.

My lord, Great King of Alashiya, I have returned in safety from the court of Egypt and give you my report. The king of Egypt heard your words and called the movement of ships in the Great Green the haste of captains at sea, not a quarrel with you; he holds you a brother and wishes your house well. He gave no sealed word today, saying his envoy will carry Egypt's answer when the season allows, and he bids you bring copper, saying gifts will be spoken of when it comes. I pressed him that his envoy come swiftly with the sealed answer, and I told him that copper will follow as you have spoken. I noticed that Egypt keeps three bands of army and one fleet near its capital, and that its court lives in comfort. I await your word, my lord.

My lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, I, Haamashshi, have come home from the court of Alashiya and report as follows. Its king sends you greeting, wishes well to his household, sons, chariots and ships, and thanks you for your frankness. The tablet of brothers is sealed before Teshub and Shamash: Alashiya will not bid for Ugarit, and Arzawa will not bid for Amurru, Tyre and Gaza, which he will take for his ships. I gave him your warning of the Egyptian fleet that convoyed an army from the Delta toward Tamassos, and he says Hatti's fleet now lies in the Cilician Sea next to his capital, though Hatti swore brotherhood with him. He asks a gift of gold from you to show our peace is real; I carried no gold and had no word from you, so I promised nothing and await your answer. I have seen no Hatti ships or armies on my road that I can swear to, and my own wages of eleven shekels for this season are still owed me.

My lord, I went to the court of Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, and gave him your words as you bade me. He received me gladly, thanked you for the warning about Suppiluliuma, and sealed the tablet as written: Arzawa holds Lukka and Alashiya will not bid for it; Arzawa may buy Ugarit and Alashiya will not bid against him there; Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus remain for Alashiya and Arzawa will not bid for them; neither king sends army or fleet against the other's lands or bought cities, and envoys pass freely. I carry the sealed tablet home to you. The king asks one thing more: that if Hatti marches on Lukka, your ships in the Cilician Sea stand by Lukka and Ugarit. I told him I am only a messenger and cannot pledge your fleet, but that I would set his request before you with all respect. He also bids you note that the Egyptian fleet at the Great Green and the army at Tamassos are a danger to you both, and he will share every report of them; I have promised to share what news of Hatti reaches us. May your household, sons, chariots and horses prosper.

My lord Suppiluliuma, I went to Great King Tushratta and gave him your word as you spoke it through my mouth. He has read your words through me and sealed the tablet, so six seasons of peace stand between Hatti and Mitanni: no army of Mitanni shall enter Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, none of Hatti shall enter Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa, and open roads stand for our envoys between the two courts. He says Carchemish is his by purchase, that it stands under his hand, and that he will hold it as his own country. On Isuwa, which you took with your own hand, he says he will not make it a quarrel between you while the peace stands, and he made no promise on the free cities or on Assyria. The sealed tablet is in my keeping and I bring it to you. At Mitanni I saw 3 army and no fleet kept near the capital, and the treasury looks thin; Kidin-Adad, envoy of Babylonia, was also at that court. I ask, my lord, that the wages you owe me be paid, for I have served you faithfully on this road.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, my lord Tarhundaradu greets his brother and asks after your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. He keeps the peace of our sealed tablet and sends no army into your homeland, and he grieves that travellers speak of a failed harvest; may Teshub restore your fields. He holds Lukka, taken from free men, and means only to keep it. Egypt's fleet roams the Great Green and Egypt's army stands in Alashiya's land, a danger to every coast, so he asks what Hatti wants from his brother in the west and what you intend in the east, where Carchemish and the free cities lie. I am bidden to hear any proposal you make and carry it home, and I may promise this much: Arzawa will not bid for any city of Hatti.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I am Tattamaru, servant of Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, and I bring you his words as he bade me. Thus says my lord: may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. We are neighbours now in the cities of the Levant: you hold Byblos, I hold Mari and Qadesh, and this season I bid for Damascus. When two kings bid for one city its elders sell to neither and both lose a season of its yield, so let us not bid against each other. I would take Damascus, Megiddo, Gaza and Tyre, and you would take Amurru. Send your answer by your envoy, and let copper and good gold pass between our houses.

Great King of Karduniash, my brother, thus my lord Napkhururiya sends word: health to your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Egypt seeks lasting brotherhood and peace with Babylonia. Egypt marches only on the free cities of the south coast, from Gaza to Damascus, and on the sea lands, and has no quarrel with Babylonia's holdings at Mari and Qadesh, nor will it send any army against them. Here is the tablet for the king's seal: neither shall send army or fleet against the other's lands, and each shall hear the other before treating with a third king against him. My lord offers an exchange of envoys between our courts. He asks what the king wishes of Egypt, and what word the king has heard from Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria.

Tattamaru, servant of my brother Burna-Buriash, be welcome. May all go well with your lord, his household, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Tell him that Alashiya also wishes to avoid a season lost to two bids for one city. But the cities he names are not all free for the dividing: I have already given my word to other kings over Amurru, Tyre and Gaza, and I mean to take them myself when my treasury allows. Let my brother take Damascus and Megiddo, which lie near his Mari and Qadesh, and leave Amurru, Tyre and Gaza to me. If he bids for Tyre or Gaza I will bid as well, and both of us will lose the season, which serves neither house. Let him also send his answer in a sealed tablet, that both kings may hold it, and say that neither will send army or fleet against the other's lands or cities, Byblos included. As for copper and good gold, they pass best between brothers who first agree on the cities. When his answer comes, copper will be spoken of. May Marduk and Shamash keep your road safe.

Mazipalali, tell Tarhundaradu, my brother, that Suppiluliuma greets him and wishes well to his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. The harvest was thin, but Hatti stands and Teshub is not angry with us. I keep the sealed peace between our homelands and I expect my brother to keep it as well; I will not move against Mira, Apasa or Seha. I thank him for his word that Arzawa will not bid for any city of Hatti. Lukka I do not concede: it is a free city and a road to my coast, and I ask only that his army there stay quiet and not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. In the east I want open roads for my envoys and peace for the lands I hold; I do not tell a brother my every plan, nor do I ask his. If he wishes to propose anything more, let him send you or another envoy with a tablet already written, and I will read it. Carry my good wishes home.

Sin-iqisham, carry this to Napkhururiya, my brother, king of Egypt: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash wishes health to your lord's house, his wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I want peace and brotherhood with Egypt, and I will gladly hear Egypt before treating with any third king against him; let that stand between us. But I cannot seal this tablet. It names Damascus in Egypt's sphere, and Damascus is mine, bought with my own gold and held by me; it also gives away Byblos and Amurru, which are not mine to give. Your own words left Damascus out when you spoke of my holdings, yet the tablet says otherwise. Write it so: neither sends army or fleet against the other's lands, and Babylonia's lands are Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa and its homeland. Egypt's sphere is Gaza and Megiddo, which Egypt holds, and the sea lands. Tyre I would buy with gold, as I bought my other cities, and I would not bid in the lands Egypt holds. Seal that, and my seal follows at once. As to Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria: I hear what all hear, that Hatti took Isuwa. I have sealed nothing against Egypt with any king, and I will not. I will send my own envoy to your court.

Great King Suppiluliuma, I hear your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord Tarhundaradu: your greeting, your keeping of the sealed peace, and your word that Mira, Apasa and Seha are not to be moved against. I will tell him that you hold Lukka not as a conquest but as a free city and a road to your coast, and that you ask his army to keep quiet and not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. The word of Arzawa stands: it will not bid for any city of Hatti. Should you send an envoy with a tablet already written, I will bring it to my lord with all speed. May Teshub restore your fields and your household prosper.
value.commitments: Arzawa will not bid for any city of Hatti.

value.speech: Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I have heard your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord Burna-Buriash. Let it stand that neither of us bids against the other in the Levant, and that Amurru is yours to take. My lord has bidden me keep Damascus, Megiddo and Gaza for him, and I have no word to give Gaza away; but if you insist upon Tyre, I may tell my lord that you hold it. I carry no seal and can set no sealed word, so my lord will answer as he sees fit. Of copper, gold, armies and fleets I have no authority to speak. May Marduk and Shamash keep your road safe.
value.commitments: Agreed in words only, subject to my lord's answer: neither Babylon nor Alashiya bids against the other in the Levant; Amurru to Alashiya; Tyre may be reported to my lord as yours if you insist. Nothing sealed, no gold promised, no land ceded, nothing said of armies or fleets or of Ugarit.

value.speech: Great King of Karduniash, my brother, I have heard your word and will carry it faithfully to my lord. I am empowered to seal the tablet of peace and spheres, and I will write it so: neither shall send army or fleet against the other's lands; Babylonia's lands are Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa and its homeland; Egypt's sphere is Gaza, Megiddo and the sea lands; and the tablet shall not name Byblos or Amurru. I set Egypt's seal to it here, that your seal may follow as you have said, and my lord's envoy shall come to your court. As to Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria, I will report that the king of Karduniash has sealed nothing against Egypt with any king, and that Hatti took Isuwa.
value.commitments: Egypt will hear Babylonia before treating with any third king against Babylonia; an exchange of envoys between the two courts; neither king sends army or fleet against the other's lands; the peace and spheres tablet sealed for Egypt in these terms (Babylonia: Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa and its homeland; Egypt: Gaza, Megiddo and the sea lands; Byblos and Amurru not named). No gold, troops, marriage or cession of land promised.

value.speech: Sin-iqisham, you said the tablet would name Damascus mine and leave out Byblos and Amurru. The clay you hand me names Damascus, Tyre, Byblos and Amurru in Egypt's sphere, and gives me only Mari, Qadesh and the north and east. That is not what you promised before me. Either your scribe erred or your tongue did, and I will not set my seal to words that differ from your spoken ones. Tell Napkhururiya, my brother: I hold Damascus, bought with my gold, and I will not bid in Gaza or Megiddo. Let him send a tablet written as you spoke, naming Damascus among Babylonia's lands, with no Byblos or Amurru, and my seal follows at once. Until then our peace stands in word: I send no army against Egypt, and I expect none against Mari, Qadesh, Damascus or Susa. My envoy will follow to your court.

Great King of Karduniash, my brother, I hear your word, and I beg the king's pardon: I believe my scribe has erred in the writing, for I spoke as the king has now said. I will carry your word to my lord exactly as you have spoken it: Damascus among Babylonia's lands, no Byblos or Amurru, and Egypt's sphere of Gaza, Megiddo and the sea lands. I will bring back a tablet written so, under Egypt's seal, and I pray the king's seal will follow at once. I will report that the king has sealed nothing against Egypt with any king, and that he will send his envoy to Egypt's court.
value.commitments: I promised that Egypt will send back a tablet of peace and spheres rewritten to name Damascus among Babylonia's lands and not Byblos or Amurru, under Egypt's seal, for the king's seal; that the two courts will exchange envoys; and that Egypt will hear Babylonia before treating with any third king against it. No gold, troops, marriage or cession of land was promised.

value.speech: Great King Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, my lord Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother, greets you and wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. He seeks lasting peace with Karduniash, and he says that Mari, Qadesh and Susa are yours, and that Hatti sends no troops into them. In turn he asks that Babylonia send no army or fleet against what Hatti holds, and make no bid for Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit or Lukka, which lie on Hatti's road. I humbly pray that you seal the tablet he sends, and let our envoys pass freely.

Pirissi, carry this to Suppiluliuma, my brother, Great King of Hatti: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash wishes health to your lord's house, his wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I want peace and brotherhood with Hatti, and I seal your clay as it is written. Neither of us sends army or fleet against the homeland of the other, nor against any province the other holds this day, nor bids for it. That binds Hatti as it binds me: Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa and all my homeland are held by me today, and I will hold your lord to the clay. Your envoys will always pass freely through my land, and mine through yours. I make no word beyond the tablet about cities that neither of us holds. Let our envoys keep the roads warm.

Great King Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, I receive the clay you have sealed and thank you for your brotherhood. I will carry it to my lord Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, together with your words as they were spoken, and I will tell him that you hold his clay. May the roads between our lands stay warm, and may the envoys of Hatti pass freely through your country as you have said.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf, by my mandate: Hatti sends no troops into Mari, Qadesh or Susa. By the sealed clay, neither Hatti nor Karduniash sends army or fleet against the other's homeland or against the provinces the other holds this day, and neither bids for them; envoys pass freely both ways. No gold given, nothing promised against Egypt, Assyria or Mitanni, and no alliance made.

orders.letter: Brother of Alashiya, Suppiluliuma greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our sealed peace stands and Hatti keeps it: no army or fleet of mine against your lands or cities you have bought. This year drought struck my fields and my treasury is thin, while your copper and your ships prosper. A brother who holds the sea and a brother who holds the land road both gain when the other stands firm. I ask you to send me, with this envoy, a gift of gold as one brother to another, as much as you can spare in respect of the friendship between our houses, and I will remember it. Tell me also what you hear of Egypt's fleet and of Arzawa's ships in the Cilician Sea. I seek no quarrel with you.
orders.mandate: Receive any gold or gift Alashiya sends and bring it home. May repeat the peace of the sealed tablet by word. Promise no troops, no gold and no cities. Say nothing of Ugarit, Carchemish or Lukka beyond what the sealed tablet says. Do not reveal my plans.

value.notes: T5: Treasury 0. Drought income is 106 (halved, rounded up per province) against upkeep 120 for 4 armies. STRIKE CARCHEMISH now: kanesh -> carchemish, isuwa and kizzuwatna support (3 vs walls 1 + harran support 1 = 2). This breaks k13 (Mitanni peace sealed T4) but not k20 (homelands only). If it succeeds, T6 income is about 124 vs upkeep 120, so I stay solvent; T7 the drought ends and income is about 245. If it bounces, T6 income 106 < 120 and one army deserts: at T6 disband the least useful army myself first. Risks: harran + washukanni could hit isuwa 2 vs 1 (my isuwa army is supporting, so it holds at 1); Arzawa lukka + mira could hit tuwanuwa 2 vs 1 since kizzuwatna no longer supports it (k5 runs to about T7-T8). Hattusa and kanesh are empty after this move. c3 Keliya goes to Alashiya (1 season) to ask for a gold gift; his wage then builds as back pay instead of draining cash. Back at T7. T6 (I wake): if Carchemish is mine, next target is Ugarit (Arzawa bought it, walls hold 1): kizzuwatna -> ugarit, carchemish army supports, 2 vs 1. Then rebuild kanesh cover and a fleet once gold returns. Do not tell Assyria about k13. Keep Assyria pact open: Mitanni squeezed between us.
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100 (yield 180, 300 gold). T1 raised armies; T2 took Isuwa by force, sealed k4 Alashiya and k5 Arzawa (homelands, to about T7-T8); T3 sealed k9 Egypt (I send no troops into Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh); Assyria offered a pact against Mitanni (Hatti: Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran; Assyria: Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni), agreed by word only. T4 sealed k13 Mitanni (six seasons, no troops against homelands, Carchemish, Isuwa; Mitanni will not bid for Ugarit); Keliya brought back k20 (homelands only). DROUGHT T4-T6 halves income (106 vs upkeep 120); isuwa army and cilicia fleet deserted at T4. T5: Arzawa envoy said Arzawa will not bid for any city of Hatti and keeps Lukka; I did not concede Lukka. T5 orders: strike Carchemish (kanesh moves, isuwa and kizzuwatna support), tuwanuwa holds, Keliya to Alashiya for a gold gift. World T5: Arzawa 1.65 (holds Lukka with army, Ugarit by purchase), Babylonia 1.64 (nine provinces incl Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa), Alashiya 1.35, Assyria 1.22, Egypt 1.21, Hatti 1.17, Mitanni 1.03 (three armies, thin treasury). Pirissi c4 returns from Babylonia about T7. Next targets: Ugarit by land (kizzuwatna army with carchemish support), then a fleet and Lukka. Cash is the limit: 30 per army, 35 per fleet.

ledger.entry: T5: Keliya brought k20 (homelands only, sealed). k13 (T4) also stands on paper: no troops against Carchemish. T5 I struck Carchemish anyway, breaking k13. Expect protest. Mitanni is weak (3 armies, thin treasury). Do not tell Assyria of k13.
T5: k4 stands (brothers, no attack on each other's lands or bought cities). Sent Keliya (c3) with words only, no tablet, asking a gold gift for the drought. Arrives T6, back T7. Nothing paid by me.

orders.letter: Brother of my house, Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets you and wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, ships and country. Ugarit has accepted my gold and is mine; Lukka stands under my army. I thank you for your frankness and send gold as a token that our peace is real. One request between brothers: Hatti's army stands at Kizzuwatna and its fleet in the Cilician Sea, beside Ugarit, whose walls hold with strength 1. A ship of yours in the Syrian Sea, supporting Ugarit's walls to hold, would save it. I will warn you at once of any Egyptian or Hatti move I learn against Tamassos or Enkomi, and I will not bid for your cities. Tell me what you see of Egypt's fleet and of Hatti, and answer by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet as written, may promise warnings both ways and that I do not bid for Alashiya's cities. May not promise further gold, armies or ships. Report what Alashiya answers about the ship at Syrian Sea.

proposal.text: Alashiya and Arzawa, brothers before Teshub and Shamash: while Hatti's army and fleet threaten Ugarit, Alashiya will keep a ship in the Syrian Sea to support the walls of Ugarit holding. Arzawa will not bid for Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza or Damascus, and will warn Alashiya of any Egyptian or Hatti move against Tamassos or Enkomi. Each warns the other of moves against the other's lands. Envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T5: Ugarit bought (mine, walls). Treasury 94, cannot raise army (100) yet. Sent c11 to Alashiya with 25 gold (their asked token) and a tablet: Alashiya keeps a ship in Syrian Sea supporting Ugarit walls; I do not bid for Amurru/Tyre/Gaza/Byblos/Damascus and warn of Egypt/Hatti moves. Reason: Hatti army at kizzuwatna + fleet at cilicia could take Ugarit (army 1 + fleet support 1 beats walls 1). Lukka holds at 2 (mira support); Hatti tuwanuwa+kizzuwatna+cilicia fleet could make 3 and take it: real risk, nothing I can do this season. T6 plan: raise army in apasa (100; scheduled) so Lukka holds at 3; c12 returns T6 from Hatti, hear his report, send him to Hatti with a tablet asking no army/fleet against Lukka and Ugarit. After T8 (pact k1 ends) consider taking Tuwanuwa: needs 3 armies (mover + 2 supports from mira/seha/lukka) vs hold 2. Upkeep matters: 3 armies = 90. Seha, apasa empty; Egypt fleet at greatgreen can convoy to lukka only.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu, capital apasa. Start strength 1300. Now T5: holdings apasa, seha, mira, lukka (army), ugarit (bought T4, 400, walls). Yield 165. Income 165, upkeep 60 (armies mira, lukka), wages about 20. Treasury 94 at T5. Pacts: k1 Hatti (no army into the other's HOMELAND, turns 2-8; Tuwanuwa/Kizzuwatna are Hatti homeland, Lukka/Ugarit are not covered). k17/k24 Alashiya: brothers, no army/fleet vs each other's lands or bought cities; Lukka mine; Ugarit mine; Alashiya takes Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus; I will not bid for them. Threats: Hatti (army tuwanuwa and kizzuwatna, fleet cilicia) told Alashiya it means to take Lukka, Carchemish, Isuwa; could also take Ugarit (walls strength 1). Egypt fleet at greatgreen, convoyed an army to tamassos at T2. Envoys: c11 Haamashshi (serves to T13, wage 11) sent to Alashiya T5; c12 Mazipalali (interpreter, serves to T7, wage 9) returns from Hatti about T6. Plans: T6 raise army in apasa (supports lukka), keep saving, after T8 consider Tuwanuwa with 3 armies, keep Alashiya friendly, ask Alashiya for a ship at Syrian Sea for Ugarit. Standings T5 by yield: Arzawa 1.65, Babylonia 1.64, Alashiya 1.35, Assyria 1.22, Egypt 1.21, Hatti 1.17, Mitanni 1.03. Real growth (with gold) mine 1.33.

ledger.entry: T4 sealed k17 and k24 (brothers; Lukka and Ugarit mine; Alashiya takes Byblos/Amurru/Tyre/Gaza/Damascus; no army or fleet vs each other). T5 c11 returned: Alashiya asks a gift of gold; Hatti's fleet lies in the Cilician Sea next to Enkomi. T5 sent c11 back with 25 gold and a tablet asking a ship in the Syrian Sea to support Ugarit's walls, and warnings both ways.

T2 sealed k1 (no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8). T4 sent c12 with goodwill, no tablet, no gold; he returns about T6. Hatti army at tuwanuwa and kizzuwatna, fleet at cilicia. Alashiya says Hatti means to take Lukka. Lukka and Ugarit are NOT covered by k1. A tablet is not enforced; watch it.

orders.letter: Ubaru of Sippar speaks for Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, to Burna-Buriash, his brother. All goes well with me. I hold to our word: Karduniash and Mitanni make war together on Assyria, and neither makes peace with Ashur-uballit apart from the other. Nineveh stands unguarded and my army takes it this season; Terqa and Ashur follow as we agreed. Strike Ekallatum and Arbela now, so that Assyria cannot spare armies for Nineveh and Terqa, and send word by your envoy of the season you strike. Seal the tablet I send. Watch Hatti, who keeps armies on my border.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet as written and agree that Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to Mitanni and Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash, and that neither king makes peace with Assyria without the other. May ask for the season of Babylon's strike. May not promise gold or any troop movement beyond what the tablet says.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, make war together on Assyria and make no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from each other. Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa go to Karduniash. The roads stay open, and the earlier tablet stands: Isuwa and Carchemish are Mitanni's, Mari is Karduniash's.

orders.letter: Zitanza of Lukka speaks for Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother. All goes well with me, and our tablet of peace stands. My brother, gold in your land is as common as dust: send me a gift of good, pure gold, as your father sent to my father, so that I may keep my chariots and armies ready. Hatti has taken Isuwa and keeps armies on my border, and a Hatti grown fat will look south to your cities next. Assyria has broken faith with me and with Babylon. Send me word of Hatti and of your armies in the north, and send your envoy to my court.
orders.mandate: May seal a tablet of brotherhood in which each king sends word if a third king moves on the other's homeland, and in which Egypt sends gold to Mitanni. May promise to share news of Hatti. May not promise troops or gold from me.

proposal.text: Egypt and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace and open roads. If a third king moves an army against the homeland of one of them, the other sends word at once. Egypt sends gold to Mitanni in token of brotherhood, as it did to Mitanni's father.

value.notes: T5: Nineveh (yield 35) is EMPTY (Assyria's army went nineveh->arbela in T3, only terqa and arbela armies known). I break k15/k22 (sealed T4) and walk taidu->nineveh. Assyria broke faith first (Terqa, T1). Also raise a new army in taidu (100) if taidu is empty after movement (if the move bounces nothing is raised). T6 PLAN: wake T6, order the new taidu army to SUPPORT nineveh holding (hold 2), harran keeps supporting carchemish, washukanni supports harran. Assyria can only reach strength 2 on nineveh (arbela move + ashur support) so a supported hold bounces them. Assyria cannot reach strength 2 on washukanni/harran (only terqa touches them), so the old taidu support chain is not needed. Do NOT attack Terqa until Babylon draws off its supporters (T2 attack bounced 2v2) and not while harran is needed to guard Carchemish: Hatti has armies at isuwa, kanesh, kizzuwatna (3 vs my 2 on Carchemish if they break k21; k12/k21 run T4-T9/T10). Envoys: c7 to Babylon with joint-war tablet (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon), urge strike on Ekallatum/Arbela. c8 to Egypt asking for gold and a brotherhood tablet. Ubaru is Sippar-born: possible Babylon sympathy, watch his report. Babylon is leader 1.64: later turn on it, or at least do not feed it. Treasury after levy about 75, income next turn about 185 vs upkeep 120 and wages 16.
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni, start 1950, strength 1675 at T5 (growth 0.86). Holdings: harran, washukanni (capital), taidu, carchemish (bought T1 for 350, walls; I cannot station troops in it). Assyria took Terqa T1; my T2 attack on it bounced 2v2 (it has a supporter at ashur/ekallatum). Sealed treaties: k3 Babylon (Isuwa/Carchemish mine, Mari his), k10 Egypt (peace; Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh in Egypt's sphere), k12 and k21 Hatti (six seasons from T4: no armies against each other's homelands, Carchemish mine, Isuwa Hatti's, I will not bid for Ugarit), k15 and k22 Assyria (peace, Terqa Assyria's). Babylon verbally agreed to a joint war on Assyria (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon); I told Babylon neither of us makes a separate peace, yet I sealed with Assyria: do not let Babylon learn. Hatti took Isuwa and has armies at isuwa, kanesh, kizzuwatna next to Carchemish; harvest failed there. Map lessons: only harran and washukanni touch Terqa/Isuwa; defenders with a support hold 2. Buying a free city costs 10 x yield and needs adjacency (none free next to me now). Nothing free borders my land. Gold: income 150, upkeep 30 per army, wages 16. Standings T5: Arzawa 1.65, Babylonia 1.64, Alashiya 1.35, Assyria 1.22, Egypt 1.21, Hatti 1.17, me 1.03. T5 decision: seize empty Nineveh with taidu army, raise a new army at taidu, support nineveh from T6.

ledger.entry: T5: Sent Ubaru (c7) with joint-war tablet: Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Karduniash; no separate peace; k3 stands. Told them I take Nineveh now and urged a strike on Ekallatum and Arbela. I secretly sealed k15/k22 with Assyria in T4 (do not let Babylon learn). No gold sent. Babylon is the leader: watch it.

T5: I BREAK k15/k22 (sealed T4) by taking empty Nineveh with the taidu army; no notice sent by envoy (Assyria broke faith first in T1 at Terqa). Expect a counter at Nineveh (arbela+ashur) and anger; I hold Nineveh at 2 with a taidu army. Assyria's treasury is thin.

T5: Sent Zitanza (c8) to Egypt (2 seasons each way) asking for good gold and a brotherhood tablet (warn each other of any third king moving on either; Egypt sends gold). k10 still stands: no Mitanni troops in Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash to Tushratta, my brother. I have heard Kidin-Adad's report and I agree: Karduniash and Mitanni make war on Assyria together; Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to you, Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to me; neither of us makes peace with Ashur-uballit without the other; the roads stay open and the old tablet stands. I do not wait: this very season my armies strike Ekallatum and Arbela. Strike Terqa in the same season and in each season after, so its garrison cannot support Ekallatum, and keep Ashur busy. Send me word by your envoy of the season in which your armies strike, and what you see of Hatti on your border. I have heard your warning about Hatti and I watch.
orders.mandate: You may confirm the partition (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylonia), no separate peace, open roads, k7 stands, and you may ask Tushratta to name the season his armies strike Terqa. You may not promise gold, cede land, bind my armies to a named season, or seal any tablet.

Struck Assyria at once: Sippar->Ekallatum supported by Dk (2); Susa->Arbela only to CUT Arbela's support of Ekallatum (T4 pattern: terqa holds, arbela supports ekallatum, ekallatum supports terqa, so Ekallatum hold should be 1 after the cut; an unseen Ashur army could make it 2 and bounce us, costing nothing). Mari loses Sippar's support this season but Ekallatum's support for any Terqa->Mari is cut by my attack, so Mari should hold 1 v 1. Hired c15 Tehip-tilla at 16 so I have an envoy at T6 for Egypt (promised my own envoy; ask for corrected tablet: Damascus mine, no Byblos/Amurru). c6 sent to Mitanni: agree partition, I strike now, ask them to strike Terqa. value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start strength 2600, growth 1.37 at T5 estimate 1.64 (Arzawa 1.65 rival, Alashiya 1.35). History: bought Mari, Qadesh, Damascus; took Susa by force from Assyria (T2, against k6 spirit); Megiddo bid T4 failed (Egypt took it). Tablets: k6 Assyria (broken in spirit), k7 Mitanni (peace, Isuwa/Carchemish not mine to bid, Mari mine), k26 Hatti sealed T5 (neither sends army/fleet against other's homeland or provinces held that day, no bids; Hatti promised no troops into Mari, Qadesh, Susa). Egypt: envoy Sin-iqisham says spoken peace, promised a corrected tablet naming Damascus mine, no Byblos/Amurru; I did not seal the bad clay; Egypt took Megiddo and will likely go for Tyre then Damascus. Mitanni (Tushratta) agreed in speech to a joint war on Assyria (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to him; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to me, no separate peace) but wants me to move first. Geometry: bought/free walled cities cannot hold troops; only Ekallatum touches Sippar and Dk; Susa touched only by Arbela; empty-after-movement rule lets me raise a new army where an army just left. Growth engine is net income ~+180/turn plus bought cities (10 percent per turn). Free cities left: Amurru 200, Tyre 250. Alashiya holds Byblos, Arzawa holds Ugarit, Lukka. c5 returns from Alashiya T7.

ledger.entry: T5: k6 openly broken by me: Sippar+Dk strike Ekallatum, Susa strikes Arbela to cut its support. Assyria T4 pattern: terqa holds, arbela supports ekallatum, ekallatum supports terqa. Hostile since Terqa. Expect counterattack on Ekallatum/Mari; keep Sippar and Dk manned.

T5: c6 back with Tushratta's word (joint war, partition Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh him; Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa me; no separate peace; he wants me to move first). Nothing sealed. T5: c6 sent again, spoken only: I agree, I strike this season, he must strike Terqa and name his season. He may let me bleed; judge by whether Terqa is attacked.

T3: c5 sent (arrives T5), spoken only: neither bids against the other in the Levant; they take Amurru, I take Megiddo/Tyre. Megiddo lost to Egypt. T5: I bid Tyre 250. Amurru: I may bid if they do not. c5 back about T7 with their answer.

orders.letter: Brother Suppiluliuma, Napkhururiya greets you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and land. Egypt keeps the tablet you sealed: no troops against each other's homelands, and the southern cities of Egypt's sphere left to Egypt. Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. Egypt will bring the coastal cities of its sphere under its hand, as the tablet says, and asks that Hatti's armies keep to the north of them. Egypt would not hinder Hatti against Lukka, which Arzawa holds. Let our envoys pass freely between our houses.
orders.mandate: May say only that Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. May not speak of Ugarit, give or promise gold, or seal anything new. Bring Hatti's answer home.

orders.letter: Brother Ashur-uballit, Napkhururiya greets you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and land. Egypt keeps the friendship we sealed. Hear what Egypt sees: Babylonia has bought Mari, Susa, Qadesh and Damascus, walled cities that cannot hold a single soldier, and one army with one supporter takes each. Egypt will take Damascus and Qadesh from the south, for they lie in Egypt's sphere. Mari and Susa lie by Assyria's hand. Babylonia grows fat on bought cities while its borders stand open. Let our envoys keep passing.
orders.mandate: No gold, no new tablet beyond the friendship already sealed. May hear Assyria's answer and bring it home. May not promise Egypt's troops anywhere.

value.notes: T5 plan. Real growth = strength/start; standings are land only and rivals spent gold on cities, so conquest is my only path. Conquered provinces stay mine without a garrison (gaza proves it). Scheduled T5 runs: megiddo->tyre (levantsea fleet supports), sinai->gaza, delta->sinai. I OVERRIDE memphis: hold (E1 stays) so delta is empty after movement and I can raise fleet F3 there (120). T6 schedule kept: tyre-army->byblos (F2 supports), gaza-army->tyre, sinai-army->gaza, memphis-army->sinai. T7: tyre army -> damascus with byblos army supporting. T8: damascus army -> qadesh, byblos army supports. Then amurru (F at syriansea supports), ugarit, mari. FLEET PLAN vs Alashiya (needs 3 fleets): T6 F1 greatgreen->cilicia (check no Hatti fleet), F3 delta->greatgreen; T7 F2 levantsea->syriansea, F3 greatgreen->levantsea; T8 F3 levantsea->enkomi, F1 (cilicia) and F2 (syriansea) support: 3 v 2; T9 F1 cilicia->tamassos, F3 at enkomi supports (2 v 1). Adapt to what I see. Letters: Mane (c1) to Hatti: no troops to Isuwa/Carchemish/Lukka, nothing on Ugarit, no gold, no new tablet. Ashur-nadin (c2) to Assyria: urge Assyria to take Mari/Susa from Babylonia; no gold. Watch c2 may defect. c17 back about T7 from Babylonia. Keep 150+ gold, wake every turn.
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600; T5 strength 2562 (1.02). Standings shown are land only; real growth is lower for rivals who spent gold on cities. Conquest is my path: provinces stay mine without garrison. Holdings: akhetaten, delta, gaza, megiddo, memphis, sinai, thebes (yield 230). Units T5: armies megiddo, sinai, delta, memphis; fleets greatgreen, levantsea; raising a third fleet at delta T5 to take Enkomi and Tamassos from Alashiya (needs 3 fleets: two supports on the attacker). Coastal chain: tyre T5, byblos T6, damascus T7, qadesh T8, then amurru, ugarit, mari. Babylonia bought Damascus, Qadesh, Mari, Susa (walls, cannot hold troops, Babylonia cannot reach them). Treaties: k11 Assyria (T4 peace, receive envoys, join no enemy), k18 Hatti (T3 peace, spheres: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh), k19 Mitanni (same). Hatti asked Egypt to keep out of Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka and make no bid; I promised nothing (want Ugarit). Mitanni (weak, thin treasury) wants good gold and an envoy; nothing sent. Alashiya (Paser) keeps asking for peace tablet and gold: NEVER seal, I take Byblos, Tamassos, Enkomi. Babylonia: c17 carried peace and sphere tablet (offered Mari/Qadesh north to Babylonia), back about T7; I will take Damascus and Qadesh regardless. People: c1 Mane (13, term to T11), c2 Ashur-nadin (14, to T8, Assyrian-born, may defect), c17 (16, to T8, owed 32). Free candidates c15 (20), c18 (24). Keep 150+ gold, wake every turn. Disband armies when no targets remain (30 upkeep each).

ledger.entry: T3: k18 sealed (peace, no troops in homelands, southern cities in Egypt's sphere). T5: Mane back. Hatti asks Egypt to keep out of Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka. I promised nothing on Ugarit. T5: sent Mane again: no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish, Lukka; no gold, no new tablet.
T3: k19 sealed (peace, spheres). T5: Ashur-nadin back. Mitanni asks for good gold and an envoy with my word on Hatti and Assyria. Nothing sent or promised. Mitanni is weak (thin treasury).
T4: k11 sealed (friendship, receive envoys, join no enemy). Gold promised later, none sent. T5: sent Ashur-nadin with warm words urging Assyria to take Mari and Susa from Babylonia; no gold.

orders.letter: Brother, Great King of Egypt, may all go well with your house, your sons, your chariots and your horses. Paser has told me your words and I thank you. Yet your ships came twice against Tamassos and now lie in the Levantine Sea at my capital's door; the haste of captains does not move me, a sealed tablet does. I send you a tablet of peace: neither of us sends army or fleet against the other's lands or bought cities, Byblos among mine. I will not bid for Gaza, Megiddo or Tyre; leave Amurru to me. When it is sealed, copper will go to Egypt from my mines, and let Egypt's gold of gifts come to Alashiya, as gifts passed between our fathers. A brother with ships at my door asks for copper before a seal; seal, and send your gift with your envoy.
orders.mandate: Paser may seal the tablet as written, promise copper to Egypt in return for a gift of gold, and say that Alashiya will not bid for Gaza, Megiddo or Tyre. He may not cede land, give units, or promise armies or fleets.

proposal.text: Egypt and Alashiya are brothers before Amun, Shamash and Teshub: there is peace between them. Neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought; Cyprus and Byblos are Alashiya's, Gaza and Megiddo are Egypt's. Alashiya will not bid for Gaza, Megiddo or Tyre; Egypt will not bid for Amurru. Alashiya will send copper to Egypt and Egypt will send a gift of gold to Alashiya. Their envoys pass freely.

orders.letter: Brother Tarhundaradu, may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. I hold the sealed tablet and thank you. About Hatti: I cannot pledge my only fleet, for Egypt's ships lie in the Levantine Sea at the door of Enkomi and in the Great Green by Tamassos, and if I leave Cyprus open it falls. But I will send word the moment Hatti's ships enter the Cilician Sea, and I ask you to share every report of Egypt and Hatti. One thing more between brothers: my fleet and army cost me 65 shekels each season to guard the sea road that also covers Ugarit, and Amurru and Tyre, which you will not bid for, wait on my treasury. A gift of 100 shekels would let me buy Amurru this year and hold the Levant coast as your friend.
orders.mandate: Ili-iddina may promise to share news and to warn of Hatti's ships, and may receive gold. He may not pledge my fleet or army, seal anything, or cede land.

value.notes: T5: Treasury 95. Real growth is 1.04 (the standings list is land-only). Strength = 10*yield + gold, so a bought city costs 10x yield and earns 10 percent a season; buy ASAP, hold no idle gold. Net income about 29 a season (115 - 65 upkeep - 21 wages). Free cities left: Amurru 20 (200), Tyre 25 (250). Gaza and Megiddo are Egypt's; Damascus, Qadesh, Mari Babylon's; Ugarit Arzawa's. Babylon (Tattamaru) agreed in words that Amurru is mine; sent nothing sealed. Egypt fleets at levantsea (next to Enkomi) and greatgreen. Mutual hold-support holds against 2 hostile fleets; 3 could crack me (cut supports). Byblos can only be hit by fleets (bought walled cities cannot hold troops). Sent Paser to Egypt with a peace tablet (cost 20): Byblos and Cyprus safe, I do not bid Gaza/Megiddo/Tyre, Egypt does not bid Amurru, copper for a gold gift. Copper is only flavour (no engine cost): ask for gold gifts. Sent Ili-iddina to Arzawa: no fleet pledge, will warn about Hatti, asked 100 gold gift. Scheduled hold-supports T7-T30 and a buy of Amurru at T10 (expected treasury ~220). Woken T7 when c14 returns. Then: read Egypt and Arzawa answers; if gold arrives buy Amurru earlier; consider Tyre later. Do not concede Tyre to Babylon (leader); Egypt may have it for gold.
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). T2: sealed k8 with Hatti (no army/fleet vs each other's lands or bought cities; Hatti may buy Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; I may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Byblos, Qadesh). Hatti fleet later went kizzuwatna->cilicia then left sight. Egypt tried to land at Tamassos in T2 and T3 and bounced off my fleet. T4: sealed k16 and k25 with Arzawa (peace; Arzawa holds Lukka and may buy Ugarit; I may buy Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus; Arzawa will not bid for those; envoys pass freely). Arzawa asked me to stand by Lukka and Ugarit if Hatti marches; I have not pledged. T5: Egypt answered only with warm words (no tablet, no gold) and wants copper; its fleets sit at levantsea and greatgreen. Babylon is the land leader (Damascus, Mari, Qadesh, Susa) and its envoy Tattamaru agreed in words that Amurru is mine, nothing sealed. I hold byblos (walled), enkomi (fleet), tamassos (army), defended by mutual hold-support. Strength is 10*yield + gold - back pay, my real growth about 1.04; a bought city pays 10 percent a season, so buy Amurru (200) then Tyre (250) as soon as gold allows. Net income ~29 a season. Envoys c13 (8 a season, term to T13) and c14 (13 a season, term to T9; renew or lose him).

ledger.entry: T5: Paser back. Egypt calls its fleet moves the haste of captains, holds me a brother, gave no tablet or gold, bids me bring copper. Fleets now at levantsea (next to Enkomi) and greatgreen. Sent Paser again with a peace tablet to seal (Byblos and Cyprus safe; I do not bid for Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre; Egypt leaves Amurru; copper for a gold gift). Nothing paid either way. Distrust.

T5: Ili-iddina brought k25 (sealed T4). Arzawa asks my fleet to stand by Lukka and Ugarit if Hatti marches; I did not pledge, said I will warn. Sent Ili-iddina again (T5) asking a 100 gold gift to buy Amurru. No gold paid either way. Arzawa a true friend so far.

orders.letter: Yanhamu, say to my brother the Great King of Hatti: Ashur-uballit greets you; may Shamash and Teshub keep your house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. I accept your word: Hatti keeps the west (Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran), Assyria the east (Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni). Know this: Tushratta sealed a peace with me over Terqa before your word reached me. It is a shield to quiet my border while we make ready, and it ends the day we strike. I will send no army into Hatti's homeland or Isuwa. The show of strength you ask: on turn 10 my army from Terqa moves on Washukanni and my army from Nineveh moves on Taidu, which cuts Taidu's support of Washukanni. If your army in Isuwa supports my move into Washukanni that same turn, Washukanni falls and its army is destroyed. Then I support your move from Isuwa into Harran with my armies at Terqa and Washukanni. Seal the tablet. If turn 10 does not suit you, name another turn by this envoy and I will keep it. Tell Yanhamu where your armies stand and whether Isuwa holds one.
orders.mandate: Yanhamu may seal the tablet as written. He may agree any strike turn from 10 to 13 that Hatti names. He may promise that Assyria sends no army into Hatti's homeland or Isuwa. He may promise nothing else: no gold, no cession of land, no gift of troops. He must learn where Hatti's armies stand and how many, and come home at once.

proposal.text: Assyria and Hatti, Great Kings and brothers, stand together against Mitanni. Washukanni and Taidu fall to Assyria; Harran, Carchemish and Isuwa to Hatti. Neither makes peace with Mitanni without first sending word to the other. Neither sends an army into the homeland of the other. On the turn the two kings fix by envoy, Hatti's army in Isuwa supports Assyria's army from Terqa into Washukanni, and Assyria's armies at Terqa and Washukanni then support Hatti's army from Isuwa into Harran.

value.notes: T5: PLAN HAMMER, kill Mitanni with Hatti. Sent c10 (Yanhamu) to Hatti (arrives T7, home T9) with a tablet (scribe 20) and strike date T10: Nineveh army -> Taidu (cuts Taidu's support of Washukanni; Taidu itself is unsupported, hold 1), Terqa -> Washukanni with Hatti's Isuwa army supporting (2 v hold 1). Mitanni formation seen T4: washukanni supports harran, taidu supports washukanni, harran supports carchemish. At T9 (woken by c10 or wake_in_turn 9): read Hatti's answer. If yes: move ashur -> nineveh at T9 (arrives end of T9), strike T10. If no or vague: hold, stay thrifty. Ashur leaving weakens Ekallatum (hold 1 + arbela = 2 v Babylon max 2; only Susa hitting Arbela plus Sippar/Durkurigalzu hitting Ekallatum beats it). After Washukanni falls: Harran next (Hatti Isuwa moves, my Terqa and Washukanni support), then Taidu (Nineveh + Washukanni, 2 v 1). I told Hatti honestly that the Mitanni peace (k14, k23) is a shield. Dismissed c9 to save wage 12. c16 back T6: read Egypt's answer, maybe ask Egypt for gold. Gold 39 minus 20 for tablet. Babylon is the runaway leader and broke k2: trust nothing.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700 (yield 135). T1 took Terqa from Mitanni and bought Susa for 350. T2 sealed k2 with Babylon; Babylon broke it at once and took Susa (lost 350). T3 raised a 4th army at Ashur. T4 sealed k14 and k23 with Mitanni (Terqa is Assyria's; no army against each other's provinces; I stay out of Isuwa and Carchemish; word by envoy before ending the peace). Map: I touch only Mitanni (terqa to harran/washukanni, nineveh to taidu) and Babylon (ekallatum to sippar/durkurigalzu/mari, arbela to susa). Ties bounce, so alone I cannot attack: only one or two of my units touch any target. Babylon leads (land 320; Susa, Mari, Qadesh, Damascus; Sippar army supports Mari). Formation T4-T12: terqa holds; ekallatum supports terqa; arbela and ashur support ekallatum; nineveh empty on purpose (retake with ashur + arbela support, 2 v 1). Hatti (via Yanhamu T5) agreed to stand with me against Mitanni: Hatti west (Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran), Assyria east (Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni); no tablet yet. T5: sent Yanhamu back with tablet and plan to strike on turn 10 (Nineveh -> Taidu cuts its support; Terqa -> Washukanni with Hatti's Isuwa support). c9 dismissed T5. c16 (Egypt friendship tablet) due back T6. c13 Ili-iddina is secretly in my pay in Babylon. Net income about +45 with no envoys at court; each envoy wage 11-14.

ledger.entry: T5: Yanhamu returned: Hatti will stand with me against Mitanni (Hatti west: Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran; Assyria east: Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni); Hatti wants a show of strength and no army across the other's homeland border. Nothing sealed. T5: sent Yanhamu back (arrives T7, home T9) with a tablet and the strike plan for turn 10 (Hatti's Isuwa army supports my Terqa army into Washukanni). I admitted my Mitanni peace is only a shield. No gold sent.

T4: sealed k14 and k23 (Terqa Assyrian; no army against each other's provinces; I stay out of Isuwa and Carchemish; word by envoy before ending the peace). A shield only: strike planned T10 with Hatti if Hatti agrees. Seen: washukanni supports harran, taidu supports washukanni, harran supports carchemish; Taidu itself unsupported. Nothing paid.

value.text: My lord Tarhundaradu, I have returned from the court of Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti. He greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. He keeps the sealed peace, and says he will not move against Mira, Apasa or Seha. He holds Lukka as a free city and a road to his coast, and asks that your army there keep quiet and not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. In the east he wants open roads for his envoys and peace for the lands he holds; he does not tell his plans and does not ask yours. Should you wish to propose anything more, he asks that you send an envoy with a tablet already written, and he will read it. I gave your word, as you bade me, that Arzawa will not bid for any city of Hatti, and he thanked you for it. The rains have failed in Hatti and the harvest withers across the land, though the king says Hatti stands. May Teshub restore your fields and may your household prosper.

My lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria: I went to the court of Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, and gave him your word as it was written. He answered that Egypt takes your friendship gladly, will receive your envoys and will join no enemy of yours, and that it looks to its southern coast and its own borders. Of the north he said that Hatti's armies stand near Isuwa and Carchemish and that a wise brother watches them; he said nothing of Mitanni or Babylon, and I have reported that silence as well. The tablet is sealed by both kings, and Egypt's gold will follow when envoys have crossed and friendship is proven. At his capital I noticed three companies of army and one fleet, and I bring the sealed tablet home to you.

value.speech: Great King Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, my brother, thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother: all goes well with him, and may all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Through my mouth, Ubaru of Sippar, he speaks his word: Karduniash and Mitanni make war together on Assyria, and neither makes peace with Ashur-uballit apart from the other. Nineveh stands unguarded and my lord's army takes it this season, with Terqa and Ashur to follow as agreed; strike Ekallatum and Arbela now, so that Assyria cannot spare armies for Nineveh and Terqa. Seal the tablet I bring, watch Hatti, who keeps armies on my lord's border, and, Great King, send word by your envoy of the season you strike.

Great King Tarhundaradu, my brother, my lord of Alashiya sends you greeting and asks that all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. He holds the sealed tablet you sent and thanks you for it. Concerning Hatti, he cannot pledge his only fleet, for Egypt's ships lie in the Levantine Sea at the door of Enkomi and in the Great Green by Tamassos, and if he leaves Cyprus open it falls; but he will send word the moment Hatti's ships enter the Cilician Sea, and he asks that you share with him every report of Egypt and Hatti. Between brothers he asks you to consider this: his fleet and army cost him 65 shekels each season to guard the sea road that also covers Ugarit, and Amurru and Tyre, which you will not bid for, wait on his treasury, and a gift of 100 shekels would let him buy Amurru this year and hold the Levant coast as your friend. I am but a humble messenger, and I beg the Great King's pardon for carrying such a request.

Hear me, Tushratta, Great King, as my lord Burna-Buriash bids me say to his brother. My lord has heard the report of Kidin-Adad and agrees with it: Karduniash and Mitanni make war on Assyria together, Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to you, Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa go to him, neither of you makes peace with Ashur-uballit without the other, the roads stay open, and the old tablet stands. He does not wait: this very season his armies strike Ekallatum and Arbela. He asks that you strike Terqa in the same season and in each season after, so that its garrison cannot support Ekallatum, and keep Ashur busy, and that you name to him the season your armies strike Terqa. He asks, too, for word by your envoy of what you see of Hatti upon your border, for he has heard your warning about Hatti and he watches.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King, king of Hatti, your brother: he greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. The sealed peace stands and Hatti keeps it; no army or fleet of his shall move against your lands or the cities you have bought. Drought has struck his fields and his treasury is thin, while your copper and ships prosper, and he asks you, as one brother to another, to send with me such gold as you can spare in respect of the friendship between your houses, which he will remember. He also asks what you hear of Egypt's fleet and of Arzawa's ships in the Cilician Sea, and bids me say he seeks no quarrel with you.

Great King, my brother, my lord the Great King of Alashiya wishes all well with your house, your sons, your chariots and your horses, and he thanks you for the words his envoy Paser has carried. Yet your ships came twice against Tamassos and now lie in the Levantine Sea at his capital's door; the haste of captains does not move him, but a sealed tablet does. He offers you this tablet of peace: neither of you shall send army or fleet against the other's lands or bought cities, Byblos among his. Alashiya will not bid for Gaza, Megiddo or Tyre, and asks that Amurru be left to him. When the tablet is sealed, copper will go to Egypt from his mines, and he asks that Egypt's gold of gifts come to Alashiya as gifts passed between your fathers. You would have copper before a seal, but my lord says: seal, and send your gift with your envoy.

To Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. The sealed peace stands and Alashiya keeps it. I grieve at the drought in your fields. My own chest is thin: I have bought walled cities and pay for fleets and armies, so I send no gold now; when my copper is sold and my cities pay, I will remember my brother. Of Egypt I tell you only what all may see: its army took Tyre last season, and its fleets lie in the Great Green and the Levantine Sea. Of Arzawa's ships I have seen nothing. I ask one thing in return: keep your fleet out of the Cilician Sea beside my capital, as the peace requires, and I will keep mine from your coasts.

Brother of Alashiya, may all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. I hold our sealed tablets and I keep them: no army or fleet of mine will touch your lands, and I will not bid for Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Byblos or Damascus. Your word that you will send notice the moment Hatti's ships enter the Cilician Sea is welcome, and I will send you what I learn of Hatti and Egypt. As for gold, my brother, my treasury is thin this season: my armies eat and my new levies cost me dearly, so I cannot send 100 shekels. A king who buys a city with his own gold keeps it better. When your ship stands in the Syrian Sea beside Ugarit, and I see that my friend guards the coast that covers us both, I will remember your need. Hold Cyprus, brother, and keep faith.

Paser, my brother of Alashiya is dear to me, and I wish all well to his house, his sons, his chariots and his ships. My captains in the Levantine Sea act on the orders of the sea and the winds as much as on mine; they hold no quarrel with Cyprus. I will not put my seal to a tablet while the copper has not yet crossed to my land; let my brother's copper come first, as you yourself say it may, and my scribes will then weigh the tablet and the gift together. Go in peace and carry my greetings home.

Ubaru of Sippar, my countryman, carry this to Tushratta, my brother: Karduniash seals the tablet. We make war together on Ashur-uballit and neither makes peace apart. Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash. I have already struck Ekallatum and Arbela and I strike again, with Susa, Sippar and Dur-Kurigalzu. My brother, take Nineveh now, and strike Terqa the same season, for Terqa and Ekallatum hold each other up; when Terqa falls, Ekallatum falls. Send word at once, by you or another, which season your army moves and what it has taken. I have given my word in blood and clay; let my brother's army show his. As for Hatti, I keep my eyes on the road.

Say to Burna-Buriash, my brother: Tushratta greets him and his household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. I have heard Kidin-Adad. The war stands as spoken: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni, Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash, no peace with Ashur-uballit by either alone, roads open, the old tablet standing. Nineveh is already mine and my army holds it. I name the season of Terqa: my armies strike Terqa in turn 7, and I press it in the seasons after, so that its garrison cannot stand behind Ekallatum. Let my brother's armies strike Ekallatum and Arbela this season as he says, and so draw Ashur's men away. As for Hatti: his army took Carchemish from the free city last season and now stands on my border at Harran, with more at Isuwa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna. Hatti has harvest failure but keeps soldiers. Watch Hatti as I do. My treasury is thin from the levies for this war; a brother who wants Terqa pressed may send gold with his next envoy to keep my armies fed.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I have heard your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord Suppiluliuma without change. The sealed peace stands and Hatti keeps it, as your tablet says, and I will tell my lord that you grieve at his drought and that your chest is thin for now. Your request concerning the Cilician Sea I will also bear to him.

Great King Tarhundaradu, my brother, I hear your words and thank you for them, and I will carry them to my lord of Alashiya exactly as you have spoken them. My lord keeps faith with you: I will keep watch for Hatti's ships on the Cilician Sea, and you shall have word of them the moment they are seen. I beg the Great King's pardon for the burden of my request, and I am glad that his favour stands with Alashiya.
value.commitments: Word to Arzawa the moment Hatti's ships enter the Cilician Sea, and news of Hatti and Egypt shared between the two courts. No fleet, army, seal or land pledged.

value.speech: Great King Burna-Buriash, my brother, I take your sealed tablet and agree it as written: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh go to Mitanni, Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash, and neither king makes peace with Ashur-uballit apart from the other. I will carry your word to my lord Tushratta with all haste. I ask, Great King, in which season your army will strike, so that my lord may know when to move. May Shamash, whom I served as a priest in Sippar, keep your household and your country safe.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf I agree the tablet as sealed: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash; neither king makes peace with Ashur-uballit apart from the other. No gold and no troop movement beyond what the tablet says. I myself will carry the king's word back to Tushratta.

value.speech: Great King, my brother, I hear your words and will carry them home to my lord exactly as you have spoken them. Copper before the seal is more than my lord has bidden me give, and I cannot pledge it; he says seal, and the copper follows. Yet I see that your scribes wait only upon the copper, and I will tell my lord so, that the tablet and your gift may come together to your court. May your house prosper and your chariots remain strong, and may the gold of gifts pass between our courts as it passed between our fathers.
value.commitments: Alashiya will not bid for Gaza, Megiddo or Tyre, and once the tablet is sealed copper will go to Egypt from his mines in return for a gift of gold.

value.speech: Tushratta, Great King, I have heard you and will carry your word to my lord Burna-Buriash as you spoke it: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to you; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to him; no peace with Ashur-uballit by either of us alone; the roads kept open; the old tablet standing. You name turn 7 for the striking of Terqa, and I will set that before my lord, but I have no power to bind his armies to any season. Your word on Hatti, at Harran and at Isuwa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna, I will also carry, and my lord watches Hatti as you do. Of gold I can promise nothing; what my lord's treasury sends with his next envoy is for him to decide.
value.commitments: Confirmed on my lord's behalf, within my mandate: the partition (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Karduniash), no separate peace with Ashur-uballit, open roads, and the old tablet stands. Nothing promised of gold, land, a season for his armies, or any tablet.

value.speech: Great King of Alashiya, my brother, thus says Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, brother of my house: he greets you and wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, ships and country. Ugarit has accepted his gold and is now his, and Lukka stands under his army; he thanks you for your frankness and sends gold as a token that our peace is real, to be weighed against the sealed inventory. One request between brothers: Hatti's army stands at Kizzuwatna and its fleet in the Cilician Sea beside Ugarit, whose walls hold with strength 1, and a ship of yours in the Syrian Sea supporting those walls would save it. He will warn you at once of any Egyptian or Hatti move he learns against Tamassos or Enkomi, and he will not bid for your cities; tell him what you see of Egypt's fleet and of Hatti, and answer by this envoy. I also bring a tablet for you to seal before Teshub and Shamash.

To Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, sons, chariots, ships and country. I weighed your gold against the inventory and it was true; I take it as a token that our peace is real. What I see: Egypt's fleets stand at the Levantine Sea beside Enkomi and in the Great Green, and last season Egypt took the walls of Tyre with an army from Megiddo, helped by its fleet. Hatti's envoy came to me with warm words, pleaded drought and a thin treasury, and asked what I hear of your ships; I told him only public things. About the new tablet, brother: I have one fleet, and it must stand in Enkomi, because two Egyptian fleets are next to my capital and my ship and my army guard each other. I cannot seal a promise to send that ship away. Send me the tablet again without the ship clause, with your warning of any move against Tamassos or Enkomi and your word to leave Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus, and I will seal it at once. Once the Egyptian fleets leave the Levantine Sea I will send a ship to the Syrian Sea. I shall warn you of any Hatti move I learn. I still mean to buy Amurru, which you have promised not to bid for; a gift of gold toward it would be remembered.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I have heard your answer and will carry it to Tarhundaradu, my lord, as you speak it. I cannot seal a tablet with the ship clause struck out, and I may promise no ship, army or gold, Amurru's gold included; that my lord alone may decide. You say a ship will go to the Syrian Sea once Egypt's fleets leave the Levantine Sea, and that word I will report to him. On my lord's behalf I promise that he will warn you at once of any Egyptian or Hatti move he learns against Tamassos or Enkomi, and that he will not bid for your cities, Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus; I thank you for your warning of any Hatti move you learn.
value.commitments: Arzawa will warn Alashiya at once of any Egyptian or Hatti move learned against Tamassos or Enkomi. Arzawa will not bid for Alashiya's cities (Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus, as the king names them). Alashiya to warn Arzawa of Hatti moves. No ship, army or gold promised. The ship clause is not agreed; the king's request for a tablet without it is referred to Tarhundaradu.

value.notes: T6: Treasury 4, nobody at court (c3, c4 away, back about T7), so no letters, no hires. Carchemish is mine (walls fell). Hold the line one season: carchemish supports isuwa hold (harran+washukanni could hit isuwa 2 v 1; with support 2 v 2 bounces; carchemish itself faces at most 1 attacker from harran so it holds), kizzuwatna supports tuwanuwa hold (lukka+mira 2 v 2 bounce; k5 with Arzawa runs to about T8). Hattusa, kanesh, sapinuwa are empty. T7 PLAN (I wake): drought over, income about 245 vs upkeep 120; c3/c4 return and I pay back pay 57, so about 70-130 gold left. Raise an army in KANESH (100) so it can support isuwa. Read what c3 brings from Alashiya (gold gift?). T8 PLAN: Ugarit (Arzawa, walls 1, yield 40): kizzuwatna -> ugarit, carchemish supports (2 v 1); kanesh army supports isuwa; accept Arzawa anger, k5 ends about T8. Later: fleet at kizzuwatna for Lukka, more armies in hattusa/sapinuwa as gold allows. Mitanni is the weak one (1.03) but k20 bars Harran until about T10. Do not tell Assyria about k13. Keep upkeep covered: below 30 gold means desertion risk.
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100 (yield 180, 300 gold). T1 raised armies; T2 took Isuwa, sealed k4 Alashiya (brothers; I may buy Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; Alashiya Ugarit, Amurru, Byblos, Qadesh) and k5 Arzawa (no army into the other's homeland, runs to about T8). T3 sealed k9 Egypt (I send no troops into Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh); Assyria offered a pact against Mitanni (Hatti: Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran; Assyria: Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni), agreed by word only, nothing sealed. T4 sealed k13 Mitanni (no troops against homelands or Carchemish), k20 (homelands only, to about T10). DROUGHT T4-T6 halved income; isuwa army and cilicia fleet deserted at T4. T5 I took Carchemish by force (kanesh moved, isuwa and kizzuwatna supported), breaking k13. Now 7 provinces, yield 245, 4 armies (carchemish, isuwa, kizzuwatna, tuwanuwa); hattusa, kanesh, sapinuwa empty. World T6: Arzawa 1.65 (apasa, seha, mira, lukka with army, Ugarit by purchase), Babylonia 1.64 (nine provinces), Hatti 1.36, Alashiya 1.35, Egypt 1.34, Mitanni 1.03 (harran, washukanni armies, thin treasury), Assyria 0.96 (took Terqa). Envoys c3 Keliya (to Alashiya, asked a gold gift) and c4 Pirissi (Babylonia) return about T7. Plan: T7 raise army in kanesh; T8 take Ugarit (kizzuwatna moves, carchemish supports); then fleet and Lukka; keep isuwa and tuwanuwa guarded. Gold counts one for one in strength, so bank surplus and keep upkeep covered.

ledger.entry: T5: struck Carchemish, breaking k13 (no troops against Carchemish). k20 (homelands only, sealed T4) stands to about T10. Expect hostility: harran and washukanni could hit Isuwa 2 v 1, so carchemish supports isuwa. Mitanni is weak (about 1.03). Do not tell Assyria of k13.

value.notes: T6 plan. Orders: tyre army -> byblos (levantsea fleet supports, 2 v walls 1); gaza -> tyre; sinai -> gaza; memphis -> sinai; greatgreen fleet F1 -> cilicia; delta fleet F3 -> greatgreen. Alashiya cannot raise new units (both homeland provinces occupied), so the fleet plan is safe: T7 F2 levantsea -> syriansea, F3 greatgreen -> levantsea, F1 holds cilicia; T8 F3 -> enkomi with F1 and F2 supporting (3 v hold 2); T9 F1 cilicia -> tamassos with F3 at enkomi supporting (2 v 1). Land: T7 army at tyre -> damascus, army at byblos supports; T8 damascus army -> qadesh, byblos army supports; T9 byblos army -> amurru (qadesh army supports); T10 ugarit (Hatti wants it, decide then); later mari. Risk this turn: Alashiya fleet from enkomi could attack levantsea and cut F2's support (then byblos bounces, retry T7). Alashiya's offer: never seal. Keep 150+ gold; wake every turn. c17 due back T7 (owed 48), c1 and c2 due T9. Terms of c2 and c17 end T8: renew only if still useful. Support targets in schedules: name actual positions at the time; I am awake each turn so give explicit orders.
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600; T6 strength 2679 (1.07), treasury 204. Standings shown are land only; rivals who bought cities spent gold. Conquest is my path: conquered cities lose walls and stay mine without garrison. Holdings T6: akhetaten, delta, gaza, megiddo, memphis, sinai, thebes, tyre (yield 255). Units: armies tyre, gaza, sinai, memphis; fleets greatgreen, levantsea, delta. Upkeep 225 vs income 255. Coastal chain: byblos T6, damascus T7, qadesh T8, amurru T9, ugarit T10, mari later. Babylonia's bought walled cities (damascus, qadesh, mari, susa) cannot hold troops and Babylonia cannot reach them. Fleet plan vs Alashiya (three fleets, Alashiya cannot raise units): T8 enkomi, T9 tamassos. Treaties: k11 Assyria (T4 friendship, receive envoys, join no enemy), k18 Hatti (T3 peace; sphere: Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh), k19 Mitanni (same). Hatti asked Egypt to keep out of Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka; I promised no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish, Lukka only. Mitanni wants gold, nothing sent. Alashiya (envoy Paser) keeps asking for a peace tablet with Byblos theirs and Egypt not bidding Amurru: NEVER seal, I take Byblos, Enkomi, Tamassos. People: c1 Mane (13, term to T11, due T9), c2 Ashur-nadin (14, term to T8, Assyrian-born, may defect), c17 (16, term to T8, due T7). Free candidate c18 Ehli-Teshub asks 24. Keep 150+ gold, wake every turn, disband spare armies once targets run out (30 upkeep each).

ledger.entry: T6: Paser brought a peace tablet (no army/fleet vs each other's lands or bought cities; Byblos and Cyprus Alashiya's; Egypt not to bid Amurru; copper for a gold gift). I did NOT seal, sent no gold, said copper first. T6 I attack Byblos; fleets then go for Enkomi (T8) and Tamassos (T9). Never seal. Keep warm words.

value.notes: T6: Hatti took Carchemish T5 (kanesh->carchemish, isuwa+kizzuwatna support), breaking k21; walls fell, it is now plain Hatti land with a Hatti army, next to Harran. My old schedule (harran supports carchemish) would have backed a HATTI unit: replaced. Defence now: harran holds, washukanni supports harran (hold 2 vs Hatti max 2 from carchemish+isuwa), taidu supports nineveh (hold 2 vs Assyria max 2 from arbela+ashur), nineveh holds. Only a Hatti+Assyria joint attack (terqa supporting) could break harran. Max strength I can bring on Terqa is 2 (only harran and washukanni touch it) and moving either leaves harran/capital open to Hatti, so NO Terqa strike unless Babylon removes Terqa's supporters (ashur/ekallatum) or Babylon supports me. The T7 Terqa date I gave Babylon was nonbinding; decide T7 on news. Better lever: Babylonian units at arbela/ekallatum could support my nineveh->ashur. Wake triggers set on terqa, ekallatum, arbela, ashur changing hands, c7/c8 return, T7. Treasury 65, net about +14 a season; no spending. Plan T7: send c7 to Hatti (renew peace past T10, k12 ends T10) or Babylon with news. Keep watching Babylon (leader). Do not let Babylon learn of k15/k22.
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni, start 1950, strength 1549 at T6 (growth 0.79; Arzawa 1.65, Babylonia 1.64 lead).
