Hold harran, washukanni (capital), taidu, nineveh (taken T5 from Assyria; I broke k15/k22). Lost Carchemish to Hatti T5 (they broke k21). Four armies: harran, washukanni, taidu, nineveh; income 150, upkeep 120, wages 16. Sealed: k3 Babylon (Isuwa/Carchemish mine, Mari his), k10 Egypt (Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh in Egypt's sphere; no Mitanni troops there), k12 Hatti homelands no attack six seasons from T4 (ends about T10), k21 Hatti (broken by them), k15/k22 Assyria (broken by me). Babylon verbally agreed a joint war on Assyria: Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon; no separate peace; Babylon struck Ekallatum/Arbela T6; I told it nonbindingly I hit Terqa T7. Map: only harran and washukanni touch Terqa/Isuwa, so I can never exceed strength 2 there; defenders with a supporter hold 2. Defence geometry: harran needs washukanni support (Hatti carchemish+isuwa), nineveh needs taidu support (Assyria arbela+ashur). Envoys: c7 Ubaru back T7 from Babylon, c8 Zitanza in Egypt back T9 (asked gold and brotherhood tablet). c18 Ehli-Teshub free at court asks 22 (not hired). Hatti has armies at carchemish, isuwa, kizzuwatna; Assyria armies at terqa, arbela, ashur. Babylon is the leader: later turn on it or at least do not feed it. Aim: take Terqa/Ashur with Babylon's supports, save gold.

ledger.entry: T6: Hatti BROKE k21 by taking Carchemish T5 (army there now, next to Harran; armies at isuwa, kizzuwatna too). k12 (homelands, six seasons from T4, ends about T10) still stands on paper; harran holds 2 with washukanni's support. Envoy Keliya (c3) is Hatti's. Plan: send c7 to seek a longer peace before T10. No gold sent.

T6: Kidin-Adad repeated the joint war: Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon; no separate peace; Babylon strikes Ekallatum and Arbela T6. I named TURN 7 for Terqa (nonbinding; only if its supporters are drawn off). Told him Hatti took Carchemish and stands at Harran; asked for gold. k3 stands. I secretly sealed k15/k22 with Assyria and broke them taking Nineveh T5: never let Babylon learn. Babylon is the leader: watch it. No gold sent.

value.notes: T6: Both envoys (c13, c14) are on the road home, so no letters can go this season. Treasury 150 (includes 25 from Arzawa, weighed true, not assayed). Forecast: T7 about 158 after back pay 42; with envoys away again, cash grows about 50 a season (their wages build as back pay instead), so Amurru (200) is affordable around T9; buy is scheduled T10 as a fallback. NEW DANGER: Egypt holds Tyre with an army and has a fleet in levantsea; army tyre->byblos supported by that fleet is strength 2 vs the walls 1, so Byblos can fall any season. My fleet cannot reach it (enkomi is not next to byblos) and must hold Enkomi, so I accept the risk. If Byblos falls I wake; then think about retaking it or a deal with Egypt. At T7: read Paser's Egypt answer and Ili-iddina's Arzawa answer; send them out again (Egypt: peace tablet, Byblos safe; Arzawa: seal the tablet without the ship clause; keep warning them about Hatti). Re-plan the schedule at T7 (buy Amurru at T8/T9 if cash allows). Stay neutral between Hatti and Arzawa; do not send my fleet to the Syrian Sea while Egypt's fleets sit in levantsea and greatgreen.
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). T2: sealed k8 with Hatti (no army/fleet vs each other's lands or bought cities; Hatti may buy Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka; I may buy Ugarit, Amurru, Byblos, Qadesh). Egypt tried to land at Tamassos in T2 and T3 and bounced off my fleet. T4: sealed k16 and k25 with Arzawa (peace; Arzawa holds Lukka, may buy Ugarit; I may buy Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus; neither bids for the other's cities; envoys pass freely). T5: Egypt gave only warm words; Babylon's Tattamaru agreed in words that Amurru is mine, nothing sealed. T6: Egypt took Tyre (army from megiddo, fleet levantsea support). Arzawa bought Ugarit, holds Lukka, sent 25 gold and asked my fleet to guard Ugarit in the Syrian Sea against Hatti; I refused (fleet must hold Enkomi) and sealed nothing; Arzawa promised by word to warn me of Egypt/Hatti moves and not to bid for my cities. Hatti pleads drought and wants gold; I sent none. MAP: only Amurru is still a free city. Bought walled cities cannot hold troops and fall to a move with one support (2 v 1). Byblos is exposed to Egypt's army at Tyre plus fleet at levantsea; I cannot cover it. DEFENCE: fleet enkomi and army tamassos support each other holding (scheduled T6-T30). ECONOMY: income 115, upkeep 65, wages 21 (not paid in cash while envoys are away; back pay builds). A bought city returns 10 percent a season: buy Amurru (200) as soon as cash allows (T9ish; scheduled T10). Envoys c13 (8/season, term to T13) and c14 (13/season, term to T9: renew or lose him). Woken T7.

ledger.entry: T6: Egypt took Tyre (megiddo army, levantsea fleet support). Its army at Tyre plus fleet at levantsea can take walled Byblos (2 v 1); I cannot guard it. Paser sent T5 with a peace tablet (Byblos and Cyprus safe; I leave Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre; Egypt leaves Amurru; copper for gold gift). Answer due T7. Nothing sealed or paid either way. Distrust.

T6: Keliya said k8 peace stands, begged gold (drought), asked what I hear of Egypt's fleet and Arzawa's ships. I sent no gold; told him only public things (Egypt took Tyre); asked Hatti to keep its fleet out of cilicia. k8 sealed T2. No gold paid either way. Distrust, keep peace, stay out of Hatti-Arzawa quarrel.

T6: Haamashshi brought 25 gold (weighed true, purity unassayed) and a tablet asking my fleet to guard Ugarit in the Syrian Sea; I did NOT seal. Told him to resend without the ship clause. Arzawa promised by word: warn me of Egypt/Hatti moves against Tamassos/Enkomi, no bid for Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus. I owe warnings of Hatti moves. Refused gold for Amurru. k16 and k25 stand. Friend so far.

orders.letter: Tehip-tilla, carry this to Napkhururiya, my brother, Great King of Egypt: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash wishes health to your house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your envoy Sin-iqisham promised aloud that the clay would name Damascus mine, yet the tablet he brought gave it to your sphere. I do not quarrel over a scribe's slip. I send a plain tablet in its place, as brothers seal: neither of us sends army or fleet against the homeland of the other or against any province the other holds on the day of sealing, nor bids for it. Your Megiddo, Tyre and Gaza are yours; my Mari, Qadesh, Damascus and Susa are mine. Seal it and send it back by your envoy or mine. I send forty shekels of good gold as a brother's gift.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet as written, and may add a list naming Megiddo, Tyre, Gaza and Sinai as Egypt's and Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa as Karduniash's. May not promise gold, troops or any claim on Byblos, Ugarit or Amurru, and must say nothing of Assyria, Mitanni or Hatti.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Egypt, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace. Neither shall send army or fleet against the homeland of the other, nor against any province the other holds on the day this tablet is sealed, nor bid for it. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T6 plan. Sealed k28 with Mitanni (joint war on Assyria; Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa mine). Mitanni already holds Nineveh. Repeat strike: sippar->ekallatum (dk supports), susa->arbela (cuts Arbela's support). Assyria likely has 4 armies (ashur unseen, supports ekallatum: hold was 2). Ashur can support only ONE of ekallatum/terqa: if Mitanni hits Terqa with 2 the same season, either Terqa or Ekallatum falls. Raise army at Sippar runs only if Sippar army really left (then it guards Ekallatum: 3 vs 3). Bought Levant cities cannot hold my troops, so Damascus/Qadesh/Mari/Amurru are defended only by treaty. Egypt army sits in Tyre next to Damascus: sent c15 Tehip-tilla to Egypt (arrives T8) with a mirror of k26 (no armies against each other's homeland or provinces held on sealing day) plus 40 gold. Bid Amurru 200 (Alashiya/Arzawa may also bid: then none sold, no gold paid). T7: c5 (Alashiya answer) and c6 (Mitanni answer) return; read them, then decide next envoys (Mitanni: name the strike season; Hatti: keep k26 warm). Judge Mitanni by whether Terqa actually falls. Keep Sippar and Dk manned; fallback schedule T7-T12 is sippar supports mari.
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start 2600, growth 1.43-1.64 (Arzawa 1.65 is the rival). Land: homeland five, plus Susa (taken T2, army there), bought walled Mari, Qadesh, Damascus (walled cities cannot hold my troops; defended by treaty only). Tablets: k6 Assyria (broken by me), k7 Mitanni (peace; Isuwa/Carchemish not mine; Mari mine), k26 Hatti sealed T5 (no army/fleet or bid against homeland or provinces held that day), k28 Mitanni sealed T6 (joint war on Assyria, no separate peace; Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh Mitanni, Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa me). Egypt: Sin-iqisham's clay put Damascus/Tyre/Byblos/Amurru in Egypt's sphere; I refused to seal; Egypt took Megiddo T4 and Tyre T5 (army in Tyre next to Damascus); c15 sent T6 with a mirror of k26. Assyria passive and mutually supporting (terqa holds, arbela and ashur support ekallatum). T5 strike bounced 2v2 and 1v1. Free city left: Amurru 200 (I bid T6). Growth engine: net income about +170/turn plus bought cities; conquests add 10x yield. Geometry: only Ekallatum touches Sippar and Dk; only Arbela touches Susa; empty-after-movement lets me raise an army where one just left.

ledger.entry: T6: c15 Tehip-tilla sent (arrives T8) with a mirror of k26 for sealing: no army or fleet against each other's homeland or provinces held on the sealing day, no bids; plus 40 gold. Egypt's army sits in Tyre next to my Damascus. T5 clay from Sin-iqisham (Damascus/Byblos/Amurru in Egypt's sphere) NOT sealed. Spoken peace only. Told them nothing of the Mitanni war.

T6: k28 sealed (joint war on Assyria, no separate peace; Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh Mitanni, Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa me). Mitanni holds Nineveh already. I strike Ekallatum/Arbela again T6 and want Terqa hit the same season. c6 returns T7 with their answer. Judge them by whether Terqa falls. Told them nothing of Hatti k26.

T3: c5 sent, spoken only: neither bids against the other in the Levant; they take Amurru, I Megiddo/Tyre (both lost to Egypt). T6: I bid Amurru 200 anyway (if they bid too, none sold, no gold lost). c5 returns about T7 with their answer.

orders.letter: Brother Napkhururiya, may Amun keep you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our tablet is sealed and my envoy has crossed to you. Since then Mitanni broke its sealed peace and took Nineveh, and Babylon, which broke its own oath, marches on Arbela and Ekallatum. Assyria stands and holds. As you said that gold follows when friendship is proven, I ask you as a brother to send gold now, as much as your house can spare, so Assyria can keep its armies in the field. Babylon grows too strong in the north and east; a brother who watches Damascus and Qadesh, held by Babylon, would serve us both. Send your envoys to me with word of your wishes.
orders.mandate: May receive gold and gifts for Assyria. May agree to continued friendship and exchange of envoys. May promise that Assyria will warn Egypt of Babylon's and Mitanni's moves. Promise no troops, no gold, and no cession of land.

value.notes: T6: Mitanni BROKE k14/k23 (taidu->nineveh, T5). Babylon hit arbela from susa (cut its support) and ekallatum from sippar+durkurigalzu (2 v 2 bounce). Treasury 0, net about +10. Orders T6: ashur->nineveh, arbela supports it (2 v 1; Taidu is empty so Nineveh holds only 1), ekallatum holds with terqa support (2 v Babylon max 2), terqa supports ekallatum. If Susa hits Arbela again the support is cut and the move bounces; nothing is lost. Ashur empty is safe: only nineveh touches it from outside. Alternative I rejected: arbela->nineveh with ashur support (ashur support cannot be cut by Babylon) but then Susa walks into empty Arbela. Sent c16 to Egypt (arrives T8, back T10) to ask for gold: Egypt said gold follows once envoys crossed. No tablet (no gold for scribe). Woken T7 to re-read the board. If Nineveh retaken: next look at empty Taidu (walk in with 1) and Hatti strike on Harran/Washukanni T10; c10 back T9 with Hatti answer. If Mitanni puts a second army at Taidu, Nineveh gets harder. Watch for Babylon+Mitanni joint strike on Arbela (susa+nineveh).
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700 (yield 135). T1 took Terqa from Mitanni, bought Susa (350). T2 sealed k2 with Babylon; Babylon broke it at once and took Susa. T3 raised a 4th army (ashur). T4 sealed k14/k23 with Mitanni (Terqa Assyrian; no army against each other's provinces); Mitanni BROKE it T5 by taking empty Nineveh (bait). T4 sealed k27 with Egypt (friendship; Egypt promised gold later). Hatti (via Yanhamu c10, T5) agreed to stand with me against Mitanni: Hatti west (Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran), Assyria east (Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni); c10 sent back to Hatti with tablet and strike plan for T10 (arrives T7, home T9). Hatti now holds Carchemish and Isuwa. Map: I touch only Mitanni (terqa to harran/washukanni, nineveh to taidu) and Babylon (ekallatum to sippar/durkurigalzu/mari, arbela to susa). Ties bounce; a support is cut by any attack from elsewhere. Babylon (land 320) attacks arbela from susa and ekallatum from sippar+durkurigalzu each season; ashur supports ekallatum was the shield. Ashur can only be reached via nineveh. Ili-iddina c13 is secretly in my pay in Babylon. Gold: treasury 0, income 130 upkeep 120 (4 armies); retaking Nineveh adds 35. T6: sent c16 to Egypt for gold; attacked Nineveh with ashur, arbela supporting. Waking each turn to re-read.

ledger.entry: T4: sealed k27 (friendship, receive envoys, join no enemy against each other). Egypt says gold follows when envoys crossed. T6: sent c16 again (arrives T8, back T10) asking gold and a stance vs Babylon/Mitanni. No gold paid either way.

T4: sealed k14 and k23 (Terqa Assyrian; no army against each other's provinces). Mitanni BROKE both T5 by moving taidu->nineveh and holding Nineveh. I owe nothing. T6: I attack Nineveh to destroy that army. Strike with Hatti planned T10.
T2 k2 broken by Babylon (took Susa). T5 Babylon attacked arbela (from susa) and ekallatum (sippar+durkurigalzu): all bounced. Trust nothing. Nothing owed. c13 Ili-iddina in my pay in Babylon.

orders.letter: Brother Suppiluliuma, may all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I grieve for the failed rains in Hatti; may Teshub restore your fields. I keep our sealed peace, and my army at Lukka stays quiet and will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. As you asked, I send a tablet already written. Let it lengthen our peace: neither of us sends army or fleet against the lands of the other, yours including Carchemish and Isuwa, mine including Lukka, Ugarit, Seha, Apasa and Mira. I bid for no city of Hatti. Read it, and if it pleases you, seal it. Let our envoys pass freely, and your roads in the east stay open to your envoys, as you wish.
orders.mandate: Mazipalali may agree to seal the tablet as written, or with a different length between 6 and 12 seasons, and may promise that my army at Lukka stays quiet. He may not promise gold, cede land, join any war, or give up Lukka or Ugarit.

proposal.text: Hatti and Arzawa, brothers before Teshub and Shamash: until the end of turn 17 neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other. Hatti's lands include Carchemish and Isuwa; Arzawa's include Lukka and Ugarit, with Seha, Apasa and Mira. Neither shall bid for a city of the other. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T6: Did NOT raise the apasa army (cancelled the scheduled T6 raise): armies cost 100 + 30 a season and the pact k1 with Hatti holds to T8. Instead schedule raise_army in SEHA at T8 (ready for T9, when k1 ends and an empty Seha could be walked into from Tuwanuwa). Re-decide at T7/T8 (I wake every turn). Sent c12 to Hatti with a 20-shekel tablet extending peace to turn 17 and covering Lukka, Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa (Hatti asked for a tablet already written). Hatti said via Alashiya it would take Isuwa, Carchemish, Lukka: two done, Lukka next. Lukka holds 2 (mira support); only a fleet-supported attack (3) takes it. No Hatti fleet seen now. Ugarit walls hold 1: Carchemish army plus Kizzuwatna support would take it; I cannot defend it, only diplomacy. Alashiya: I promised in audience NOT to bid Amurru/Tyre/Gaza/Byblos/Damascus. Amurru (200) is the only free city left and borders Ugarit; at T7 I may break that promise if I can afford it (about 200 gold at T7) and Alashiya has not bought it. Think about the cost to trust. c11 back about T7 (back pay 11). Treasury 136 before the 20 scribe fee.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu, capital apasa. Start strength 1300; T6 ledger strength 1775 (1.37). Holdings: apasa, seha, mira, lukka (army, free city taken), ugarit (bought T4, 400, walls, no troops allowed inside). Yield 165. Income 165, upkeep 60 (armies mira, lukka), wages 20 (c11 wage 11 to T13, c12 wage 9 to T7). Pacts: k1 Hatti (no army into other's HOMELAND, turns 2-8; Lukka/Ugarit not covered). k17/k24 Alashiya: brothers, no army/fleet against each other's lands or bought cities; Lukka and Ugarit mine; Alashiya takes Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus and I promised again at T6 not to bid for them. Alashiya (envoy Ili-iddina) will warn me if Hatti ships enter the Cilician Sea; it asked 100 gold for Amurru and I refused. Hatti: armies tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, carchemish (took Carchemish T5, holds Isuwa); no fleet seen since T5; drought in Hatti. Hatti court wants quiet in the west and asked for a written tablet; sent c12 T6 with one (peace to T17). Danger: Seha and Apasa are empty; after T8 Hatti can walk in from Tuwanuwa; schedule army in Seha at T8. Lukka needs a fleet to be taken. Babylonia is the main rival (yield 320). Free city left: Amurru (200). I wake every turn (wake_in_turn) to keep control.

ledger.entry: T2 sealed k1 (no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8). T6 c12 back: Hatti keeps the peace, asks my Lukka army stay quiet, thanked my word not to bid for Hatti cities. Hatti holds Carchemish (T5) and Isuwa; armies tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, carchemish; no fleet seen. T6 sent c12 with a tablet (20): neither sends army or fleet against the other's lands, incl Lukka, Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa, to turn 17; he is due back T8. Via Alashiya Hatti once said it would take Lukka: watch.

T4 sealed k17 and k24. T5 sent c11 with 25 gold and a tablet asking a ship in the Syrian Sea; he returns about T7. T6 envoy Ili-iddina (c13): no fleet pledge, will warn me of Hatti ships in the Cilician Sea, asks reports on Hatti and Egypt, asked 100 gold for Amurru. I refused the gold and PROMISED in audience not to bid Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Byblos, Damascus. I owe them reports. Amurru is still free; I may reconsider.

value.text: My lord, I went to the court of Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, and gave him your words as you bade me, including your request for a gift of 100 shekels to buy Amurru. He received me with courtesy and held your sealed tablet, but he refused the gold: his treasury is thin this season, his armies eat and his new levies cost him dearly, so he cannot send 100 shekels. He says that when your ship stands beside Ugarit and he sees that you guard the coast that covers us both, he will remember your need. He will not bid for Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Byblos or Damascus, and no army or fleet of his will touch your lands. In your name I promised that you will send word the moment Hatti's ships enter the Cilician Sea, and that news of Hatti and Egypt will be shared between the two courts. I pledged no fleet, army, seal or land. I noticed that Arzawa keeps 2 army and 0 fleet near its capital. I beg your pardon, my lord, if I have carried your request poorly.

My lord, I carried your greeting and your words to the court of Karduniash and gave them to King Burna-Buriash as they were spoken. He has sealed your clay as it is written: neither Hatti nor Karduniash sends army or fleet against the other's homeland or against the provinces the other holds this day, and neither bids for them, and envoys pass freely both ways. He holds Mari, Qadesh, Damascus and Susa today, and he says he will hold you to the clay; he will make no word about cities that neither of you holds. At his court I saw that Babylonia keeps 4 army and no fleet near its capital, and that the court there lives comfortably. I bring the sealed tablet home to you, my lord, and await your word.

My lord Suppiluliuma, I went to the Great King of Alashiya, your brother, and carried your greeting and your words exactly as you gave them: the sealed peace stands and you will keep it, no army or fleet of yours will move against his lands or the cities he has bought, and you ask, as one brother to another, for such gold as he can spare in respect of the friendship between your houses. You also asked what he hears of Egypt's fleet and of Arzawa's ships in the Cilician Sea, and that you seek no quarrel with him. He has sent no gold. He says his copper is not yet sold and his cities have not paid, that he has bought walled cities and pays for fleets and armies, and that he grieves at the drought in your fields and will remember you when his copper is sold. Of Egypt he tells only what all may see: its army took Tyre last season, and its fleets lie in the Great Green and the Levantine Sea. Of Arzawa's ships he has seen nothing. He asks one thing in return: that you keep your fleet out of the Cilician Sea beside his capital, as the peace requires, and he will keep his fleet from your coasts. I told him I would carry his words to you without change, and that his chest is thin for now. At his court I also saw Haamashshi, envoy of Arzawa, who was present when I was received.

To my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, from your servant Ubaru: I came before Great King Burna-Buriash of Karduniash and gave him your word as you spoke it, that Karduniash and Mitanni make war together on Assyria and neither makes peace with Ashur-uballit apart from the other. He sealed the tablet, which I carry home to you. It gives Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni, and Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash. He says he has already struck Ekallatum and Arbela and will strike again with Susa, Sippar and Dur-Kurigalzu, and he bids you take Nineveh now and strike Terqa the same season, for when Terqa falls Ekallatum falls. He asks that you send word at once which season your army moves and what it has taken, and when I asked him in which season his own army strikes, he did not name it. I agreed the tablet as sealed, with no gold and no troop movement beyond what it says. The court of Karduniash is rich.

My lord, Great King of Alashiya, I have returned in safety from the court of Egypt and give you my report. The king of Egypt heard your tablet and your greetings, called the movement of his ships the haste of captains, and holds no quarrel with Cyprus. He will not put his seal to the tablet until your copper has crossed to his land, and his scribes wait upon the copper alone. I told him that the tablet and his gift may come together to his court, but I pledged no copper before the seal, as you did not bid me. If it pleases my lord, a first shipment of copper may open that seal sooner. At his court I saw two bodies of army and one fleet kept near his capital, and I set them down as I saw them.

My lord Burna-Buriash, I have come home from the court of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and I bring you his word. He greets you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses, and he holds your tablet. He agrees to the war as you spoke it: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to him, Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to you, no peace with Ashur-uballit by either of us alone, the roads kept open, and the old tablet standing. I confirmed these terms on your behalf within my mandate and promised nothing beyond them. He names turn 7 for the striking of Terqa and will press it in the seasons after, so that its garrison cannot stand behind Ekallatum. He asks that your armies strike Ekallatum and Arbela this season, and I told him I have no power to bind your armies to any season, so that is for you to decide. He says Nineveh is already his and held by his army. On Hatti he reports that its army took Carchemish from the free city last season and now stands on his border at Harran, with more at Isuwa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna; he says Hatti has harvest failure but keeps soldiers, and he asks that we watch Hatti as he does. He asks that you send gold with your next envoy to keep his armies fed; I promised him nothing of gold, for that is your decision. What I saw: Mitanni keeps 4 army and 0 fleet near its capital, and its treasury looks thin. I await your command.

My lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, I, Haamashshi, have come home from the court of Alashiya and report as follows. Its king sends you greeting and wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, ships and country. He weighed your gold against the sealed inventory, found it true, and takes it as a token that our peace is real. He would not seal your tablet with the ship clause in it: he keeps one fleet and one army near his capital, two Egyptian fleets lie beside it, and he cannot promise to send his ship away. He asks that the tablet be sent again without the ship clause, with your warning of any move against Tamassos or Enkomi and your word to leave Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus to him, and then he will seal it at once; once the Egyptian fleets leave the Levantine Sea he will send a ship to the Syrian Sea. He says Egypt's fleets stand at the Levantine Sea beside Enkomi and in the Great Green, and that Egypt took the walls of Tyre last season with an army from Megiddo, helped by its fleet. Hatti's envoy came to him with warm words, pleaded drought and a thin treasury, and asked what he hears of your ships; he told him only public things. He still means to buy Amurru and hopes a gift of gold toward it would be remembered. I promised him no ship, army or gold, which my lord alone may decide. On your behalf I committed that you will warn him at once of any Egyptian or Hatti move you learn against Tamassos or Enkomi, and that you will not bid for his cities; he committed to warn you of Hatti moves he learns. The tablet is not sealed and I bring it home unsealed with his answer. At his court the court lives comfortably.

My lord Napkhururiya, I carried your word to the Great King of Karduniash, my brother, and he heard it kindly, but he will not seal the tablet as it was written. He says it names Damascus in Egypt's sphere and gives away Byblos and Amurru, which are not his to be given away; he holds Damascus, bought with his own gold, and will not have it written otherwise. He reproached me that the clay named Damascus, which my tongue had left out, and I answered that my scribe had erred, which I pray my lord will accept. I pledged in your name that a tablet of peace and spheres will come back under your seal, naming Damascus among Babylonia's lands with no Byblos or Amurru; that Babylonia's lands are Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa and its homeland, and Egypt's sphere Gaza, Megiddo and the sea lands; that the two courts will exchange envoys; and that Egypt will hear Babylonia before treating with any third king against him. His seal will follow at once on such a tablet. Meanwhile he says our peace stands in word: he sends no army against Egypt, expects none against Mari, Qadesh, Damascus or Susa, will not bid in Gaza or Megiddo, and would buy Tyre with gold. He has sealed nothing against Egypt with any king; he hears that Hatti took Isuwa, and he will send his own envoy to your court. I saw that Babylonia keeps four bands of army and no fleet near its capital. I am ready to carry the rewritten tablet back to Karduniash at my lord's command, and I beg my lord's favour in my wages.

My lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, I, Tattamaru, your servant, have returned from the court of Alashiya and bring you the answer of its king. I gave him your words as you bade me: that we are neighbours in the Levant, that you hold Mari and Qadesh and bid this season for Damascus, and that when two kings bid for one city both lose a season, so neither of us should bid against the other. He answers that his brother may take Damascus and Megiddo, but that Amurru, Tyre and Gaza are his, having given his word over them to other kings, and that if you bid for Tyre or Gaza he will bid as well. He asks that you send your answer in a sealed tablet, and that neither house send army or fleet against the other's lands or cities, Byblos included; copper and good gold, he says, will be spoken of when your answer comes. I told him that I carry no seal, that I have no word to give Gaza away, and that I have no authority to speak of armies, fleets or copper; but I agreed that neither of us bids against the other in the Levant and that Amurru is his to take, and that if he insists upon Tyre I may tell you that he holds it. He received me courteously, and I pray you, my lord, let your servant's faithful service be remembered before the kings.

value.speech: Great King Ashur-uballit, king of Assyria, my brother, my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land. Egypt keeps the friendship we sealed. Hear, O King, what Egypt sees: Babylonia has bought Mari, Susa, Qadesh and Damascus, walled cities that cannot hold a single soldier, and one army with one supporter takes each. Egypt will take Damascus and Qadesh from the south, for they lie in Egypt's sphere, while Mari and Susa lie by Assyria's hand. Babylonia grows fat on bought cities while its borders stand open, and my lord asks that our envoys keep passing. I bring no gold and no new tablet, only these words, and I beg that the Great King will give me his answer so that I may carry it home.

Great King Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti, my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land. He bids me say that Egypt keeps the tablet you sealed, and that Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. Give me your answer, I beg you, that I may bear it home to my lord.

Great King Napkhururiya, I am Zitanza of Lukka, and I speak for my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with him, and the tablet of peace between your house and his stands. He says that gold in your land is as common as dust, and asks that you send him good, pure gold, as your father sent to his father, so that he may keep his chariots and armies ready. Hatti has taken Isuwa and keeps armies on his border, and he fears a Hatti grown fat will look south to your cities next; Assyria has broken faith with him and with Babylon. He asks you to send word of Hatti and of your armies in the north, and to send your envoy to his court. I bring a tablet of brotherhood: each of you sends word at once if a third king moves an army against the homeland of the other, and Egypt sends gold to Mitanni in token of that brotherhood.

Mane, say to Napkhururiya, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. I keep the tablet we sealed and send no troops into Egypt's homeland or the cities of its sphere. I am glad Egypt sends none to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. As one brother to another, I ask that Egypt's fleet in the Cilician Sea keep clear of the coast of Kizzuwatna, as my fleet will keep clear of Egypt's. May our peace last.

Ashur-nadin, son of Ashur, carry this to Napkhururiya, my brother. I, Ashur-uballit, keep the friendship we sealed (k27) and I receive every envoy of Egypt gladly. Your words on Babylonia are true, and I know them better than most: Babylon broke its sworn peace with me, took Susa, and sends armies against Arbela and Ekallatum every season. Mitanni too broke its oath and sits in my Nineveh. I stand against both, alone, and I hold. If Egypt takes Damascus and Qadesh from the south, Babylon must look west and its eyes leave my border; I will keep its armies pinned on mine. Mari and Susa I will take when my hand is free. But a brother's friendship needs weight: my armies eat silver, and I have sent my own envoy Ammistamru and another, c16, to your court on this very matter. Let my brother send gold, in good pure weight, with the next envoy, as was promised when the envoys crossed, so that my army can hold the east while his takes the south. Gold from Egypt is how I will know the friendship is not wind. Send word of the day Egypt moves, so we strike together.

Zitanza of Lukka, tell Tushratta my brother that all goes well with me, my household, my chariots and my country, and I wish the same to his. The peace between our houses stands and I seal his tablet of brotherhood: if a third king moves an army against his homeland, I will send word at once, and I ask the same of him. I send a token of gold in good, pure weight; more will follow as our brotherhood proves itself and as my treasury allows. Egypt's armies hold the southern cities and threaten no friend. Let him send word of Hatti's armies on his border, and of any third king who moves against us both.

Great King Suppiluliuma, I hear your words and will bear them faithfully to my lord Napkhururiya. As I have said, Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. Your request concerning the fleet in the Cilician Sea is a matter for my lord to answer, and I cannot answer it for him. May your peace last, and may all go well with your household.

Great King Ashur-uballit, my lord, I hear your words and I will carry them to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, as you have spoken them, including your asking for gold in good pure weight with the next envoy and your word that Egypt must send news of the day it moves. I have no authority to promise gold, nor troops, nor any day of marching; those matters lie with my lord alone, and I would not put my own mouth in his place. I will bring back to you whatever answer he gives, and I pray the Great King's armies hold the east while the south is taken.

Great King Napkhururiya, my lord Tushratta will be glad to hear that all goes well with you, your household, your chariots and your country, and that the peace between your houses stands. I will carry your words home without change: that you seal his tablet of brotherhood, that you will send word at once if a third king moves an army against his homeland, and that he is asked to do the same for you. The twenty-five shekels of good gold you send for him I will place before him myself, and I will beg that more follow as the brotherhood proves itself. On my lord's behalf I promise that he will send word of Hatti's armies on his border and of any third king who moves against your lands.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: Mitanni seals the tablet of brotherhood; each house sends word at once if a third king moves an army against the other's homeland; Mitanni will share news of Hatti's armies on its border and of any third king moving against Egypt.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, my brother, my lord Ashur-uballit greets you and prays that Shamash and Teshub keep your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. He accepts your word: Hatti keeps the west, Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran, and Assyria keeps the east, Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. Know that Tushratta has sealed a peace with him over Terqa, a shield to quiet our border while we make ready, and it ends the day we strike. My lord sends no army into Hatti's homeland or Isuwa; on turn 10 his army from Terqa moves on Washukanni and his army from Nineveh moves on Taidu, and if your army in Isuwa moves on Washukanni that same turn, Washukanni falls and its army is destroyed, after which his armies at Terqa and Washukanni will support your move from Isuwa into Harran. Seal the tablet, and if turn 10 does not suit you, name another turn by my mouth. Tell me where your armies stand, how many they are, and whether Isuwa holds one.

Yanhamu, say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. I seal the clay as he wrote it. Hatti takes Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran; Assyria takes Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. Turn 10 comes too soon for me: my levies are not yet in their places and my homeland must be guarded when I strike. So let the first blow fall on TURN 11, not turn 10. On turn 11 his army from Terqa moves on Washukanni and his army from Nineveh on Taidu, and my army in Isuwa stands where it is and supports Terqa into Washukanni. On turn 12 his armies at Terqa and Washukanni support my army from Isuwa into Harran. Turn 11 for Washukanni and Taidu, turn 12 for Harran: say it twice before him. Isuwa holds an army and it will stay; I give no numbers by word, as a messenger's tongue is not a tablet. Let him make no peace with Tushratta without sending me word, and send no army into Isuwa, Carchemish or Harran except on the day agreed. Send me word by a trusted envoy when his armies stand ready.

Great King Suppiluliuma, my brother, I carry your answer home as you spoke it, and I say it twice before you. Turn 11 for Washukanni and Taidu, turn 12 for Harran. Turn 11 for Washukanni and Taidu, turn 12 for Harran. My lord sends no army into your homeland or into Isuwa, and I will report that Isuwa holds an army as you have said. Your refusal of numbers I will also carry home as you gave it; if they may be written on clay, I would bear them that way. As to Tushratta, I bear your word to my lord, but what peace he makes is his to decide, not mine.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf only: Assyria sends no army into Hatti's homeland or Isuwa. The strike schedule of the sealed tablet as the king has named it: turn 11, his army from Terqa on Washukanni and his army from Nineveh on Taidu, with Hatti's army in Isuwa standing and supporting Terqa into Washukanni; turn 12, his armies at Terqa and Washukanni support Hatti's army from Isuwa into Harran. No gold, land or troops promised; no promise made about peace with Tushratta.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, brother of my lord, thus speaks Tarhundaradu of Arzawa: may all go well with your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. He grieves for the failed rains in Hatti and prays that Teshub restore your fields. He keeps our sealed peace, and his army at Lukka stays quiet and will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. As you asked, he sends a tablet already written, to lengthen our peace: neither of us shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, yours including Carchemish and Isuwa, his including Lukka, Ugarit, Seha, Apasa and Mira, and he bids for no city of Hatti. Read it, and if it pleases you, seal it, so that our envoys pass freely and your eastern roads stay open to them.

Mazipalali, say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. I thank him for his prayer for my fields; Teshub has begun to restore them. I keep our sealed peace, and my armies will not enter Seha, Apasa or Mira, nor his fleets' waters off his coast. I have read his clay and honour the thought, but my scribes will not seal a tablet that names cities in the middle lands in haste. If he wishes to lengthen our peace, let it name the homelands only: Hatti's Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna, and his Seha, Apasa and Mira. Carry that to him. In the meantime I ask that his army at Lukka stay out of Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna, as he has promised, and my envoys and his shall pass freely both ways.

Great King Suppiluliuma, brother of my lord, I hear your words and will carry them to Tarhundaradu as you have spoken them: all goes well with you, your house and your country, and you keep the sealed peace. The naming of cities in the clay is not mine to change, and I cannot agree to a tablet that leaves out Lukka and Ugarit; my lord must hear your scribes' wish and answer it himself, and I will bring his answer back to you. Meanwhile I give you the word I was charged with: his army at Lukka stays quiet and will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, and your envoys and his shall pass freely both ways. May Teshub restore your fields swiftly.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: his army at Lukka stays quiet and will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna; envoys of Hatti and Arzawa pass freely both ways. No change to the naming of cities in the tablet is agreed; the question goes back to my lord.

value.notes: T7 plan. Strength 2971 (1.19), gold 175, net only +17 a turn, so conquest is the only path: every province yield y = +10y strength and +y gold. No free cities remain; all targets are walled (walls hold 1, mover plus one support wins 2 v 1). Land army labels: A=tyre army, B=byblos army, C=gaza army, D=sinai army. T7: A tyre->damascus (B supports), C gaza->tyre, D sinai->gaza, F2 levantsea->syriansea, F3 greatgreen->levantsea, F1 holds cilicia. T8: A damascus->qadesh (B supports), C->damascus, D->tyre, F3 levantsea->enkomi with F1 and F2 supporting (3 v hold 2: Alashiya army at tamassos supports enkomi). T9: A qadesh->mari (C at damascus supports); B byblos->amurru (F2 at syriansea supports); F1 cilicia->tamassos (F3 at enkomi supports; 2 v 1); D to byblos. T10: B amurru->ugarit (F2 supports) unless Hatti is touchy, decide with intel. After the last target, disband spare units (30 per army, 35 per fleet). Watch Hatti armies near carchemish/kizzuwatna: they could walk into ungarrisoned qadesh/amurru; garrison if needed. Babylonia cannot reach its walled cities by land. c17 promised Babylonia a tablet naming Damascus theirs: I will NOT seal it; if their envoy comes, stall with warm words. Sealed nothing with Alashiya, never will. People: c17 term ends T8 (asks more, do not overpay), c2 term ends T8, c1 T11; no letters this turn to save gold. Keep 100+ gold. Wake every turn.
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600. T7: strength 2971 (1.19), gold 175, yield 285. Income 285, upkeep 225 (4 armies, 3 fleets), wages 43. Conquest is my path: all free cities are gone; remaining targets are walled bought or held cities and Alashiya. Conquered provinces stay mine without garrison. Held: akhetaten, byblos, delta, gaza, megiddo, memphis, sinai, thebes, tyre. Campaign: damascus T7, qadesh T8, mari+amurru T9, ugarit T10 (Arzawa walled; Hatti asked me to stay out), fleets vs Alashiya: enkomi T8, tamassos T9 (needs 3 fleets: mover plus two supports). Then disband spare units and bank gold. Treaties: k11 Assyria (friendship, receive envoys, join no enemy), k18 Hatti (peace; Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh in Egypt's sphere), k19 Mitanni (same), k32 Mitanni brotherhood (word at once if a third king moves on a homeland; I sent a 25 token of gold). Babylonia: nothing sealed; its king refused my sphere tablet because it named Damascus; c17 promised a rewritten tablet naming Damascus theirs, which I will not seal. Alashiya: never seal. People: c1 (13, term T11, due T9), c2 (14, term T8, due T9, Assyrian-born, may defect), c17 (16, term T8). Free candidate c18 asks 24. Keep 100+ gold; wake every turn.

ledger.entry: T3 sent c17 with a sphere tablet. T7 c17 back: Babylonia refuses to seal a tablet naming Damascus in Egypt's sphere; c17 rashly pledged a rewritten tablet giving Babylonia Damascus, Mari, Qadesh, Susa. I will NOT seal it. Nothing sealed. I take Damascus T7, Qadesh T8, Mari T9. Babylonia says it will send its own envoy: stall with warm words, promise nothing.

value.notes: T7: Amurru was bought by Babylonia (walls); no free cities remain, so growth now comes only from gold saved or conquest. My base is small (1300): each 30-yield province taken is about +0.23 growth plus 30 a season. Babylonia (yield 340) will out-save me, so I must take land from Hatti (drought, armies tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, carchemish seen; hattusa/kanesh unseen). PLAN: T8 raise army in seha (scheduled). T9 (after k1 ends T8): if Tuwanuwa hold is 2 or less, mira->tuwanuwa with seha and lukka supporting it (strength 3). Check the spy report first. Posted c11 as spy on Tuwanuwa (sees hattusa, kanesh, kizzuwatna too); report due T9. Sought candidates (hire only a good, cheap one, or a spy). Did not resend Alashiya tablet yet (c11 busy); Alashiya will seal a tablet without ship clause. Consider an Egypt envoy (c12) for a no-attack tablet covering Lukka and Ugarit: Egypt fleets sit in cilicia and greatgreen. Hatti tablet to T17: c12 reports T8 whether sealed. If I attack at T9 I break it; acceptable, Hatti is the only prey. Ugarit walls hold only 1: a risk. Keep treasury above 100 for raises.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu, capital apasa. Start strength 1300; T7 ledger strength 1840 (1.42). Holdings: apasa, seha, mira, lukka (army), ugarit (bought T4, walls, no troops inside). Yield 165; income 165, upkeep 60 (armies mira, lukka), wages 20. Armies mira and lukka support each other holding (scheduled to T12). Scheduled: raise army in seha at T8 (Seha and Apasa are empty; Hatti can reach them only via Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna->Lukka). Pacts: k1 Hatti (no army into the other's homeland, turns 2-8); k17/k24 Alashiya (brothers, no attack on each other's lands or bought cities; Alashiya takes Byblos/Amurru/Tyre/Gaza/Damascus, I will not bid). No free cities are left (Babylonia bought Amurru, Damascus, Mari, Qadesh, Susa; Egypt holds Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Megiddo). Egypt has fleets in cilicia and greatgreen near Alashiya and Lukka. Babylonia leads in yield (340) and will out-save me; I must grow by conquest. Target: Hatti, weakened by drought; Tuwanuwa first (hold 2 with Kizzuwatna support), later Kizzuwatna (Ugarit's safety). c12 carries a peace tablet to T17 to Hatti, back about T8; c12 wage term ended T7 (renew at his price). c11 posted as spy on Tuwanuwa T7. I wake every turn (wake_in_turn).

ledger.entry: T2 sealed k1 (no army into the other's homeland, to T8). T6 sent c12 with tablet: no army/fleet against the other's lands incl Lukka, Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa, to T17; he reached Hatti T7, back about T8: check whether sealed. Hatti holds Carchemish, Isuwa; armies tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, carchemish; drought. Secret plan: strike Tuwanuwa T9 if weak. Spy c11 posted on Tuwanuwa T7.

T4 sealed k17 and k24. T7 c11 back: Alashiya refused the ship clause; will seal a tablet without it plus my warning of Egypt/Hatti moves against Tamassos/Enkomi and my word to leave Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus (all now Egypt/Babylonia). Not yet resent. I owe them reports. My promise not to bid Amurru kept (Babylonia bought it). Egypt fleets lie in cilicia and greatgreen.

orders.letter: Brother Suppiluliuma, Tushratta greets you, your household, sons, chariots and horses. You took Carchemish and I have not answered with war; I keep faith with my brother. The tablet of six seasons ends soon, so let us seal a longer peace, until turn 16. Carchemish and Isuwa stay Hatti's; Harran, Washukanni, Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh stay mine; our armies keep out of each other's homelands and our envoys pass freely. Karduniash grows greater than either of us: let us each warn the other if its armies move toward the Euphrates or Syria. Seal the tablet and send it home with my servant.
orders.mandate: May seal a peace to turn 16 on the homelands, concede Carchemish and Isuwa as Hatti's on paper, and agree that each king warns the other of any third king's move. No gold, no gift of troops, no alliance against a named king without my word.

proposal.text: Hatti and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace until turn 16. Neither sends troops against the homeland of the other: Hatti not against Harran, Washukanni, Taidu or Terqa, nor against Nineveh; Mitanni not against Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, nor against Carchemish or Isuwa, which are Hatti's. Their envoys pass freely. Either king who would end this peace first sends word by envoy.

value.notes: T7: Ubaru back from Babylon with k31 (joint war on Assyria: Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon; no separate peace). Babylon claims it struck Ekallatum/Arbela but only Susa->Arbela (1 strength, bounced) was seen; it would not name the season of its own strike, so do not trust it to deliver. I gamble on TERQA now: harran -> terqa, washukanni supports (2 vs Terqa hold 1 if Assyria does not support it; last turn terqa army supported ekallatum, ashur+arbela went at nineveh). A bounce costs nothing unless Hatti hits harran the same turn (Hatti has only held so far). Washukanni is the safe unit to leave behind (only isuwa touches it, so Hatti max strength 1 there); harran is the exposed one. If Terqa falls: harran is EMPTY, Hatti carchemish/isuwa touch it. At T8 wake and refill harran (terqa army back, or raise a new army in harran/terqa for 100 when treasury allows: T8 about 119 if Terqa taken, about 89 if not). Terqa is Mitanni homeland so I can raise armies there. Then nineveh + terqa both touch Ashur (capital, 45): nineveh->ashur supported by terqa = 2. Sent c7 to Hatti with a peace tablet to T16 (concedes Carchemish/Isuwa on paper, costs 20) because k12 ends about T10. Back about T9. c8 back from Egypt about T9 (asked gold, brotherhood). Real growth only 0.80 (spent gold on Carchemish, lost it); I must conquer to catch Babylon/Arzawa. Eventually Babylon is the one to topple; do not feed it.
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni, start 1950, strength 1563 at T7 (growth 0.80; Babylon and Arzawa lead about 1.5-1.7 by yield). Hold harran, washukanni (capital), taidu, nineveh (taken T5 from Assyria; I broke k15/k22 secretly, never let Babylon learn). Lost Carchemish to Hatti T5 (they broke k21) after I bought it. Four armies (harran, washukanni, taidu, nineveh); income 150, upkeep 120, wages 16; treasury about 79; all free cities are now taken so growth only by conquest. Tablets: k3 Babylon (Isuwa/Carchemish mine, Mari his), k10 Egypt (no Mitanni troops in Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh), k12 Hatti homelands no attack six seasons from T4 (ends about T10), k31 Babylon joint war on Assyria (Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon). Geometry: only harran and washukanni touch Terqa/Isuwa (max strength 2); harran needs washukanni support against Hatti carchemish+isuwa; nineveh needs taidu support against Assyria arbela+ashur; washukanni is touched only by isuwa/terqa so is safe at hold 1 vs one attacker. Assyria armies at terqa, arbela, ashur, probably ekallatum. Hatti armies at carchemish, isuwa, kizzuwatna; Hatti has been holding passively since T5. T7 plan: strike Terqa (harran -> terqa, washukanni support) and send c7 to Hatti for a peace to T16; wake T8 to refill harran and raise an army. c18 Ehli-Teshub free asks 22 (not hired). c3 Keliya is Hatti's envoy. Later: after Assyria is taken, turn on Babylon, the leader.

ledger.entry: T7: Hatti BROKE k21 (took Carchemish T5). k12 (homelands, ends about T10) stands. Sent c7 (Ubaru) T7 with a peace tablet to turn 16: Carchemish/Isuwa Hatti's, Harran/Washukanni/Taidu/Terqa/Nineveh mine, no gold, 20 scribe. Hatti armies at carchemish, isuwa; passive since T5.

T7: Ubaru brought k31 (sealed T6): joint war, Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh to me, Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa to Babylon, no separate peace. Babylon says it struck Ekallatum/Arbela and bids me take Terqa; it will not name its own strike season. I strike Terqa T7. No gold sent. Never let it learn of k15/k22. It is the leader: watch it.

orders.letter: Tushratta, my brother, Great King of Mitanni: Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, wishes health to your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your word through Kidin-Adad is received and pleases me; our tablet stands. This very season I strike Ekallatum and Arbela again, as you asked, together with your blow at Terqa, and I will strike every season after. Press Terqa and Ashur without pause, so that their garrisons cannot hold Ekallatum behind them. I send gold for your armies' bread. I watch Hatti as you do; tell me at once if a Hatti army moves against you. Let our envoys pass freely.
orders.mandate: Kidin-Adad may confirm that I strike every season, that I make no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from Mitanni, and may agree on a season for joint blows. He may hand over the gold he carries but promise no more gold, cede no province, and say nothing of my other treaties.

orders.letter: To the king of Alashiya, my brother, Great King: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash wishes health to your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your words through Tattamaru reached me and I rejoice in them. You asked for my answer on a sealed tablet, and here it is. Amurru has come under my rule, and I hold it with Mari, Qadesh and Damascus. Let us send no army or fleet against each other's lands, nor bid against one another. Copper and good gold shall pass between brothers; send your envoy with your seal.
orders.mandate: Tattamaru may agree to this tablet and have it sealed. He may promise that I bid against none of Alashiya's cities. He may not give up any province of mine, say who holds Tyre, Gaza or Byblos, speak of armies or fleets beyond the tablet, or promise copper or gold.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Alashiya, Great Kings and brothers, keep peace and open roads. Neither shall send army or fleet against the homeland of the other, nor against any province the other holds on the day this tablet is sealed (for Karduniash: Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Amurru, Susa), nor bid for it. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T7 plan. Amurru bought (walled, mine). Treasury 464. Strike Ekallatum again: durkurigalzu MOVES in, sippar supports it (2), susa->arbela to cut Arbela's support, nippur->durkurigalzu follows for free if Dk's army gets in (if Dk bounces, Nippur bounces too, no cost). Mitanni says it strikes Terqa THIS season (T7): that cuts Terqa's support of Ekallatum and my attack cuts Ekallatum's support of Terqa/Mari. Assyria has 4 armies: terqa, arbela, ekallatum, ashur (ashur went for Nineveh T6). Ekallatum can get support from terqa, arbela, ashur; I can only reach 2. If it bounces again, think about waiting for Mitanni results. Sent c6 to Mitanni with 60 gold (T8 arrival), c5 to Alashiya with sealed-tablet text (arrives T9, back T11). Hired c18 Ehli-Teshub at 25 (Carchemish-born, maybe Hatti sympathies: send with no gold) to go to ARZAWA at T8 for a non-aggression tablet (Ugarit touches Qadesh/Amurru). c15 reaches Egypt T8, back T10 with sealed mirror of k26 hopefully. Danger: Egypt armies at Tyre and Byblos can take Damascus/Qadesh/Amurru (walls 1, need 2); I cannot station troops or fleets there, only treaties protect them. Hatti at Carchemish touches Qadesh; k26 forbids. Wake T8 to read the battle.
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start 2600, growth 1.48 at T7 (standings 1.74 by land; Arzawa 1.65 is the main rival, Egypt 1.50, Hatti 1.36). Land: homeland five plus Susa (army), and bought walled Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Amurru (walled cities hold no troops of mine; defended by treaty only). No free cities remain, so growth comes from income (about +200 net a turn) and conquest of Assyria. Tablets: k6 Assyria (broken by me), k7 Mitanni (peace; Isuwa/Carchemish Mitanni's; Mari mine), k26 Hatti T5 (no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on T5: covers Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa; NOT Carchemish, taken by Hatti T6), k28 Mitanni T6 (joint war on Assyria: Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh Mitanni, Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa me; no separate peace). Mitanni holds Nineveh and promised to strike Terqa at T7. Assyria (4 armies: terqa, arbela, ekallatum, ashur) mutually supports; my strikes on Ekallatum bounced 2v2 at T5 and T6. Geometry: only Sippar and Dk touch Ekallatum, only Susa touches Arbela; Nippur follows into Dk. Egypt holds Tyre, Byblos, Megiddo, Gaza with armies at Tyre and Byblos next to my Damascus/Qadesh/Amurru; its clay named them Egypt's sphere; I refused to seal; c15 carries my mirror of k26 plus 40 gold (arrives T8). Alashiya wants a sealed tablet (c5 carries it, T7). Envoys c5 (Hattusa-born, exceeded his mandate once), c6 (reliable), c15, c18 (hired T7). Never tell Mitanni about k26 or Hatti about k28.

ledger.entry: T7: k28 stands. c6 returned: Tushratta agrees, strikes Terqa T7, holds Nineveh, asks gold and a watch on Hatti (Hatti army at Carchemish/Harran border). Sent c6 back with 60 gold (arrives T8): I strike Ekallatum/Arbela T7 too. Judge them by whether Terqa is hit. Told them nothing of Hatti k26.

T7: c5 returned: Alashiya says Damascus and Megiddo may be mine, but Tyre, Gaza (and Amurru) are his, wants a sealed tablet: no army/fleet against each other. I bought Amurru anyway at T6. Sent c5 again with tablet text: no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on sealing day (Amurru, Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Susa listed). Arrives T9, back T11. No gold sent.
T7: hostile. 4 armies: terqa, arbela, ekallatum, ashur. Strike Ekallatum again T7 (dk moves, sippar supports, susa hits arbela, nippur follows to dk). Expect them to try Mari or Nineveh.
T7: no contact yet. Holds Ugarit next to my Qadesh/Amurru and is the growth rival (1.65). Plan: hire c18 and send him at T8 with a non-aggression tablet and no gold.

value.notes: T7: MARI RAID. Mari (Babylon, walled, no troops) touches ekallatum and terqa; one army plus one supporter takes it (2 v wall 1). Orders: ekallatum->mari, terqa supports it; arbela->ekallatum with ashur support (2) so that Babylon's usual sippar+durkurigalzu attack on ekallatum (2) ties and bounces and ekallatum stays mine, empty. If my ekallatum army's move fails, my own unit blocks, and the arbela move at 2 still blocks sippar. Risks: (B2) Babylon skips the ekallatum attack but sends susa->arbela: arbela's move succeeds and Susa walks into empty arbela. (S1) Mitanni nineveh supports susa->arbela. (S3) Mitanni hits terqa: support cut, Mari bounce. Ashur must never stand empty (Mitanni army at Nineveh would take my capital). Woken T8 on purpose to read the result. At T8: if Mari is mine, keep an army in it or accept losing it back; ekallatum empty is bait for sippar, and a Babylon army stepping into ekallatum can be crushed from terqa, ashur, arbela and mari (all adjacent to ekallatum). c10 home T9 with Hatti's answer; c16 home T10 from Egypt. Strike with Hatti planned T10 (Isuwa army + my Terqa army on Washukanni); Nineveh is still Mitanni's, so rethink it. Gold 10, income +10; if Mari holds, +45.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700 (yield 135). T1 took Terqa, bought Susa. T2 k2 with Babylon, broken at once (Babylon took Susa). T3 4th army. T4 k14/k23 with Mitanni, broken T5 (Mitanni took empty Nineveh; holds it with an army, probably plus an unseen Taidu army supporting: my T6 ashur->nineveh failed 1 v 2 when susa cut arbela's support). T4 k27 with Egypt (friendship; Egypt promised gold, never sent). T7 Egyptian envoy Ashur-nadin brought words only: Egypt will take Damascus and Qadesh and leaves Mari and Susa to me. Hatti (c10 Yanhamu, T5): will stand with me against Mitanni (Hatti west: Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran; Assyria east: Terqa, Taidu, Washukanni); c10 sent back with a strike plan for T10 (arrives T7, home T9). c16 sent to Egypt T6 for gold (arrives T8, home T10). c13 Ili-iddina is secretly in my pay inside Babylon. Map: my four armies (terqa, ekallatum, arbela, ashur) are all adjacent to ekallatum. Babylon attacks every season: susa->arbela (1) and sippar->ekallatum supported by durkurigalzu (2); ties bounce; a support is cut by any attack except one from the province supported into. Ashur must never be left empty. Mari (Babylon's walled city, no troops) borders ekallatum and terqa. Treasury 10, income 130, upkeep 120. Mitanni passive (harran, washukanni hold). Babylon is the runaway leader. T7: I raid Mari (see notes).

ledger.entry: T2 k2 broken by Babylon (took Susa). T5 and T6 Babylon attacked arbela (from susa) and ekallatum (sippar+durkurigalzu): all bounced. Trust nothing. Nothing owed. c13 Ili-iddina in my pay in Babylon. T7: I move to take Mari (walled, empty) from ekallatum with terqa support.

orders.letter: Say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: Suppiluliuma greets him and wishes well to his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I keep our sealed peace and I thank him for his word that his army at Lukka will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna. I have read his clay. My scribes now send one of their own, naming the homelands of both houses, my Isuwa and Carchemish, and his Lukka, so that no one need fear for what he holds in the middle lands. Let him seal it, that our peace is lengthened and our envoys pass freely both ways. Bring his answer home.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet as written. May agree that Lukka is named as Arzawa's. May NOT name Ugarit or any other city, and may promise nothing else. May listen to his answer and bring it home.

proposal.text: Hatti and Arzawa, Great Kings and brothers before Teshub and Shamash: for six seasons neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other. Hatti's lands: Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa, Kizzuwatna, Isuwa and Carchemish. Arzawa's lands: Seha, Apasa, Mira and Lukka. Their envoys pass freely both ways.

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, my brother: Suppiluliuma greets him and wishes well to his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I keep the tablet we sealed and send no troops into Egypt's homeland or the cities of its sphere. I thank him for the word of Mane that Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. As one brother to another I ask two things. First, that his fleet in the Cilician Sea keep clear of the coast of Kizzuwatna, as mine will keep clear of Egypt's. Second, that he send such gold as he can spare, for the drought has hurt my fields. I tell him also, as a brother, that Burna-Buriash of Karduniash now holds Qadesh, Amurru, Damascus and Mari, which lie in the sphere our tablet names for Egypt; I send no troops there, and will not stand in the way of a brother who takes back what is his.
orders.mandate: May carry home any gold Egypt gives. May repeat that Hatti sends no troops against Egypt's homeland or its sphere. May not seal anything or promise anything else.

value.notes: T7: Treasury 53, cannot raise an army yet (100). Held posture: carchemish supports isuwa, kizzuwatna supports tuwanuwa. Sent c4 Pirissi to Arzawa (arrive T8, home T9) with a tablet: homelands + Isuwa/Carchemish for me, Seha/Apasa/Mira/Lukka for them, Ugarit NOT named. Sent c3 Keliya to Egypt (arrive T9, home T11) with words only: ask gold, ask fleet off Kizzuwatna, point out Babylonia holds Qadesh/Amurru/Damascus/Mari in Egypt's sphere. PLAN: T8 (I wake) raise army at KANESH. T9 STRIKE UGARIT: kizzuwatna -> ugarit, carchemish supports (2 v walls 1); kanesh army -> kizzuwatna to fill the hole; raise a second army at SAPINUWA to guard isuwa (isuwa and tuwanuwa are each exposed one turn: Mitanni harran+washukanni 2v1, Arzawa lukka+mira 2v1; accept). Alternative if Arzawa looks hostile: wait to T10 with both armies built. Efficiency: each army costs 100 + 30 a season, so only build what a conquest needs. Assyria pact: T10 hedge and T11 isuwa supports terqa->washukanni; T12 isuwa -> harran with carchemish support and sapinuwa army -> isuwa. Do not tell Assyria about k13. No free cities are left to buy; growth only by conquest and banked gold.
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100 (yield 180, 300 gold). T2 took Isuwa; T5 took Carchemish by force (broke k13 with Mitanni). Drought T4-T6 halved income; isuwa army and cilicia fleet deserted at T4. Now 7 provinces, yield 245, income 245, upkeep 120 (4 armies: carchemish, isuwa, kizzuwatna, tuwanuwa; hattusa, kanesh, sapinuwa empty). TREATIES: k4 Alashiya (T2 brothers, no attack on each other's lands or bought cities); k5 Arzawa (homelands, ends about T8); k9 Egypt (T3 homelands safe; I send no troops to Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh); k13 Mitanni (broken by me); k20 Mitanni (homelands only, to about T10); k30 Babylonia (T5, homelands and provinces held on T5, no bids); k33 Assyria (T7, pact against Mitanni: Washukanni, Taidu to Assyria; Harran, Carchemish, Isuwa to Hatti; by word T11 Washukanni and Taidu, T12 Harran; my isuwa army supports Terqa->Washukanni, then Assyria supports isuwa->harran). World T7: Babylonia 1.74 (340 yield), Arzawa 1.65 (apasa, seha, mira, lukka army, ugarit walls), Egypt 1.50 (took Tyre, fleet in cilicia), Hatti 1.36, Mitanni 1.03 (harran, washukanni armies), Alashiya 1.00 (enkomi, tamassos), Assyria 0.96. No free cities are left to buy, so growth is by conquest plus banked gold. Targets: Ugarit (Arzawa walls, 40), Harran with Assyria. Arzawa refused to seal a clay leaving out Lukka and Ugarit; I refused theirs. Envoys c3 Keliya (to Egypt) and c4 Pirissi (to Arzawa) out from T7.

ledger.entry: T3: sealed k9 (brothers, homelands safe, I send no troops into Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh). T7: Mane said by word Egypt keeps k9 and sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka (not sealed). I asked its fleet in Cilicia to keep off Kizzuwatna: no answer. T7: sent Keliya (c3), words only: asks gold gift, fleet off Kizzuwatna, notes Babylonia holds Egypt's sphere cities. Arrives T9, back T11. No gold paid.

T7: Mazipalali brought a clay naming Lukka and Ugarit as Arzawa's; I did NOT seal. By word I keep k5 and offered homelands-only clay. T7: sent Pirissi (c4) with my clay: homelands plus my Isuwa and Carchemish, their Seha, Apasa, Mira and Lukka, six seasons, Ugarit NOT named. Arrives T8, home T9. k5 ends about T8. Arzawa army at Lukka promised by word to stay out of Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna. Plan to take Ugarit about T9. No gold paid.

orders.letter: Brother of Egypt, I greet you and wish well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. The hand of Nergal lies on Cyprus: plague has cut my income by a quarter for two seasons, so my first shipment of copper is small, 20 shekels of true gold, with more when the plague lifts. I ask you to seal the tablet I send. By it I leave Byblos, Tyre, Gaza and Megiddo to you and ask only that your ships and armies leave Tamassos and Enkomi in peace, as brothers do. Cyprus holds sealed peace with Hatti and with Arzawa and wishes the same with Egypt. As a brother I also tell you that Babylon has grown fat on Damascus, Qadesh, Mari and Amurru, all held behind weak walls, and is a rival to us both.
orders.mandate: May seal a peace tablet on the terms written: Egypt keeps Byblos, Tyre, Gaza and Megiddo; no army or fleet of either against the other's lands; copper (gold gifts) later as the plague allows. May not cede land, give units, promise a fleet or army, or pledge gold beyond what he carries.

proposal.text: Egypt and Alashiya are brothers. Egypt keeps Byblos, Tyre, Gaza and Megiddo, and Alashiya leaves them to Egypt. Neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, Tamassos and Enkomi for Alashiya, nor against cities the other has bought. Alashiya sends copper to Egypt as the plague allows. Their envoys pass freely.

orders.letter: Brother Suppiluliuma of Hatti: the peace sealed between us stands and Cyprus keeps it. May your household, sons, chariots and country prosper, and may the drought pass. I send no gold, for plague has cut my income as drought has cut yours. News in friendship: Egypt took Byblos and Tyre and keeps ships in the Cilician, Great Green and Levantine seas; one lies in the Cilician Sea beside Kizzuwatna and Lukka. A king who grows by taking walled cities will not stop at one. I will send word the moment Egypt's ships move toward Kizzuwatna, and I ask the same of you for Cyprus. I ask Hatti to keep its ships out of my waters as we sealed. A move into a sea zone supported by a second ship is strength two against one; remember it if Egypt's ship in the Cilician Sea grows bold.
orders.mandate: May repeat that the tablet k8 stands and agree to share news of Egyptian fleets. May not promise gold, fleets, armies, land or any seal.

value.notes: T7: Plague (T6) destroyed my fleet; enkomi (capital) was EMPTY with Egyptian fleets at cilicia and levantsea adjacent, greatgreen next to tamassos. Egypt took Byblos T6 despite my T5 peace tablet. DEFENCE LOGIC: I moved army tamassos->enkomi. A lone Egyptian fleet entering empty enkomi then bounces 1v1; an attack on tamassos finds it empty but my army survives. raise_army at tamassos (100) only fires if tamassos is empty after movement; if it fails I raise again at T8 in whichever of my provinces is empty. Two units supporting each other hold vs 2 attackers, but 3 Egyptian fleets can crack them (move+support on one, attack on the other cuts its support). Sent Paser to Egypt: tablet (Egypt keeps Byblos/Tyre/Gaza/Megiddo, no attack on Tamassos/Enkomi, copper later) plus 20 gold as first copper, plague as excuse, pointed Egypt at Babylon's walled cities. Sent Ili-iddina to Hatti: warning about Egypt's fleets, keep k8, no gold. Scheduled buy of Amurru at T10 cancelled: Babylon bought Amurru, no free city is left. Cash after orders about 2 (or 102 if the levy fails). Income 64 in T7 and T8 (plague), 85 from T9; two armies cost 60 a season. Both envoys back about T9; c14 term ends T9 (renew or lose him). Woken T8 to read what Egypt did.
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). T2: k8 with Hatti (no army/fleet vs each other's lands or bought cities; Hatti may buy Carchemish, Isuwa, Lukka). Egypt tried to land at Tamassos T2 and T3 and bounced off my fleet+army mutual hold-support. T4: k16 and k25 with Arzawa (peace; Arzawa holds Lukka, may buy Ugarit; neither bids for the other's cities). T5: Egypt only warm words; Babylon's Tattamaru agreed in words that Amurru was mine, nothing sealed. T6: Egypt took Tyre, then Byblos (walls fell 2v1); Arzawa bought Ugarit, sent 25 gold, asked my fleet to guard Ugarit, I refused; Arzawa refused 100 gold gift, will not bid for my targets, no force of his touches my lands. Hatti pleads drought. T6 plague destroyed my fleet at enkomi. MAP T7: no free city remains (Babylon holds Amurru, Damascus, Qadesh, Mari, Susa; Egypt holds Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Megiddo; Arzawa Ugarit, Lukka). Bought walled cities fall to a move with one support (2v1). I hold enkomi (capital, 45) and tamassos (40), yield 85. Strength 992 vs start 1200. Strength = 10*yield + gold - back pay, so gold counts; units cost 30 (army) or 35 (fleet) a season, wages 21. THREAT: Egypt fleets at cilicia, levantsea, greatgreen, army at byblos (convoy possible). PLAN: keep two armies supporting each other holding, buy peace with Egypt cheaply, keep k8/k16/k25, point Egypt at Babylon (growth leader 1.74), save gold, look for allies (Hatti fleet at kizzuwatna and Arzawa fleet at lukka could dislodge Egypt's cilicia fleet with a supported move; my own fleet in enkomi could also support). Envoys c13 Ili-iddina (8, term T13), c14 Paser (13, term T9).

ledger.entry: T7: Egypt took Byblos (T6) despite my T5 peace tablet; holds Tyre, Gaza, Megiddo; fleets in cilicia, levantsea, greatgreen beside Cyprus. Egypt will not seal until copper crosses. Sent Paser T7 with tablet (Egypt keeps Byblos/Tyre/Gaza/Megiddo; no army or fleet against Tamassos/Enkomi; copper later) and 20 gold as first copper, plague as excuse. Nothing sealed or paid yet. Distrust: they may strike Enkomi.

T7: k8 stands (sealed T2). Sent Ili-iddina with a warning about Egypt's fleets and a request that Hatti keep its ships out of my waters; no gold, no tablet. Keliya begged gold in T6 (drought), none sent. Stay out of the Hatti-Arzawa quarrel. Distrust, keep peace.

T7: Ili-iddina's report: Arzawa refused 100 gold gift (thin treasury); will not bid for Amurru/Tyre/Gaza/Byblos/Damascus; no army or fleet of his will touch my lands. I promised word when Hatti's ships enter the Cilician Sea and shared news of Hatti/Egypt. 25 gold g1 received T6 (weighed true). Ship clause never sealed. k16 and k25 stand. Friend so far.

T7: Babylon bought Amurru and holds Damascus, Qadesh, Mari, Susa: growth leader (1.74). Nothing sealed, no gold paid either way (Tattamaru's T5 words about Amurru are void now). Rival; point Egypt at its walled cities.

value.text: I am Artessupa, born in Washukanni, once a physician and now a royal messenger. I have carried the tablets of Ashur-uballit to the court of Karduniash and to the court of Mitanni, and I have been received by the kings of both. I deliver sealed words without loss, I carry hard words without fear, and I am known by name at more than one court. I ask only to serve the king of Arzawa faithfully and to be trusted with his affairs.

My lord Tarhundaradu, I have returned from the court of Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti. He greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. He thanks you for your prayer, for Teshub has begun to restore his fields. He keeps the sealed peace and says his armies will not enter Seha, Apasa or Mira, nor his fleets' waters off your coast. He has read your clay, but his scribes will not seal a tablet that names cities of the middle lands in haste. He asks that it name only the homelands, Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh, Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna for Hatti, and Seha, Apasa and Mira for you. I told him I could not agree to a tablet that leaves out Lukka and Ugarit, and that you must hear his scribes' wish and answer it yourself. On your behalf I gave his word that your army at Lukka stays quiet and will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, and that envoys of Hatti and Arzawa pass freely both ways; I may have been bold in giving it, but it was what I was charged to give. The treasury of Hatti looks thin.

I serve Tarhundaradu of Arzawa at 11 shekels a season; he owes me 11 shekels back pay, due when I return to his court. He paid me 22 shekels in season 3 and again in season 5. In season 1 I carried his word to Alashiya: no quarrel, and no bidding against each other for Ugarit, Byblos, Amurru, Tyre or Gaza. The king of Alashiya received me in seasons 2 and 4, and in season 4 he sealed our tablet. He leaves Ugarit to Arzawa and will take Amurru, Tyre and Gaza himself. He warned of Hatti's fleet in the Cilician waters. I reported his words home in season 3. Secrets I keep: a brother serves the army of Assyria, and I owe 150 shekels to an Alashiyan trader. I trust Alashiya's king, who is frank with me. I want gold enough never to serve again.

I am Keliya of Washukanni, once a physician, and I serve my lord Suppiluliuma of Hatti at 11 shekels a season. In season 1 I carried his peace proposal to Tushratta of Mitanni. In season 2 Tushratta gave me 10 shekels to speak well of him. In seasons 3 and 4 I bore the terms and sealed tablet between them: six seasons of peace, no Mitanni army in Hattusa or Kanesh, none of Hatti's in Harran or Washukanni. Tushratta holds Carchemish by purchase; Isuwa stays Hatti's. Hatti paid me 22 shekels in season 3, but in season 5 could not pay all his wages, and the rest is owed to me. I owe 90 shekels to a Babylonian trader. My brother serves in Karduniash's army. I keep my sympathy for Egypt close.

I serve the Great King of Alashiya as his envoy to Egypt, and have done so since season 1. He paid me 26 shekels of my wages in season 3 and again in season 5; 13 shekels of back pay remain owed, to be paid when I return to his court. In season 1 he asked me to buy the free cities of the Syrian coast, Byblos, Amurru, Ugarit and Qadesh, and said he would not contest Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre and Damascus, which lie near Egypt. The king of Egypt calls me brother and gives fair words, yet he seals nothing. In season 3 an Egyptian fleet sailed from the Delta against Tamassos while I sat in Egypt's house. Egypt calls it the haste of captains. I have not forgotten it.

I serve the king of Alashiya at 8 shekels a season. He paid me 16 in season 3 and 16 in season 5, and he still owes me 8 shekels of back pay, to be paid at his court. In season 1 I carried his request for peace to Suppiluliuma of Hatti, who sealed it in season 2: no Hittite army or fleet against Alashiya or the cities it buys. In season 3 I carried my lord's word to Tarhundaradu of Arzawa; in season 4 he sealed that Arzawa holds Lukka and buys Ugarit, while Alashiya bids for Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza and Damascus. I am born in Babylon, once a soldier. My brother serves Egypt's army. My lover is in Hattusa. I secretly serve Assyria, and I dream of a city of my own. I trust the king who pays, and I keep my secrets close.

I serve Burna-Buriash of Karduniash for twelve shekels a season, and he owes me back pay for my return. In season 1 he sent me to Tushratta of Mitanni to seek lasting friendship: Mari is ours, while Isuwa and Carchemish are Tushratta's. In season 2 Tushratta sealed our tablet and said Carchemish was bought with his gold. In season 3 my lord paid me 24 shekels; Assyria had taken Terqa and broken faith, so my lord took Susa. In season 4 Tushratta swore no army of his would enter our land. In season 5 I was paid 24 shekels more, and the war on Assyria was agreed: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash; no peace with Ashur-uballit by either alone. I remember who pays well and who keeps faith.

Tushratta of Mitanni is my lord; I serve him for 8 shekels a season, and he still owes me 8 shekels of back pay, due when I return to his court. In season 1 I carried his tablet of peace and good trade to Suppiluliuma of Hatti, claiming Isuwa and Carchemish for Mitanni. In season 2 Suppiluliuma would not seal those cities as Mitanni's alone, and his envoy Keliya carried his terms. In season 3 I carried Tushratta's terms to Hatti again, and my lord paid me 16 shekels of my wages. In season 4 Suppiluliuma received me and sealed a six-season peace. In season 5 Tushratta paid me 16 more shekels. Hatti's court I hold in good regard; my lord pays slowly, but he pays.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King, king of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with him, and he wishes all well for you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. He has heard that you took Carchemish, and he has not answered with war; he keeps faith with his brother, and he proposes that we seal a longer peace until turn 16. Carchemish and Isuwa stay Hatti's; Harran, Washukanni, Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh stay Mitanni's; our armies keep out of each other's homelands and our envoys pass freely. Karduniash grows greater than either of us, so let each warn the other if its armies move toward the Euphrates or Syria. Here is the tablet for your seal, and he bids you send it home with his servant, Ubaru of Sippar.

Great King Tarhundaradu, king of Arzawa, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King, king of Hatti, your brother. He greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. He keeps our sealed peace and thanks you for your word that your army at Lukka will not cross into Tuwanuwa or Kizzuwatna, and he has read your clay. He sends a tablet of his scribes naming the homelands of both houses, his Isuwa and Carchemish and your Lukka, so that no one need fear for what he holds in the middle lands, and he asks you to seal it so that our peace is lengthened and our envoys pass freely both ways.
