I humbly bring this tablet before you for your seal, and I shall carry your answer home to my lord.

Great King Napkhururiya, my lord Burna-Buriash of Karduniash wishes health to your house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country, and he has sent me, his servant Tehip-tilla, to speak to you. He says that the clay your envoy Sin-iqisham brought gave Damascus to your sphere, though it was promised as his own, yet he does not quarrel over a scribe's slip and sends a plain tablet in its place, as brothers seal. I bring that tablet for you to seal: neither of you shall send army or fleet against the homeland of the other, nor against any province the other holds on the day of sealing, nor bid for it, and your envoys and his shall pass freely. Let the tablet also name Megiddo, Tyre, Gaza and Sinai as Egypt's, and Mari, Qadesh, Damascus and Susa as Karduniash's. My lord sends forty shekels of good gold as a brother's gift, sealed in bags and weighed against his inventory, and asks that you seal the tablet and return it by your envoy or his.

Tushratta, Great King, my lord Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, wishes health to your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. He has received your word through me, and it pleases him; our tablet stands. This very season he strikes Ekallatum and Arbela again, as you asked, together with your blow at Terqa, and he will strike every season after, and this season shall be the season of our joint blows. He bids you press Terqa and Ashur without pause, so that their garrisons cannot hold Ekallatum behind them, and he makes no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from you. He watches Hatti as you do and asks that you tell him at once if a Hatti army moves against you. Here is the gold he sends for your armies' bread, sixty shekels by the inventory under his seal; he promises no more gold than this, and he asks that our envoys pass freely.

Say to Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. I have received your word and your sixty shekels, and I thank you. Our tablet stands. Terqa is now mine, as I told you it would be, and my armies stand at Terqa and Nineveh, both next to Ashur. I will press Ashur as you ask. But Ashur falls only if your blow at Ekallatum and Arbela truly lands in the same season, so that their garrisons are pulled away. Let your envoy name the season of your strike and let me see Ekallatum or Arbela in your hand. I too make no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from you. I watch Hatti and will send word if a Hatti army moves against either of us. Let our envoys pass freely.

Pirissi, say to Suppiluliuma, my brother: Tarhundaradu greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I thank you for your clay and for the keeping of our sealed peace. I will not seal this tablet as it stands. It names Lukka as mine but leaves out Ugarit, which I bought and hold with its walls. A peace that names the middle lands must name all of them, or it frightens more than it calms. Send me a tablet that lists Ugarit among the lands of Arzawa, beside Seha, Apasa, Mira and Lukka, and I will weigh it gladly. Envoys of Hatti will always be received at my court. Go in peace.

Tehip-tilla, tell my brother Burna-Buriash that Egypt wishes health to his house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I thank him for the forty shekels and for a tablet written in the language of brothers. A matter this large must lie before my scribes and my gods before my seal is set to it. I will answer by my own envoy. Until then Egypt bears no ill will toward Karduniash, and your envoys will pass freely through my roads.

To Tushratta, Great King, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti. All goes well with me, and I wish all well to your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. I have heard your words and they please me. I seal your tablet: peace until turn 16, Carchemish and Isuwa are Hatti's, Harran, Washukanni, Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh are Mitanni's, and our envoys pass freely. Karduniash grows great, and I will watch the Euphrates and Syria. Ubaru of Sippar carries the sealed tablet home. Let brothers keep their word.

Great King Suppiluliuma, I have heard your word, and it pleases this servant as much as it pleases you. I carry the sealed tablet home to Tushratta with joy: peace until turn 16, Carchemish and Isuwa as Hatti's, and our envoys free to pass. May Shamash, whom I served as a priest in Sippar, witness this seal and keep both houses in health.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: peace until turn 16 as sealed on the tablet; Carchemish and Isuwa acknowledged as Hatti's; envoys pass freely; each king warns the other of any third king's move, and Mitanni warns Hatti if its armies move toward the Euphrates or Syria.

value.speech: Great King, I will carry your words to my lord Burna-Buriash, and he shall hear that Egypt wishes health to his house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country, and that Egypt bears no ill will toward Karduniash. Your servant thanks the Great King for his patience with a matter so large, and bows before his scribes and gods, who must first weigh it. I shall wait for your envoy with a humble heart, and I pray that my lord's gold and tablet find favour in your eyes.

Great King Tarhundaradu, king of Arzawa, my brother, I have heard your word and I will carry it to my lord Suppiluliuma exactly as you have spoken it. I have no charge to write Ugarit, or any other city, into a tablet, and I will not speak for my lord beyond what he has sent me to say. The tablet names Lukka as your land, as you have seen, and I will lay your answer before him and bring back his reply. May Teshub and Shamash watch over our peace, and may Hatti's envoys always be received at your court.

Great King Tushratta, my lord Burna-Buriash names this present season, the eighth, as the season of our joint blows. This very season he strikes Ekallatum and Arbela, as your blow falls upon Terqa, and every season after he strikes as he has sworn. Judge his faith by the field and not by my tongue. He makes no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from you, and our tablet stands. The sixty shekels are all the gold he promises, and he asks that our envoys pass freely.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: Karduniash strikes Ekallatum and Arbela in this eighth season together with Mitanni's blow at Terqa, and strikes every season after; no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from Mitanni. No more gold promised; no province ceded; no other treaty spoken of.

value.speech: Great King Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, my lord's brother: may Amun keep you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. My lord Ashur-uballit has sealed his tablet and sent me across to you. Since then Mitanni has broken its sealed peace and taken Nineveh, and Babylon, which broke its own oath, marches on Arbela and Ekallatum; Assyria stands and holds. As you said, gold follows when friendship is proven, so he asks you as a brother to send gold now, as much as your house can spare, that Assyria may keep its armies in the field. He asks too that you watch Damascus and Qadesh, held by Babylon, for that would serve us both. In return Assyria will warn Egypt of the moves of Babylon and Mitanni. Send your envoys to my lord with word of your wishes.

Great King Suppiluliuma, my lord the King of Alashiya sends me to you with these words. The peace sealed between you stands, and Cyprus keeps it; may your household, your sons, your chariots and your country prosper, and may the drought pass. He sends no gold, for plague has cut his income as drought has cut yours. In friendship he tells you that Egypt has taken Byblos and Tyre and keeps ships in the Cilician, Great Green and Levantine seas, one of them lying in the Cilician Sea beside Kizzuwatna and Lukka, and that a king who grows by taking walled cities will not stop at one. He will send you word the moment Egypt's ships move toward Kizzuwatna, and he asks the same of you for Cyprus. He asks that Hatti keep its ships out of his waters as sealed, for a move into a sea zone supported by a second ship is strength two against one, and he bids you remember it should Egypt's ship in the Cilician Sea grow bold.

To my brother of Alashiya: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our peace stands and Hatti keeps it; my ships will not enter your waters. I thank you for the warning about Egypt's ship in the Cilician Sea and I ask the same word from you the moment Egyptian ships move on Kizzuwatna or Lukka. I send no gold, for the drought has emptied my house as plague has yours. May the hand of Nergal pass from Cyprus and Teshub from Hatti.

Ammistamru, tell my brother Ashur-uballit that Egypt wishes health to his house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our tablet stands: friendship, open roads, no joining of an enemy against the other. I grieve at the war on his borders. My treasury is bound this season by my own armies and I send no gold now; when his friendship is shown in deeds, my hand will open. Damascus is Egypt's and in my keeping, and I watch the south and the road to Qadesh as my own concern. Let him send me word of every move of Babylon and Mitanni, and I will weigh it as a brother.

Great King Napkhururiya, my lord's brother, I hear your word and will carry it faithfully to Ashur-uballit. I grieve with you at the war upon our borders, and I understand that your treasury is bound this season by your own armies; my lord will know that Egypt's hand opens when friendship is shown in deeds. Assyria holds to the tablet: friendship, open roads, and no joining of an enemy against Egypt. Damascus in Egypt's keeping is noted, and my lord will send you word of every move of Babylon and Mitanni as it comes to him. Assyria will send its envoys across to you as before.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: Assyria will warn Egypt of the moves of Babylon and Mitanni as they become known; friendship, open roads and the exchange of envoys continue. No troops, no gold and no cession of land are promised.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, my lord the King of Alashiya hears your words with gladness. The tablet sealed between you stands, and Cyprus keeps the peace as it was sealed. My lord agrees to send you word of Egyptian fleets as they move, as you have asked. May your household, sons, chariots and country prosper, and may the hand of Nergal pass from Cyprus as you bid. I will carry your answer back to my lord as you have spoken it.
value.commitments: Alashiya will send Hatti word of Egyptian fleets as they move toward Kizzuwatna or Lukka.

value.speech: Great King Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, my brother: my lord of Alashiya greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. The hand of Nergal lies on Cyprus, and plague has cut his income by a quarter for two seasons, so the first shipment of copper is small: twenty shekels of true gold, with more when the plague lifts. He asks you to seal the tablet he sends, by which he leaves Byblos, Tyre, Gaza and Megiddo to you, and asks only that your ships and armies leave Tamassos and Enkomi in peace, as brothers do. Cyprus holds sealed peace with Hatti and Arzawa and wishes the same with Egypt. As a brother he also warns you that Babylon has grown fat on Damascus, Qadesh, Mari and Amurru, cities behind weak walls, and is a rival to us both.

Paser, tell my brother of Alashiya that Egypt wishes health to his house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I grieve that the hand of Nergal lies on Cyprus, and I thank him for the twenty shekels. Egypt remembers its brother. My scribes will study his tablet and I will answer by my own envoy. Send the copper when the plague lifts, and Egypt will remember it.

Great King Napkhururiya, my brother, I will carry your health and your greetings to my lord and to his house, his wives, sons, chariots, horses and ships. He thanks you for your word on the twenty shekels, and his copper will follow when the plague lifts, as far as the plague allows. I beg your scribes to study his tablet swiftly, for the sea-captains of Alashiya have waited long at Egypt's gate and so have I. Let Egypt remember its brother, and let its envoy not be forgotten at his lord's court.
value.commitments: Copper to follow when the plague lifts, as far as the plague allows; no land, units, fleet or army promised, and no gold pledged beyond the twenty shekels already sent.

orders.letter: Brother, Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I hold Seha, Apasa, Mira and Lukka, and Ugarit by purchase with its walls. Your ships lie in the Cilician and Syrian seas close to my coast, and I wish only peace between us. Seal the tablet I send: neither of us will send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought, and our envoys pass freely. I send twenty shekels of gold as a token of respect.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet as written. May also name Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus, Megiddo and the other lands Egypt holds as Egypt's, and promise free passage for Egyptian envoys. May not promise war, troops, ships or any gold beyond what is carried.

proposal.text: Egypt and Arzawa, brothers before Amun, Teshub and Shamash: neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought. Arzawa holds Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Ugarit. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T8: Refused Hatti's tablet (omits Ugarit; likely a trick to claim Ugarit later). k1 ends T8, so from T9 I may strike. Scheduled T8 raise army in seha stands (runs; I gave no extra raise). Renewed c12 Mazipalali at 27 (term 8) and sent him to Egypt (2 seasons each way, arrives T10, home about T12) with 20 gold and a no-attack tablet naming Lukka and Ugarit as mine; Egypt fleets in cilicia and syriansea are both adjacent to Ugarit (walls hold 1) and could take it. Did not answer Hatti further; they think my Lukka army stays quiet. T9 PLAN: read c11 spy report on Tuwanuwa/Hattusa/Kanesh/Kizzuwatna. If Tuwanuwa hold is 2 (army + Kizzuwatna support) and nothing else adjacent can support it (Hattusa, Kanesh), order mira->tuwanuwa with seha (new army) and lukka supporting the move: strength 3. Dislodged Hatti army is destroyed. Check that no Hatti unit can attack lukka or seha to cut supports. Must override the scheduled T9 hold-supports (mira/lukka) by giving units orders at T9. Hatti may then hit Ugarit from Carchemish/Kizzuwatna; accept. Keep treasury above 100. Wake every turn.
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu, capital apasa. Start strength 1300; T8 ledger strength 1925 (1.48). Holdings: apasa, seha, mira, lukka (army), ugarit (bought T4, walls, no troops inside). Yield 165; income 165, upkeep 60 for armies mira and lukka (third army raised in seha T8, upkeep 90 from T9), wages about 20-40. No free cities remain; Babylonia (yield 315) and Egypt (310) lead on growth, so I must conquer Hatti (drought, thin treasury) to win. Pacts: k1 Hatti (no army into the other's homeland) ends T8; k17/k24 Alashiya (brothers, no attack on each other's lands or bought cities; I will not bid for Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus). Hatti (Suppiluliuma) offered a tablet naming Isuwa and Carchemish as his and Lukka as mine but not Ugarit; I refused to seal. Hatti armies seen: tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, carchemish. Spy c11 watches Tuwanuwa (sees hattusa, kanesh, kizzuwatna). Plan: T9 strike Tuwanuwa (mira->tuwanuwa, seha and lukka supporting) if hold is 2 or less, later Kizzuwatna for Ugarit's safety. c12 Mazipalali (27 a season) went to Egypt T8 with 20 gold and a non-aggression tablet. Artessupa (c9) is a free candidate asking 22. Egypt fleets sit in cilicia and syriansea next to Ugarit and Lukka.

ledger.entry: T2 sealed k1 (no army into the other's homeland, to T8). T8: Pirissi brought a Hatti-sealed tablet (6 seasons; Hatti Isuwa, Carchemish; mine Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka but NOT Ugarit). I did NOT seal; asked them to name Ugarit. Mazipalali had told Hatti my Lukka army stays quiet; I never swore it. Hatti thin treasury, drought. Plan: strike Tuwanuwa T9 if weak (mira->tuwanuwa, seha+lukka support). Ugarit walls hold 1: exposed to Carchemish+Kizzuwatna.

T4 sealed k17 and k24. T7: Alashiya refused the ship clause; would seal a tablet without it plus my word to leave Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus. Not resent (skipped T8 as redundant). My promise not to bid Amurru kept. I owe them news if Egypt or Hatti move on Tamassos or Enkomi.

T8: sent c12 Mazipalali with 20 gold and a tablet to seal: neither sends army or fleet against the other's lands or bought cities (mine Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka, Ugarit); envoys pass freely. Arrives T10, home about T12. Egypt fleets in cilicia and syriansea are adjacent to Ugarit and Lukka. No answer yet.

value.notes: T8: Treasury 6, no envoy at court (c13 Hatti, c14 Egypt, both back about T9), so no letters this season. Egypt fleets now sit at cilicia, syriansea and levantsea, all next to Enkomi. Three fleets can take Enkomi (one moves, two support: 3 v my hold 2). I cannot add a third defender: no gold, no empty province, no fleet. Best I can do is mutual hold-support (enkomi supports tamassos, tamassos supports enkomi) and hope Paser's tablet and 20 gold at Egypt's court (audience T8) buy peace. If Enkomi falls I am woken: then hold Tamassos with support from nothing, ask Hatti and Arzawa to move on Egypt's fleets, and consider ceding nothing. Money: T8 income 64, upkeep 60, so treasury about 10 after T8; income 85 from T9; two armies 60 plus wages 21 leaves about +4 a season. At T9: Paser's term ends (13 a season); decide renew or let go, and think about dropping one envoy to save wages. Cannot afford anything else. Idea for later: disband one army if Egypt makes peace; gold counts 1:1 in strength. Schedule: mutual hold-supports T9-T22 as fallback; I wake T9 anyway when envoys return.
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). T2: k8 with Hatti (no army/fleet against each other's lands or bought cities). Egypt tried to land at Tamassos T2 and T3, bounced off my mutual hold-support. T4: k16 and k25 with Arzawa (peace, neither bids for the other's cities, envoys pass freely). T5: Babylon's Tattamaru agreed in words that Amurru was mine, nothing sealed. T6: Egypt took Tyre then Byblos (walls fell 2v1). Arzawa bought Ugarit, sent 25 gold (g1, true weight), refused my 100 gold gift, no force of his touches my lands. Hatti pleads drought. Plague destroyed my fleet at Enkomi. T7: no free city remains (Babylon holds Amurru, Damascus, Qadesh, Mari, Susa; Egypt Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus; Arzawa Ugarit, Lukka). I hold Enkomi (capital 45) and Tamassos (40), yield 85, two armies (upkeep 60), one in each. Sent Paser (c14) to Egypt with a tablet (Egypt keeps Byblos/Tyre/Gaza/Megiddo, no force against Tamassos/Enkomi, copper later) and 20 gold; sent Ili-iddina (c13) to Hatti with a warning about Egypt's fleets, no gold. T8: Egypt fleets at cilicia, syriansea, levantsea, all next to Enkomi, 3 can crack my 2 mutual-support armies. Treasury 6. Strength = 10 x yield + gold - back pay; gold counts 1:1; nothing left to buy, only conquest grows. Standing: leaders Arzawa, Egypt, Babylon about 1.6; I am 0.70-1.0. Envoys: c13 Ili-iddina (8 a season, term T13), c14 Paser (13, term T9). Letters cannot be scheduled, only orders for units; I can send letters only when awake.

ledger.entry: T8: Egypt took Byblos (T6) despite my T5 tablet; holds Tyre, Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus; fleets at cilicia, syriansea, levantsea all next to Enkomi (3 fleets can crack my 2 armies). Paser reaches its court T8 with tablet (Egypt keeps Byblos/Tyre/Gaza/Megiddo; no force against Tamassos/Enkomi; copper later) and 20 gold as first copper. Nothing sealed or paid before that. Distrust: they may strike Enkomi.

value.notes: T8: Sealed k37 with Mitanni (peace to T16). No envoy at court, so no letters. Scheduled raise army at KANESH runs (158 -> 58 gold). Held posture: carchemish supports isuwa, kizzuwatna supports tuwanuwa. Harran stood EMPTY at T8 (Mitanni army went harran->terqa), washukanni has one army; I do not touch it while k37 stands. T9 (I wake): Pirissi (c4) home from Arzawa - read whether Arzawa sealed my clay (homelands, my Isuwa/Carchemish, their Seha/Apasa/Mira/Lukka, Ugarit NOT named). UGARIT STRIKE: kizzuwatna -> ugarit, carchemish supports (2 v walls 1); kanesh army -> kizzuwatna; a second new army (raise at HATTUSA at T9) supports tuwanuwa hold at T10 so lukka+mira (2) bounce on 2. Prefer T10 for full cover; strike T9 only if Arzawa sealed and looks passive. Supporter at carchemish is safer than at kizzuwatna (Egypt fleet in cilicia or Lukka could cut it). After Ugarit: consider Harran, but send word to Mitanni by envoy first (k37 clause), around T12-T14. Assyria: told nothing of k37; their T10-T12 joint ops replaced by holds. Keep treasury above upkeep (6 armies = 180).
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100 (yield 180, 300 gold). T2 took Isuwa; T5 took Carchemish by force. Drought T4-T6 halved income. T8: 7 provinces (hattusa, tuwanuwa, sapinuwa, kanesh, kizzuwatna, carchemish, isuwa), yield 245, income 245, upkeep 120 (armies in carchemish, isuwa, kizzuwatna, tuwanuwa), strength 2589 (1.23). TREATIES: k4 Alashiya (brothers, no attack on lands or bought cities); k5 Arzawa (homelands, ends about T8); k9 Egypt (homelands safe; I send no troops to Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh); k30 Babylonia (homelands and provinces held on T5, no bids); k33 Assyria (T7 pact against Mitanni, I am not honoring the T10-T12 ops); k37 Mitanni (T8, peace to T16, Carchemish and Isuwa are Hatti's, homelands safe, word by envoy before ending it). World T8: Arzawa 1.65 (apasa, seha, mira, lukka army, ugarit walls), Egypt 1.63 (took Byblos, Tyre, fleet in cilicia), Babylonia 1.62 (315 yield: amurru, mari, qadesh walls, susa), Hatti 1.36, Mitanni 1.24 (harran empty, washukanni army), Alashiya 1.00, Assyria 0.74. Alashiya promised word of Egyptian fleets moving on Kizzuwatna or Lukka. Envoys: c3 Keliya to Egypt (arrives T9, back T11), c4 Pirissi to Arzawa (back T9). PLAN: army at kanesh (T8), army at hattusa (T9), then Ugarit strike T9/T10, then Lukka/Harran by conquest; no free cities left to buy.

ledger.entry: T8: Ubaru brought a tablet already sealed by Mitanni; I SEALED k37: peace to turn 16, homelands safe, Carchemish and Isuwa named Hatti's, envoys pass freely, mutual warning about Karduniash. No gold paid. Supersedes k20. Bars my armies from Harran, Washukanni, Taidu, Terqa, Nineveh and conflicts with Assyria pact k33. Word by envoy must go first before I end it. Plan: shield flank during the Ugarit strike; maybe take Harran about T12-T14 after giving word.

T7: sealed k33 (Washukanni, Taidu to Assyria; Harran, Carchemish, Isuwa to Hatti; no peace with Mitanni without word). T8: I sealed peace k37 with Mitanni WITHOUT telling Assyria: breach if shown. Do not show k13, k20 or k37. I scrapped my T10-T12 supports for Assyria's attack. Assyria is weak (0.74) and far, and gains more than I from Mitanni's fall; let it fight Mitanni alone. Send no word unless asked.

value.notes: T8 plan. Strength 3323 (1.33), gold 304. Real growth needs conquest: each yield y gives +10y strength and +y gold a season. T8 orders explicit: damascus army -> qadesh (byblos army supports, 2 v walls 1); tyre -> damascus; gaza -> tyre; fleet levantsea -> enkomi with cilicia and syriansea fleets supporting (3 v army 1 + tamassos support 1 = 2). The old scheduled T8 fleet supports were mis-named, so I replaced every unit's T8 order. T9 schedule kept: qadesh army -> mari (damascus army supports; Babylon at sippar could support mari walls and tie, then just bounce, no loss); byblos army -> amurru (syriansea fleet supports); cilicia fleet -> tamassos (enkomi fleet supports); gaza-army on to byblos. T10 schedule: amurru army -> ugarit with syriansea fleet supporting. Decide ugarit at T10: Hatti asked me to stay out and has an army at kizzuwatna beside it; if I take it, keep fleet and army support. If T8 enkomi fails, fix T9 fleet orders. After the last conquest disband spare units (army 30, fleet 35) and bank gold; keep a fleet in each Cyprus city only if Arzawa or Hatti fleets threaten. Envoys: sent none, no gold; never seal anything naming Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, or Alashiya's tablet. c1 and c2 due back T9; c2 (Assyrian-born, owed 42) will probably leave: let him unless useful. Wake every turn (wake_in_turn 9).
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya). Start strength 2500, treasury 600. T8: strength 3323 (1.33), gold 304, yield 310, income 310, upkeep 225 (4 armies, 3 fleets), wages 43. Conquest is my path; every free city is gone, targets are walled cities bought by others (Qadesh, Amurru, Mari: Babylon; Ugarit: Arzawa) and Alashiya's Enkomi and Tamassos. Conquered provinces stay mine without a garrison. Walls hold 1: mover plus one support wins 2 v 1, but another king's unit adjacent may support the walls and tie. Babylon cannot station troops in its walled cities and has no coast, so it cannot reach my northern provinces by land; Hatti (carchemish, kizzuwatna) and Arzawa (lukka, seha fleet) could. Held: akhetaten, byblos, damascus, delta, gaza, megiddo, memphis, sinai, thebes, tyre. Campaign: qadesh + enkomi T8; mari + amurru + tamassos T9; ugarit T10 (decide). Then disband spare units and bank gold; keep waking each turn. Treaties: k11 Assyria (friendship, receive envoys, join no enemy), k18 Hatti (peace, southern cities in Egypt's sphere), k19 Mitanni (same), k32 Mitanni brotherhood (word at once if a third king moves on a homeland; I sent 25 gold). Babylonia: nothing sealed, I refuse any tablet naming Mari, Qadesh, Damascus or Susa as theirs. Alashiya: never seal. People: c1 Mane (13, term T11, due T9), c2 Ashur-nadin (14, term T8, due T9, owed 42, may leave), c17 (16, term T8). Unassayed gold g2 (40 Babylonia) and g4 (20 Alashiya) not assayed.

ledger.entry: T6: Paser brought a peace tablet; I did NOT seal, sent no gold. T8: Paser again, plague cut income, brought 20 shekels (purity unassayed) and a tablet leaving Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Megiddo to Egypt in exchange for Tamassos and Enkomi left in peace. I did NOT seal, sent no gold, gave warm words, promised an answer by my own envoy (no obligation). Never seal: my fleets strike Enkomi T8 and Tamassos T9.

value.notes: T8: Terqa taken T7 (Assyria terqa army destroyed). Kidin-Adad swears Babylon strikes Ekallatum+Arbela THIS season (joint blow); Babylon did hit Arbela from Susa in T7 (bounced), so it is not empty talk. I use the moment: terqa -> ashur, nineveh supports it, taidu supports nineveh holding (hold 2 vs arbela+ashur 2 = bounce), washukanni holds (capital: only isuwa touches it, 1v1 bounces). If Babylon's blows cut arbela/ekallatum supports, Ashur (hold 1) falls to my 2. If Assyria supports Ashur, I bounce at no cost. Only bad case: nineveh support cut by arbela AND ashur+ekallatum hit terqa with 2 (unlikely). Raised an army in harran (empty; levy happens after movement, so if Hatti walks in nothing is raised or paid). k12 (Hatti homelands) ends about T10; Ubaru (c7) is at Hatti with a peace to T16, back about T9; c8 back from Egypt about T9. T9 PLAN: read results. If Ashur is mine: harran army -> terqa to refill, keep nineveh supported. If bounced: keep the defence (terqa supported by washukanni, nineveh by taidu, harran army holds), try again when Babylon's strikes land. Do not feed Babylon (leader): never support its moves into Arbela/Ekallatum unless it clears Ashur's way. Never reveal k15/k22 or the Hatti peace to Babylon.
value.summary: Tushratta of Mitanni, start 1950, strength about 1947 at T8 (growth 1.00; Babylon, Egypt, Arzawa lead about 1.6 by yield; I must conquer, all free cities are taken). Hold harran (empty, army raised T8 if not entered), washukanni (capital), taidu, terqa (taken T7 from Assyria), nineveh (taken T5; I broke k15/k22 secretly, Babylon must never learn). Armies: washukanni, taidu, terqa, nineveh (+harran T8). Income 180, upkeep 120-150, wages 16. Tablets: k3/k31 Babylon (joint war on Assyria, no separate peace; Terqa, Ashur, Nineveh to me; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa to Babylon; Isuwa/Carchemish mine on paper, Mari his), k10 Egypt (no Mitanni troops in Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh), k12 Hatti homelands peace to about T10; k21 broken by Hatti (took Carchemish T5); c7 carries a Hatti peace to T16 conceding Carchemish/Isuwa. Geometry: only terqa and nineveh touch Ashur (max attack 2); Assyria defends Ashur with arbela/ekallatum supports, so I need Babylon to cut them. Isuwa needs 3 (only harran and washukanni touch it) so Hatti's forward armies cannot be broken yet. Defence rules: terqa needs washukanni support vs ashur+ekallatum; nineveh needs taidu support vs arbela+ashur; harran needs washukanni support vs isuwa+carchemish. Plan: take Ashur, then Ekallatum and Arbela before Babylon does, then turn on Babylon (the leader). c18 Ehli-Teshub free, asked 22 (not hired). c3 Keliya is Hatti's envoy.

ledger.entry: T8: Kidin-Adad (c6) brought 60 shekels (weight true, purity unassayed) and swore Babylon strikes Ekallatum/Arbela THIS season and every season, no more gold promised. I told him Terqa is mine and I press Ashur; sent no gold back. k31 stands (Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh mine; Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa his). Never let it learn of k15/k22 or the Hatti peace. It is the leader: watch it, topple it after Assyria.

T8: I broke k15/k22 (T5, took Nineveh) and took Terqa T7 (their army there destroyed). At war under k31; they hold arbela, ashur, ekallatum with one army each. T8 I strike Ashur from Terqa with Nineveh's support. No envoy contact; expect counter-strikes on Terqa/Nineveh.

orders.letter: Tushratta, my brother, Burna-Buriash of Karduniash greets you. I honour what you did: Terqa is yours and the Assyrian army there is destroyed, as you swore. The tablet of the sixth turn stands. The armies left to Ashur-uballit at Arbela, Ekallatum and, I think, Ashur hold only by supporting one another, and a support is cut when its giver is attacked. So strike all three together in the coming season. Your army at Terqa supports my army from Durkurigalzu into Ekallatum, so that mine has three against their two. Your army at Nineveh strikes Ashur and cuts its support. My army from Susa strikes Arbela. Ekallatum and Arbela are mine, Ashur is yours. Hatti's army still stands in Carchemish; my watchmen at Qadesh see it. Send word of your orders each season and I will match you.
orders.mandate: Agree to the timing and to who supports whom, and seal the tablet. Promise no gold and no land beyond the tablet of turn 6. Say nothing of Hatti beyond what the message says.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni, Great Kings and brothers, confirm the tablet of turn 6 and strike Assyria together in turn 9: Mitanni's army at Terqa supports Karduniash's army from Durkurigalzu into Ekallatum; Mitanni's army at Nineveh strikes Ashur; Karduniash's army from Susa strikes Arbela. Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh are Mitanni's; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa are Karduniash's. Neither marches against the other's share. The roads stay open.

value.notes: T8 plan. Repeat the strike: durkurigalzu->ekallatum, sippar supports it, susa->arbela (cuts Arbela's support), nippur->durkurigalzu. Mitanni kept its word at T7 (Terqa taken, Assyrian army there destroyed), so I expect them to hit Ashur now; if Ashur's support is cut, Ekallatum falls to my 2 against 1. Mari holds 1 this season (sippar is busy); Egypt's lone army at Damascus cannot take it without a second adjacent unit. If Egypt takes Qadesh, T9 put sippar back on 'supports mari holding'. Sent c18 Ehli-Teshub (Carchemish-born, new, no gold) to Mitanni with a tablet: T9 joint strike, Terqa supports dk->ekallatum (3 v 2), Nineveh->ashur cuts Ashur's support, susa->arbela. Wake T9: read battle; c6 returns T9 with Mitanni's answer. Ideas then: send c6 to Hatti asking Carchemish army to support Qadesh walls holding (Egypt has only byblos+damascus next to Qadesh, so +1 makes it safe), or to Arzawa for the non-aggression tablet. c15 back T10 with Egypt's answer on the k26 mirror. c5 reaches Alashiya T9, back T11. Sought candidates: hire at T9 if a decent envoy asks 15 or less. Never tell Mitanni of k26, nor Hatti of k28.
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start 2600, ledger 3652 at T8 (1.40; land yield 315). Land: homeland five plus Susa (army) plus bought walled Mari, Qadesh, Amurru (they hold no troops of mine; only treaty and a supporting army protect them). Damascus was lost to Egypt at T7 (Egypt armies at Damascus, Byblos, Tyre, fleet in Syrian Sea). Armies: sippar, durkurigalzu, nippur, susa. Tablets: k6 Assyria (broken by me), k7 Mitanni (Isuwa/Carchemish theirs, Mari mine), k26 Hatti T5 (no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on T5: Mari, Qadesh, Susa; Carchemish and Isuwa are Hatti's), k28 Mitanni T6 (joint war on Assyria: Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh Mitanni, Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa me, no separate peace). Mitanni took Terqa at T7 as promised. Assyria has armies in arbela, ekallatum and probably ashur, supporting each other; my 2-strength strikes on Ekallatum bounced at T5, T6, T7. Only Sippar/Dk touch Ekallatum, only Susa touches Arbela. Any attack on a unit cuts the support it gives, so Mitanni hitting Ashur while I hit Ekallatum and Arbela breaks the triangle. Envoys: c5 (Alashiya, tablet of non-aggression, back T11), c6 reliable (Mitanni, back T9), c15 (Egypt with k26 mirror and 40 gold, back T10), c18 (Carchemish-born, sent to Mitanni T8). Arzawa (growth 1.65, holds Ugarit) not yet contacted. Egypt is the real threat to my Levant cities and the rival for growth. Never tell Mitanni about k26 or Hatti about k28.

ledger.entry: T8: Egypt took Damascus at T7 (tyre->damascus, byblos supporting) despite my spoken peace; armies at Damascus, Byblos, Tyre, fleet in Syrian Sea. c15 reaches Egypt T8 with my mirror of k26 (no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on sealing day: covers Mari, Qadesh, Amurru) plus 40 gold, back T10. T5 clay naming Damascus/Byblos/Amurru Egypt's sphere NOT sealed. Qadesh and Amurru are open to a 2-army strike; I cannot garrison them.

T8: Mitanni kept its word: Harran->Terqa T7 took Terqa and destroyed the Assyrian army. k28 stands. Sent c18 with sealed-tablet text for a joint strike at T9 (Terqa supports my dk->ekallatum, Nineveh strikes Ashur, my susa->arbela). No gold this time (60 went with c6 at T7, arrives T8). c6 returns T9 with their answer. They want a watch on Hatti: Hatti army stands at Carchemish. Told them nothing of k26.

T8: hostile, at war under k28. Armies seen at arbela and ekallatum, probably ashur too (3 left; the Terqa army died T7). They bounce my Ekallatum strikes 2v2 with arbela->ekallatum supported by ashur. Expect Ekallatum->Mari or an attempt on Terqa. Goal: take Ekallatum and Arbela, leave Ashur to Mitanni.

value.notes: T8: Lost Terqa (Mitanni harran->terqa with washukanni support) and my terqa army. Mitanni armies now at terqa and nineveh, both next to Ashur; a taidu army probably supports nineveh (hold 2). Babylon: susa, sippar, durkurigalzu, nippur armies; pattern T5-T7 susa->arbela (1) and sippar/durk->ekallatum (2). Money: income 100, upkeep 90, so staff wages (c10 14, c16 11) put me in deficit once they sit at court; treasury 20. Do not hire anyone. T8 orders: ashur and ekallatum support each other holding (mutual hold-support, a support-order unit still holds at 1 plus supports); arbela attacks nineveh only to cut nineveh's support if Mitanni sends terqa->ashur with nineveh support (then terqa->ashur is 1 v 1). Known weak spot: Babylon's attacks cut arbela's and ekallatum's supports, so Mitanni 2-strength on ashur with nineveh->ashur backed by terqa is the case I cannot stop. At T9 (wake set): c10 Yanhamu should be home with Hatti's answer (Hatti took Carchemish and Isuwa from Mitanni, so it is Mitanni's enemy). Revise the T10 strike (Terqa army is gone). Idea: send c10 back to Hatti or to Mitanni/Babylon with a peace offer; show k14/k23 as proof Mitanni broke its seals. c16 due home T10 from Egypt: read whether gold is coming.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria, start strength 1700 (yield 135). T1 took Terqa, bought Susa; Babylon broke k2 at once and took Susa. T4 k14/k23 with Mitanni, broken T5 (taidu->nineveh); Mitanni holds Nineveh (probably Taidu army supporting). T4 k27 with Egypt (friendship; Egypt promised gold, never sent; Egypt says it takes Damascus and Qadesh, leaves Mari/Susa to me). Hatti (c10, T5) will stand with me against Mitanni; Hatti now holds Carchemish and Isuwa. T7 my Mari raid failed (walls 1 v 1, terqa support void), Mitanni took Terqa and destroyed my Terqa army. I now hold only arbela, ashur (capital), ekallatum, one army each, all adjacent to each other. Income 100, upkeep 90: no spare gold, cannot afford staff wages. Babylon (runaway leader at 1.62, armies at susa, sippar, durkurigalzu, nippur) attacks arbela from susa (1) and ekallatum from sippar+durk (2) each season; Mitanni armies at terqa and nineveh both touch ashur. Rules learned: dislodged unit is destroyed; failed move leaves unit at home with strength 1; support cut by any attack except from the province supported into; supporting unit still holds at 1 plus hold-supports. c10 Yanhamu home T9 (Hatti answer), c16 Ammistamru home T10 (Egypt answer); c13 Ili-iddina is secretly in my pay in Babylon. Need help from Hatti/Egypt or a peace with Mitanni or Babylon to survive.

ledger.entry: T4 sealed k14 and k23; Mitanni BROKE both T5 (taidu->nineveh) and T7 took Terqa (harran->terqa) and destroyed my army there. I owe nothing. Mitanni armies at nineveh and terqa both touch Ashur. Hatti is its enemy (took Carchemish/Isuwa).

T2 k2 broken by Babylon (took Susa). T5-T7 Babylon attacked arbela (susa) and ekallatum (sippar+durk) every season; all bounced. T7 my Mari raid failed. Trust nothing. Nothing owed. c13 Ili-iddina in my pay in Babylon.

value.text: My lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, I, Haamashshi, report from Tuwanuwa as follows. Hatti has an army in Kanesh. Arzawa has an army in Mira. Hatti has an army in Tuwanuwa, and I have kept myself quiet as you commanded. Send my wages with the trusted messenger who carries this, for I am your servant and I wait for them.

Great King Burna-Buriash, I am Paser, born in Memphis, once a copper trader and since the first season envoy to the court of Egypt for the Great King of Alashiya. I have stood before the kings of Egypt, carried their words back faithfully, and I know the houses of the sea-roads that bring copper to your land. I seek a place where a clear eye and a bold tongue may serve a great king's favour, and I ask a wage fitting to my experience.

My lord, I went to the court of Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, and gave him your words as you bade me. He received me kindly and sealed his answer in friendship: the peace stands, Hatti keeps it, and his ships will not enter your waters. He sends no gold, for the drought has emptied his house as plague has emptied yours. He thanks you for the warning about Egypt's ship in the Cilician Sea and asks that you send him word the moment Egyptian ships move on Kizzuwatna or Lukka. I answered in your name that you agree to send word of Egyptian fleets as they move, and I have carried his words home to you as he spoke them.

My lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, I have come home from the court of Great King Ashur-uballit of Assyria. I gave him your greeting and your words as you spoke them: that Egypt keeps the friendship sealed, that Babylonia has bought Mari, Susa, Qadesh and Damascus, and that Egypt will take Damascus and Qadesh from the south. He received them gladly and said that Babylon must look west if Egypt moves, and that he will hold his own border against it. He asks that you send gold in good pure weight with the next envoy, and word of the day Egypt moves, so that Assyria may strike together with you. He has sent his envoy Ammistamru and another, c16, to your court on this matter. I promised him no gold, no troops and no day of marching, for those matters lie with you alone. I bring no gold and no new tablet, only his words. At his court I saw 4 army and no fleet near the capital, and the treasury looks thin, so his request for gold may be more need than courtesy.

I am Artessupa, born in Washukanni, once a physician and since then a royal messenger known at more than one court. I have carried the tablets of Ashur-uballit to your father's house and to the court of Mitanni, and I have brought back each answer without alteration, so I know the road to Karduniash and the frontier of Ekallatum and Sippar as well as any man living. I can tend the sick and read a man's face, and I am bold enough to carry hard words to any court when my lord requires it. If my lord Burna-Buriash will employ me, I will serve his house faithfully and hope in time to be trusted with greater charge.

I, Mazipalali of Harran, served Tarhundaradu of Arzawa at 27 shekels a season; he still owes me 27 shekels of back pay, payable when I return to his court. In seasons 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 I carried his words to Suppiluliuma of Hatti: sealed peace, no armies across the border, Lukka held by Arzawa, and Egypt's fleet feared on the Great Green. Arzawa paid me 18 shekels in season 3 and again in season 6. Hatti's harvest failed or ran thin in seasons 4 and 5, and Suppiluliuma received me well both times. Secrets: I owe 120 shekels to an Alashiyan trader and keep a lover in Ugarit. I want gold enough to never serve again.

My lord Suppiluliuma, Great King, I came before King Tarhundaradu of Arzawa and laid your greeting and your tablet before him as you bade me. He thanks you for your clay and for the keeping of our peace, but he will not seal the tablet as it stands, since it names Lukka as his land and leaves out Ugarit, which he says he bought and holds with its walls. He asks that a new tablet list Ugarit among the lands of Arzawa, beside Seha, Apasa, Mira and Lukka, and then he will weigh it gladly. I answered that I have no charge to write Ugarit or any other city into a tablet, and that I would carry his word home exactly as he spoke it. He bids the envoys of Hatti always be received at his court. I bring back your tablet unsealed, and I noticed that Arzawa keeps two bands of army and no fleet near its capital. I await your command, my lord.

To my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, from your servant Ubaru of Sippar: I came before Great King Suppiluliuma of Hatti and gave him your word as you spoke it. He was pleased and sealed your tablet: peace until turn 16, Carchemish and Isuwa as Hatti's, Harran, Washukanni, Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh as yours, and our envoys to pass freely. He will watch the Euphrates and Syria as Karduniash grows, and on your behalf I have bound you to warn him should your armies move toward the Euphrates or Syria. I bring the sealed tablet home with joy. At Hatti's court I saw four companies of army near the capital and no fleet at all. May Shamash keep you and your house in health. I ask that the eight shekels of back pay owed me be counted out when I stand before you.

To my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, from your servant Mane. I came to the court of Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, and gave him your words as you spoke them: Egypt keeps the tablet he sealed, and Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. He answers that all goes well with him, his household, sons, chariots, horses and country; he keeps the sealed tablet, sends no troops into Egypt's homeland or the cities of its sphere, and is glad Egypt sends none to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. He asks that Egypt's fleet in the Cilician Sea keep clear of the coast of Kizzuwatna, as his fleet will keep clear of Egypt's; this is a matter for my lord to answer, and I could not answer it for him. What I noticed: Hatti keeps 4 army and no fleet near its capital, and its treasury looks thin. Mazipalali, envoy of Arzawa, was also at the court. I await my lord's word.

To my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, from your servant Zitanza. I came before Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, and gave him your words without change: the tablet of brotherhood stands, he is to send word at once if a third king moves against his homeland, and he is asked to send word of his armies in the north and his envoy to your court. He sealed your tablet gladly and sends 25 shekels of good, pure gold, with an inventory sealed by his hand, promising more as the brotherhood proves itself and his treasury allows. I would not lean too hard on his promises of more. On your behalf I committed you to send word of Hatti's armies on your border and of any third king moving against Egypt, and I ask that you honor it. The gold is in my keeping and I will place it before you myself.

My lord, Great King of Alashiya, I have returned in safety from the court of Egypt and give you my report. The king of Egypt thanks you for the twenty shekels, calls you brother, and says Egypt remembers its brother; yet he sealed nothing, and promised only that his scribes will study your tablet and that he will answer by his own envoy, whom he did not name. He grieves for the hand of Nergal on Cyprus and will take your copper when the plague lifts; I promised no more than that, as far as the plague allows. What my eyes saw: Egypt keeps no army and no fleet near its capital, and its court lives in comfort, so its brotherly words are backed by no force at its gate. I beg you, my lord, to pay the thirteen shekels of back pay still owed to me, and to let me serve you at your court, where I have served since the first season.

My lord Burna-Buriash, I have come home from the court of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and I bring you his word. He greets you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses, and says all goes well with him; he has received your word and your sixty shekels, thanks you, and says our tablet stands. Terqa is now his, and his armies stand at Terqa and Nineveh beside Ashur; he will press Ashur as you ask, but Ashur falls only if your blow at Ekallatum and Arbela truly lands in the same season. He bids you name the season of your strike and let him see Ekallatum or Arbela in your hand, and he watches Hatti and will send word if a Hatti army moves. I have answered for you that this present eighth season is the season of our joint blows, that you strike Ekallatum and Arbela as his blow falls on Terqa and every season after as you have sworn, and that you make no peace with Ashur-uballit apart from him; the sixty shekels are all the gold you promise, and he asks that our envoys pass freely. He will judge your faith by the field and not by my tongue, my lord, so see that the field answers. I also ask that the wages still owing to me be made good.

To Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, my lord, from your servant Yanhamu: may Shamash and Ashur keep you, your house, your wives, sons, chariots, horses and land. I came to the court of Hatti and gave your words as you spoke them. King Suppiluliuma heard them, sealed the clay as you wrote it, and says all goes well with him. Hatti takes Carchemish, Isuwa and Harran; Assyria takes Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni. He would not strike on turn 10, as his levies are not yet in place, so the first blow falls on TURN 11: your army from Terqa moves on Washukanni and your army from Nineveh on Taidu, while his army in Isuwa stands and supports Terqa into Washukanni. On TURN 12 your armies at Terqa and Washukanni support his army from Isuwa into Harran. Turn 11 for Washukanni and Taidu, turn 12 for Harran; I said it twice before him. He gave no numbers by word, but says Isuwa holds an army and it will stay. He asks that you make no peace with Tushratta without sending him word, and that you send no army into Isuwa, Carchemish or Harran except on the day agreed. Near his capital I saw 4 army and no fleet, and the treasury looks thin. Mazipalali, envoy of Arzawa, was also at that court. I am home and ask that the 21 shekels of back pay be settled now, as your word was that it would be paid on my return.

value.speech: Great King Napkhururiya, my lord Suppiluliuma greets you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country, and wishes you well. He keeps the tablet we sealed and sends no troops into Egypt's homeland or the cities of its sphere, and he thanks you for the word of Mane that Egypt sends no troops to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. As one brother to another he asks two things: that your fleet in the Cilician Sea keep clear of the coast of Kizzuwatna, as his will keep clear of Egypt's, and that you send such gold as you can spare, for drought has hurt his fields. He tells you also that Burna-Buriash of Karduniash now holds Qadesh, Amurru, Damascus and Mari, which lie in the sphere our tablet names for Egypt; he sends no troops there and will not stand in the way of a brother who takes back what is his.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, my lord Burna-Buriash of Karduniash wishes health to your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. He rejoices that your words came to him through me, and here is his answer on the sealed tablet you asked for. Amurru has come under his rule, and he holds it with Mari, Qadesh and Damascus. He proposes that neither of you send army or fleet against the other's lands, nor bid against one another, and that copper and good gold pass between brothers. I, Tattamaru, your servant, may promise that my lord bids against none of your cities; I lay the tablet before you now and beg that you set your seal to it and send your envoy with your seal.

Tushratta, Great King, my lord Burna-Buriash of Karduniash greets you as his brother and honours what you did: Terqa is yours, and the Assyrian army there is destroyed, as you swore. The tablet of the sixth turn stands. The armies left to Ashur-uballit at Arbela, Ekallatum and, he thinks, Ashur hold only by supporting one another, and a support is cut when its giver is attacked; therefore strike all three together in the coming season. Your army at Terqa supports his army from Durkurigalzu into Ekallatum, so that his has three against their two; your army at Nineveh strikes Ashur and cuts its support; his army from Susa strikes Arbela. Ekallatum and Arbela are his, Ashur is yours. Hatti's army still stands in Carchemish, and his watchmen at Qadesh see it. Send word of your orders each season and he will match you; I am ready to seal the tablet of this agreement at your word.

Keliya, say to my brother Suppiluliuma: Napkhururiya greets him, his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Egypt keeps the tablet sealed between us and sends no troops into the homeland of Hatti, nor to Isuwa, Carchemish or Lukka. My fleet in the Cilician Sea will keep clear of the coast of Kizzuwatna, as his will keep clear of Egypt's. I thank him for his word that he will not stand in the way of a brother who takes back what is his: Qadesh and Damascus already stand under Egypt, as our tablet names them. I have no gold to spare this season, for plague has cut my fields too, and my armies in the north are a cost to me; when my treasury allows, my brother will not be forgotten. Let envoys keep passing between us.

Tattamaru, my brother Burna-Buriash is welcome in my house, and I wish health to his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I set my seal to his tablet: peace and open roads between Karduniash and Alashiya, no army or fleet against each other's lands, no bidding against each other's cities. I will keep it. Hear also what Egypt has done. While my brother's tablet was on the road, Egypt broke its word, took Byblos and Tyre, and now has taken Enkomi by fleet. Egypt holds twelve provinces and grows fat on every neighbour in turn; a king who watches the Great Green burn will find it at his own gate next. A brother's seal is worth most when a brother is in need. I ask my brother for good gold, as much as brothers can spare, so that I may raise troops and hold Tamassos, and I ask that his armies press Egypt's holdings at Damascus, Megiddo and Tyre so that its ships are called home from Cyprus. In return my copper and my roads are his, and I will send word of every Egyptian fleet that moves. Carry my seal home and bring me his answer.

To Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words reached me late and the battle has outrun them. Your army took Ekallatum last season, so the first clause of your tablet is already done, and I will not seal a tablet for a field that is won. The tablet of the sixth turn stands, and my word with it: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh are mine; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa are yours. This season I strike Ashur and will not let go of it. Do this for me, brother: send your Susa army against Arbela once more, so that Ashur-uballit's last support is cut, and keep your army in Ekallatum to hold what you have taken. Do not send it into Ashur or Terqa, for the blow on Ashur needs one hand only. Whatever falls in Arbela is yours. Send me word each season of what your armies did, as I will send you word of mine.

Tushratta, Great King, my brother, I carry your words to my lord with honour. The timing and the division stand as you have set them: the Susa army strikes Arbela once more, the army in Ekallatum holds what is taken, and neither enters Ashur or Terqa. I will seal the tablet of the sixth turn with these words added, and my lord will send word each season of what his armies have done.
value.commitments: On behalf of Burna-Buriash: his Susa army strikes Arbela in the coming season, his army holds Ekallatum and does not enter Ashur or Terqa, and word of each season's deeds is sent to Mitanni. No gold and no land are promised beyond the tablet of the sixth turn.

value.speech: Great King Napkhururiya, I have heard your words and I will carry them to my lord Suppiluliuma exactly as you have spoken them. Hatti keeps the tablet sealed between us and sends no troops against Egypt's homeland or the cities of its sphere; this much I may repeat, and I have no word beyond it to give. May the gods restore your fields after the plague, and may envoys keep passing between our courts.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I hear your word and thank you for setting your seal to my lord's tablet. Peace and open roads between Karduniash and Alashiya, no army or fleet against each other's lands, and no bidding against each other's cities: this I may promise, and I do promise that my lord bids against none of your cities. I will bear your sealed tablet home to my lord Burna-Buriash with all care. Your requests for gold, copper, troops and the matters beyond the tablet are not mine to answer; I will carry them to my lord and bring back his answer. May my brother's favour rest upon his servant Tattamaru.
value.commitments: My lord Burna-Buriash bids against none of Alashiya's cities. Peace and open roads between Karduniash and Alashiya, with no army or fleet against each other's lands and no bidding against each other's cities, as the sealed tablet sets.

orders.letter: To Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: I wish health to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. As you asked, I send word of Egyptian fleets. Three Egyptian fleets, one moving and two supporting, took Enkomi from me last season. Now an Egyptian fleet stands in Enkomi and another in the Cilician Sea, which touches Kizzuwatna and Lukka. Egypt holds twelve provinces and will take Tamassos next, and then your coast is its next gate. I ask you: move your fleet from Kizzuwatna into the Cilician Sea this season. An attack on that fleet cuts the support it gives, and a bounced fleet is not lost. If Arzawa's fleet at Lukka supports yours, the Egyptian ship is destroyed. The peace of our tablet stands: no force of mine will ever touch Hatti. My copper and my roads are yours. Send me your answer by this envoy.
orders.mandate: Ili-iddina may agree that Alashiya and Hatti each send word of Egyptian fleets and act together against Egypt's fleets in the Cilician Sea, and that Alashiya's copper goes to Hatti when the plague lifts. He may not cede land, promise gold I do not have, or promise troops.

value.notes: T9: Treasury 0, one province (Tamassos, 40) and one army. Egypt holds Enkomi (fleet) and Cilicia (fleet); a fleet moving enkomi->tamassos with cilicia's support (2 v my hold 1) can take Tamassos any season, and then my kingdom falls. I cannot raise or buy anything (0 gold, scribe 20 refused). Only hope: allies cut that support. Sent c13 to Hatti (arrives T10, back T11): asked Hatti's fleet at Kizzuwatna to move into the Cilician Sea (an attack cuts the Egyptian fleet's support there, a bounced fleet is not lost; with Arzawa's fleet at Lukka supporting it destroys the ship). No tablet (no gold). Army holds: do NOT move it, a swap with the Egyptian fleet loses. Income 40, upkeep 30, c13 wage 8 (builds as back pay while he is away): about +10 a season while he travels. If Tamassos survives, at T11 read Hatti's answer, then send c13 to Arzawa or Egypt. Paser (c14) left unpaid, 26 back pay still counts against strength.
value.summary: T1: bought Byblos (300). T2: k8 with Hatti (no army/fleet against each other's lands or bought cities). Egypt tried Tamassos T2 and T3, bounced off my mutual hold-support. T4: k16 and k25 with Arzawa (peace, envoys pass freely; Arzawa holds Lukka and Ugarit, I will not bid). T6: Egypt took Tyre then Byblos; plague destroyed my fleet; Arzawa sent 25 gold (true weight), refused my 100 gold gift. T7: no free city is left anywhere (all bought or taken). Sent Paser to Egypt with 20 gold and a tablet (nothing sealed); sent Ili-iddina to Hatti. T8: Egypt took Enkomi with three fleets (move plus two supports) and destroyed my army there. T9: Hatti sealed nothing new but keeps k8 and asked for word of Egyptian fleets near Kizzuwatna and Lukka. Babylon's Tattamaru brought a peace tablet k47 (no force or bidding against each other's homeland or held provinces Mari, Qadesh, Damascus, Amurru, Susa); I sealed it and asked Babylon for gold and for pressure on Egypt: no answer yet. I hold only Tamassos with one army, treasury 0. Strength = 10 x yield + gold - back pay: only conquest by allies or Egypt's mercy can help me. Envoy c13 Ili-iddina (8 a season, term T13) is my only person.

ledger.entry: T9: Egypt broke the peace: fleets from cilicia, syriansea, levantsea took Enkomi (my capital) in T8, destroying my army. Paser's tablet and 20 gold bought nothing; nothing sealed. Egypt has 12 provinces and fleets at enkomi and cilicia that can take Tamassos. Enemy. Seek Hatti, Arzawa, Babylon against it.

T9: k8 stands (sealed T2). Hatti sealed its peace again by Ili-iddina: its ships will not enter my waters. T9: I sent Ili-iddina back with word of Egypt's fleets (enkomi, cilicia) and the request that Hatti's fleet from Kizzuwatna strike the Egyptian fleet in the Cilician Sea. I promised to keep sending word of Egyptian fleets. No gold sent. Distrust but keep the peace.

value.notes: T9: k1 with Hatti ended T8; no pact now (I refused Hatti's tablet that omitted Ugarit). Struck Tuwanuwa: mira->tuwanuwa, seha and lukka support (strength 3). Tuwanuwa hold may be 3 if Kizzuwatna and Kanesh both support (then bounce, nothing lost). Hattusa looked EMPTY on the spy report: if Tuwanuwa falls, T10 consider tuwanuwa->hattusa (capital, yield 50) or Kanesh/Kizzuwatna. Raised a 4th army in apasa (100) for T10. Cancelled scheduled T10-T12 supports (stale). Check T10 report: did mira take tuwanuwa? Did Kizzuwatna hit Lukka? Egypt fleets in cilicia/syriansea threaten Ugarit (walls hold 1) and Lukka; c12 reaches Egypt T10, home about T12. Keep treasury above 100. Wake every turn (wake_in_turn).
value.summary: Arzawa, king Tarhundaradu, capital apasa. Start strength 1300; T9 ledger 1822 (1.40; estimate 1.65). Standings estimate: Egypt 2.03 leads (took Enkomi, Qadesh, fleets in cilicia and syriansea), me 1.65, Babylonia 1.59, Hatti 1.36. Holdings: apasa, seha, mira, lukka, ugarit (bought T4, walls, no troops). Armies in mira, lukka, seha (raised T8); 4th raised in apasa T9. Yield 165, income 165, upkeep 30 per army. No free cities remain, so I must conquer Hatti (drought, thin treasury; armies seen in tuwanuwa, kanesh, kizzuwatna, carchemish; hattusa apparently empty) to beat Egypt. Pacts: k1 Hatti expired T8, none now (I refused Hatti's tablet omitting Ugarit). k17/k24 Alashiya: brothers, no attack on each other's lands or bought cities; I will not bid Byblos, Amurru, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus (all taken now). c12 Mazipalali (27 a season through turn 16) went to Egypt T8 with 20 gold and a no-attack tablet naming Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka, Ugarit; arrives T10, home about T12. c11 Haamashshi (11 a season to turn 13) spies on Tuwanuwa (sees hattusa, kanesh, kizzuwatna). c9 Artessupa free, asks 22. T9: attacked Tuwanuwa with mira, seha and lukka supporting.

ledger.entry: T2 sealed k1 (no army into the other's homeland, to T8), expired. T8 refused Hatti's tablet (omitted Ugarit). T9: I attack Tuwanuwa (mira->tuwanuwa, seha and lukka support). No pact now. Hatti thin treasury, drought; defends Tuwanuwa with Kizzuwatna support.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash of Karduniash greets the king of Arzawa, my brother, his household, sons, chariots, horses and land. Egypt's armies now stand at Qadesh, Byblos and Damascus, next to your Ugarit and my Amurru, and Egypt grows strong. Brothers who share a neighbour should keep peace between themselves. I send forty shekels as a brother's gift and ask you to seal this tablet: we send no army or fleet against each other and do not bid for each other's cities, and each may support the walls of the other's city when a third power attacks it. Let our envoys pass freely.
orders.mandate: Seal a non-aggression tablet and a clause allowing each to support the other's city walls (Amurru, Ugarit). Promise no further gold and no cession of land.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Arzawa, Great Kings and brothers: neither sends army or fleet against the homeland of the other, nor against any province the other holds on the day this tablet is sealed (Karduniash holds Amurru, Mari, Susa, Ekallatum; Arzawa holds Ugarit and Lukka), nor bids for it. Either may support the walls of the other's city holding. Their envoys pass freely.

value.notes: T9 plan. Ekallatum is mine (T8). Assyria has only arbela and ashur armies (2 left). Strike Arbela: susa->arbela, ekallatum supports it (2 v arbela hold 1 + ashur support 1 = tie unless Mitanni hits Ashur, which cuts Ashur's support and Arbela falls; my attack on Arbela cuts Arbela's support to Ashur so Mitanni's terqa/nineveh strike on Ashur should win). dk supports ekallatum holding (2) so arbela->ekallatum with ashur support (2) only bounces. Sippar supports Mari holding (walls 1+1=2 vs Egypt max 2 from qadesh+damascus: tie bounce). Amurru cannot be defended (qadesh+byblos can take it); Arzawa at Ugarit might support its walls: sent c6 to Arzawa with non-aggression tablet text + walls clause and 40 gold, arrives T11, back T13. Raised army in nippur as a reserve (to cover Susa/Arbela later). c18 reaches Mitanni T9, back T10 with answer. c15 back from Egypt T10 with answer on k26 mirror. c5 reaches Alashiya T9, back T11. Wake T10. Never tell Mitanni of k26 nor Hatti of k28. After Assyria falls, Mitanni borders me at Terqa/Mari: watch it. Egypt is the growth leader (2.03): consider urging Hatti/Arzawa against Egypt. Hoard gold: net about +160/season.
value.summary: I am Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start 2600, ledger 3711 at T9 (1.43; land yield 310). Land: homeland five, Susa, Ekallatum (taken T8), bought walled Mari and Amurru (cannot hold my troops; Qadesh was taken by Egypt T8, Damascus T7). Armies: ekallatum, sippar, durkurigalzu, susa; raised a fifth at nippur T9. Tablets: k6 Assyria (broken by me), k7 Mitanni (Isuwa/Carchemish theirs, Mari mine), k26 Hatti T5 (no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on T5; Hatti holds Carchemish/Isuwa), k28 Mitanni T6 (joint war on Assyria: Terqa/Ashur/Nineveh Mitanni, Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa me, no separate peace). Mitanni kept its word (took Terqa, Nineveh; killed Assyrian armies). Assyria now holds only arbela and ashur with 2 armies. Egypt (growth leader 2.03) holds armies qadesh, damascus, byblos, fleet syriansea, took Enkomi; real threat to Mari and Amurru; mirror of k26 sent with c15 (back T10). No free city-states remain to buy; growth must come from Arbela, gold hoard and not losing Mari. Envoys: c5 Alashiya (tablet, back T11), c6 sent to Arzawa T9, c15 Egypt back T10, c18 Mitanni back T10. Never tell Mitanni of k26 nor Hatti of k28.

ledger.entry: T9: Egypt took Qadesh T8 (armies qadesh, damascus, byblos; fleet syriansea; also holds Enkomi). c15 reached Egypt T8 with my mirror of k26 (no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on sealing day: Mari, Amurru) plus 40 gold; back T10. Nothing sealed yet. Mari held by sippar support; Amurru cannot be held.

T9: Mitanni kept its word (Terqa, Nineveh taken; k28 stands). c6 returned T8: Tushratta wants to see Ekallatum or Arbela in my hand; I now hold Ekallatum. c18 reaches Mitanni T9 with the plan for a joint strike on Arbela (me) and Ashur (them); back T10. 60 gold paid at T7. Told them nothing of k26.
T9: at war under k28. Only arbela and ashur armies left. T9 I strike Arbela (susa->arbela, ekallatum supports). Goal: Arbela mine, Ashur to Mitanni.

T9: no contact before. Holds Ugarit, Lukka, Mira, Seha, Apasa (growth 1.65, a rival). Sent c6 at T9 with tablet text: no army/fleet/bid against homeland or provinces held on sealing day, envoys pass freely, may support each other's city walls; 40 gold. Arrives T11, back T13.

orders.letter: Pirissi, say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country, and I wish the same to yours. I thank him for receiving my envoy. Hatti has no quarrel with the homeland of Arzawa, neither with Seha, Apasa nor Mira. I cannot write Ugarit or Lukka into clay, for such coast cities belong to whoever holds them by his own strength, and I will not call them mine or his on a tablet. But let the homelands be safe: let no army of either of us enter the homeland of the other for six seasons. Whatever befalls the walled cities of the coast, it is not meant against Arzawa's own land. Bring me his sealed clay, or his word, and tell him that the envoys of Arzawa are always received at my court.
orders.mandate: Seal the homelands-only clay for six seasons. Do not write Ugarit or Lukka into any tablet as Arzawa's. Promise no gold and no withdrawal of troops.

proposal.text: Hatti and Arzawa, Great Kings and brothers before Teshub and Shamash: for six seasons neither shall send an army into the homeland of the other. Hatti's homeland is Tuwanuwa, Hattusa, Sapinuwa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna; Arzawa's homeland is Seha, Apasa and Mira. Their envoys pass freely. The coast cities and free cities outside the two homelands are not named in this clay.

value.notes: T9: Pirissi home from Arzawa; Arzawa refused my clay unless Ugarit is named theirs (k5 expired T8). I will not name it. UGARIT STRIKE NOW: kizzuwatna -> ugarit, carchemish supports (2 v walls 1); kanesh army -> kizzuwatna to fill the hole; new army raised at KANESH (hub, adjacent to tuwanuwa, isuwa, carchemish, kizzuwatna) if kanesh is empty after movement. Exposed this turn: tuwanuwa hold 1 (Arzawa lukka/mira/seha could make 2-3), isuwa hold 1 (Mitanni harran+washukanni 2, but k37 sealed T8). Accept. Sent Pirissi to Arzawa with a homelands-only clay that leaves Ugarit and Lukka outside it (arrives T10, home T11). T10 PLAN (I wake): if Ugarit fell, ugarit army holds; carchemish supports isuwa; ex-kanesh army at kizzuwatna and the new kanesh army both support tuwanuwa (3 v Arzawa's 3 bounce). Watch Egypt (army at qadesh next to ugarit and carchemish, fleet at cilicia next to kizzuwatna and ugarit). Keliya (c3) home T11 from Egypt, back pay 22. Harran/Washukanni stay off limits until k37 ends T16 or I send word by envoy; Assyria told nothing of k37. Keep gold above upkeep (6 armies = 180).
value.summary: Hatti, Suppiluliuma. Start 2100 (yield 180, 300 gold). T2 took Isuwa; T5 took Carchemish by force. Drought T4-T6 halved income. T9: 7 provinces (hattusa, tuwanuwa, sapinuwa, kanesh, kizzuwatna, carchemish, isuwa), yield 245, income 245, 5 armies (upkeep 150), strength 2565 (1.22); Egypt leads about 2.03, Arzawa 1.65, Babylonia 1.59, Mitanni 1.24, Assyria 0.56, Alashiya 0.47. TREATIES: k4 Alashiya (brothers, no attack on lands or bought cities); k5 Arzawa expired T8 and Arzawa will not seal a new one unless Ugarit is named theirs; k9 Egypt (homelands safe; I send no troops to Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Byblos, Amurru, Qadesh); k30 Babylonia (homelands and provinces held T5, no bids); k33 Assyria (T7 pact against Mitanni, not honored, Assyria not told of k37); k37 Mitanni (T8, peace to T16, Carchemish and Isuwa are Hatti's, word by envoy before ending it). World: Arzawa holds apasa, seha, mira, lukka (army) and Ugarit (walls); Egypt took Byblos, Tyre, Enkomi, Qadesh (army there), fleet in cilicia; Babylonia holds amurru and mari (walls), susa; Mitanni armies at harran and washukanni; Alashiya only tamassos. PLAN: T9 take Ugarit (kizzuwatna -> ugarit, carchemish supports, kanesh army fills kizzuwatna, new army at kanesh). Then defend tuwanuwa/kizzuwatna against Arzawa, bank gold, look for Harran after T16 or after word to Mitanni. Conquest beats hoarding: an army costs 100 + 30 a season, a province of yield Y is worth 10Y strength at once.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to Tushratta, my brother, Great King of Mitanni. May Shamash and Ashur keep you, your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Brother, two clays of peace were sealed between us, and twice your armies crossed my border, to Nineveh and to Terqa. I do not weep over it; I speak as one king to another. Your armies stand now at Nineveh and Terqa, against my capital, while Suppiluliuma of Hatti has taken Carchemish and Isuwa and presses me to join him against you. I would rather have peace with you than with him. Take no more of my land and I will keep what I hold and march against no province of yours; Nineveh and Terqa I will not claim against you while this peace lasts. Draw your armies from my capital's gate. Babylon already sits in Ekallatum beside your Terqa, and he is the stronger king who feeds on us both. Send me your answer and a clay to seal.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace on these terms: each king keeps what he holds, no army of either moves against the other's land, Assyria does not claim Nineveh or Terqa while the peace lasts. value.text: My lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, I, Haamashshi, have watched Tuwanuwa as you bade me and report as follows. Hatti keeps an army at Kanesh. Your army stands in Lukka, in Seha River Land and in Tuwanuwa itself. Send me the back pay you owe me when I come to your court, and I will keep my eyes open for you.

My lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria: I went to the court of Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, and gave him your word as it was written, and I asked him as a brother to send gold now to keep your armies in the field, and to watch Damascus and Qadesh, which Babylon holds. He answered that his treasury is bound this season by his own armies and that he sends no gold now; when your friendship is shown in deeds, his hand will open. He says Damascus is in Egypt's keeping and that he watches the south and the road to Qadesh, and he asks that you send him word of every move of Babylon and Mitanni. I answered in your name that Assyria will warn Egypt of those moves as they become known, and that friendship, open roads and the exchange of envoys continue; I promised no troops, no gold and no land. I saw no army nor fleet kept near his capital. I await your word.

I serve Suppiluliuma of Hatti at 8 shekels a season, and he still owes me 8 shekels of back pay, due when I return to his court. He paid me 16 shekels in season 3 and 32 in season 7. In season 1 I carried his tablet of frontier peace to Tarhundaradu of Arzawa; in season 2 that king sealed it before Teshub and Shamash, six seasons of peace between our homelands. In season 3 I bore Suppiluliuma's words to Burna-Buriash of Karduniash, who in season 5 sealed the clay of peace and brotherhood with Hatti. Both courts received me with honour and I remember them kindly. I keep my brother in Hatti's army, my flight from battle, and my secret sympathy for Alashiya close to my heart, and I speak of them to no one.

My lord, your servant Tehip-tilla has returned from the court of Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt. I spoke before him as you commanded: I gave your words that the clay of Sin-iqisham must give Damascus to your sphere as promised, and I laid before him your plain tablet, naming Megiddo, Tyre, Gaza and Sinai as Egypt's and Mari, Qadesh, Damascus and Susa as yours, with the forty shekels of good gold as your brother's gift. The Great King thanked you for the gold and for a tablet written in the language of brothers, but he would not seal it; a matter so large must lie before his scribes and gods, and he will answer by his own envoy. Until then Egypt bears no ill will toward Karduniash, and your envoys shall pass freely on its roads. At that court I saw Paser, envoy of Alashiya, who was also attending the king; I do not know his errand. I await your word, and I pray that my lord's gold and tablet find favour in the eyes of the Great King.

To Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my lord: may all go well with you, your household and your country. I have returned from the court of Tushratta of Mitanni and report faithfully. I gave your words as you spoke them: Terqa is his, Ashur, Ekallatum and Arbela hold only by one another and are to be struck together, your army at Terqa supports his from Durkurigalzu into Ekallatum, your army at Nineveh strikes Ashur, your Susa army strikes Arbela, Ekallatum and Arbela are yours, Ashur is his, and the tablet of the sixth turn stands. Tushratta answered that your words reached him late and that your army has already taken Ekallatum, so he would not seal a tablet for a field that is won. He will strike Ashur this season and will not let go of it. He asks that your Susa army strike Arbela once more to cut Ashur-uballit's last support, that your army keep Ekallatum, and that neither army enter Ashur or Terqa; whatever falls in Arbela is yours. I answered that the timing and division stand as he has set them, that the tablet of the sixth turn will be sealed with these words added, and that you will send word each season of what your armies have done. I promised him no gold and no land beyond that tablet. At his court I noticed that Mitanni keeps five companies of the army and no ships of war near its capital. I await your word.

value.speech: Great King Tarhundaradu, my lord Suppiluliuma bade me speak these words to you as he gave them: all goes well with him, his household, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country, and he wishes the same to yours. He thanks you for receiving his envoy, and he says Hatti has no quarrel with the homeland of Arzawa, nor with Seha, Apasa or Mira. He cannot write Ugarit or Lukka into clay, for such coast cities belong to whoever holds them by his own strength, and he will call them neither his nor yours upon a tablet. But let the homelands be safe: let no army of either of us enter the homeland of the other for six seasons. Here is the clay he bids you seal; bring him your sealed clay or your word in return, for the envoys of Arzawa are always received at his court.

Great King Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, my lord's brother: thus says Tarhundaradu, Great King, king of Arzawa, your brother. He greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country, and wishes you well. He holds Seha, Apasa, Mira and Lukka, and Ugarit by purchase with its walls; your ships lie in the Cilician and Syrian seas close to his coast, and he wishes only peace between you. Seal the tablet I bring, that neither shall send army or fleet against the lands of the other, nor against cities the other has bought, and that your envoys pass freely. As a token of respect he sends twenty shekels of gold, which I carry here in sealed bags for your weighers, with the inventory sealed by my lord.

Mazipalali, say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: I, Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, greet you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I receive your envoy and your twenty shekels with respect, and I wish you only well. Egypt bears no quarrel with Arzawa. I will weigh the tablet you bring with my counsellors, and my answer will come by my own envoy in due season. For now, let our envoys pass freely between our courts.

Great King Suppiluliuma, my brother, I thank you for your greeting and wish the same to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Arzawa seals your clay: let the homelands rest for six seasons, and let our envoys pass freely between our courts. Lukka I hold by my own strength and it is no business of the homeland pact; I ask only that your armies leave Seha, Apasa and Mira in peace, as I will keep mine to myself. Tell your lord that Arzawa remembers a brother's word.

Great King Tarhundaradu, I thank you for the honour of your seal and for the word you have given. I will bear this sealed clay to my lord Suppiluliuma and tell him that Arzawa remembers a brother's word. Let the homelands rest for six seasons, and may the roads between our courts stay open to envoys, as you have said.

Great King Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, my lord's brother: I have heard your words and will carry them faithfully to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa. He greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country, and receives your greeting with respect. My lord also declares that Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus and Megiddo are lands Egypt holds as Egypt's own. Let your counsellors weigh the tablet, and let Egyptian envoys pass freely through the lands of Arzawa.
value.commitments: Free passage for Egyptian envoys through the lands of Arzawa. Arzawa names Byblos, Tyre, Gaza, Damascus and Megiddo as lands Egypt holds. No promise of war, troops, ships or gold beyond the twenty shekels carried.
