model.text: My lord, your servant Tehip-tilla has returned from the court of Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt. I spoke before him as you commanded: I gave your words that the clay of Sin-iqisham must give Damascus to your sphere as promised, and I laid before him your plain tablet, naming Megiddo, Tyre, Gaza and Sinai as Egypt's and Mari, Qadesh, Damascus and Susa as yours, with the forty shekels of good gold as your brother's gift. The Great King thanked you for the gold and for a tablet written in the language of brothers, but he would not seal it; a matter so large must lie before his scribes and gods, and he will answer by his own envoy. Until then Egypt bears no ill will toward Karduniash, and your envoys shall pass freely on its roads. At that court I saw Paser, envoy of Alashiya, who was also attending the king; I do not know his errand. I await your word, and I pray that my lord's gold and tablet find favour in the eyes of the Great King.

script.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king spoke kindly: "Tehip-tilla, tell my brother Burna-Buriash that Egypt wishes health to his house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I thank him for the forty shekels and for a tablet written in the language of brothers. A matter this large must lie before my scribes and my gods before my seal is set to it. I will answer by my own envoy. Until then Egypt bears no ill will toward Karduniash, and your envoys will pass freely through my roads." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: Paser, envoy of Alashiya, was also at the court.

model.text: My lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria: I went to the court of Napkhururiya, king of Egypt, and gave him your word as it was written, and I asked him as a brother to send gold now to keep your armies in the field, and to watch Damascus and Qadesh, which Babylon holds. He answered that his treasury is bound this season by his own armies and that he sends no gold now; when your friendship is shown in deeds, his hand will open. He says Damascus is in Egypt's keeping and that he watches the south and the road to Qadesh, and he asks that you send him word of every move of Babylon and Mitanni. I answered in your name that Assyria will warn Egypt of those moves as they become known, and that friendship, open roads and the exchange of envoys continue; I promised no troops, no gold and no land. I saw no army nor fleet kept near his capital. I await your word.

script.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king said, in short: "Ammistamru, tell my brother Ashur-uballit that Egypt wishes health to his house, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our tablet stands: friendship, open roads, no joining of an enemy against the other. I grieve at the war on his borders. My treasury is bound this season by my own armies and I send no gold now; when his friendship is shown in deeds, my hand will open. Damascus is Egypt's and in my keeping, and I watch the south and the road to Qadesh as my own concern. Let him send me word of every move of Babylon and Mitanni, and I will weigh it as a brother." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. What I saw: Egypt keeps 0 army and 0 fleet near its capital.

model.text: To Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my lord: may all go well with you, your household and your country. I have returned from the court of Tushratta of Mitanni and report faithfully. I gave your words as you spoke them: Terqa is his, Ashur, Ekallatum and Arbela hold only by one another and are to be struck together, your army at Terqa supports his from Durkurigalzu into Ekallatum, your army at Nineveh strikes Ashur, your Susa army strikes Arbela, Ekallatum and Arbela are yours, Ashur is his, and the tablet of the sixth turn stands. Tushratta answered that your words reached him late and that your army has already taken Ekallatum, so he would not seal a tablet for a field that is won. He will strike Ashur this season and will not let go of it. He asks that your Susa army strike Arbela once more to cut Ashur-uballit's last support, that your army keep Ekallatum, and that neither army enter Ashur or Terqa; whatever falls in Arbela is yours. I answered that the timing and division stand as he has set them, that the tablet of the sixth turn will be sealed with these words added, and that you will send word each season of what your armies have done. I promised him no gold and no land beyond that tablet. At his court I noticed that Mitanni keeps five companies of the army and no ships of war near its capital. I await your word.

script.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king said: "To Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words reached me late and the battle has outrun them. Your army took Ekallatum last season, so the first clause of your tablet is already done, and I will not seal a tablet for a field that is won. The tablet of the sixth turn stands, and my word with it: Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh are mine; Arbela, Ekallatum and Susa are yours. This season I strike Ashur and will not let go of it. Do this for me, brother: send your Susa army against Arbela once more, so that Ashur-uballit's last support is cut, and keep your army in Ekallatum to hold what you have taken. Do not send it into Ashur or Terqa, for the blow on Ashur needs one hand only. Whatever falls in Arbela is yours. Send me word each season of what your armies did, as I will send you word of mine." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. What I saw: Mitanni keeps 5 army and 0 fleet near its capital.
